facilities: Renewable energy projects (PV solar and hot water)
context.description: A.I.C Diguna Rainbow Polytechnic is a faith-based applied technology training institution founded in 2002 in the Tinderet sub-district of Nandi County, run as part of the DIGUNA mission and reporting more than 2000 technicians trained. The Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority registers it as TVETA/PRIVATE/VTC/0006/2016, registered on 3 June 2016 with a licence valid to 13 July 2028 and the status 'Registered and Licensed'. Its accredited table lists ten programmes: nine NITA trade tests in carpentry and joinery, electrical wireman, hairdressing, masonry, plumbing and pipe fitting, tailoring, welding and fabrication, dressmaking and beauty therapy, plus a KASNEB craft award in information communication technology. The DIGUNA vocational-school page states that its courses are TVETA-accredited in masonry, apparel manufacturing, welding and fabrication, carpentry and joinery, electrical, plumbing and barbering, and describes renewable-energy projects in PV solar and hot water plus a library under construction. All listed awards are artisan-level trade tests or a craft certificate, which correspond to the schema's Artisan and Certificate levels.

context.description: Advanced Career Training College, which trades as ACT College, is a private TVC recorded in the TVETA register as TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0002/2025 in Kitui County, with a licence current to 28 January 2030 and the status Registered and Licensed. The college's published programme catalogue lists Business Management at Certificate and Diploma level, Information Communication Technology at Certificate and Diploma level, a Care Giving certificate, a Certified Nursing Assistant certificate, Computer Packages, IELTS preparation and a driving school with NTSA Class A, B1 and B2 licences. Its fees page states that certificate and diploma programmes carry the awarding body "Varies" together with an ACT College completion certificate, that Computer Packages and IELTS awards are issued by ACT College itself, and that the driving award is an ACT College certificate together with the NTSA driving licence. No published page names KNEC, TVET CDACC or NITA as the examining body for the Business Management, ICT, Care Giving or CNA programmes, and no Nursing diploma or Office Administration qualification appears on the current course catalogue even though both were carried in the imported record. The college occupies C - House, Level 3, Kitui Township along the Kitui-Kibwezi road, and publishes hello@advancedctcollege.com, admissions@advancedctcollege.com, a reception line on +254 101 661 548 and a calls/WhatsApp line on +254 113 922 262.

name: Africa Institute of Health and Development

context.about: Africa Institute of Health and Development is a private technical and vocational college at Kinanie Shopping Center in Athi River, Machakos County, Kenya. It is registered and licensed by the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority as TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0164/2016 and trains health, community development, business and social work professionals at KNEC craft and diploma level and at CDACC competency-based levels.
context.description: The Africa Institute of Health and Development (AIHD) is a private technical and vocational college operating from Kinanie Shopping Center on the Athi River side of Machakos County, registered by the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority under registration number TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0164/2016, with a licence valid to 2 July 2029. The institute describes itself as a health and development training provider registered with the Directorate of Industrial Training, the Ministry of Education and TVETA, and lists KNEC, KASNEB, ABMA, ICM and ABE as its examination bodies. The TVETA register of accredited programmes records fourteen qualifications, including KNEC craft and diploma programmes in business management, social development, banking and finance, social work and community development, supply chain management and tourism management, plus CDACC Level 4 competency-based programmes in community health, home care management and accommodation operations. Its own prospectus additionally advertises a long list of specialist diplomas in community based health, conflict and disaster management, guidance and counselling, occupational health and safety, project planning and management, and health and physiotherapy, which are not all reflected in the regulator's accredited list. The institute publishes the telephone lines 0721 421615 and 0721 318501 and the email address info@aihd.ac.ke. Note that the source database records this institution under a Nairobi town address, whereas both the regulator and the institution's own website place it in Machakos County at Athi River.

Its own schools page lists the NEGST School of Theology, the School of Business and Economics, the School of Education, Arts and Social Sciences and the Institute for the Study of African Realities. The CUE accredited programme register of 31 July 2026 lists thirty-four AIU awards, made up of eleven bachelor's degrees, thirteen master's degrees, eight doctorates and two postgraduate diplomas. The contact page publishes the Karen-Dagoreti Road address, P.O. Box 24686-00502, the general line info@aiu.ac.ke on +254 796 352 397, and separate admissions, records, ICT, public relations and ODeL support addresses, and the ODeL portal at https://odel.aiu.ac.ke answers with a live learning-management login. The university's history page reports 2,685 students, 2,956 alumni and 126 staff on its own authority, but no independent enrolment figure, named vice-chancellor contact or official logo file was published on the pages checked, so those fields are left null.

The university's main campus page describes a 124-acre site next to the Nairobi National Park, off Magadi Road near Ongata Rongai, and lists over fifty lecture halls, the Grace Roles library, accommodation, dining areas and sports facilities. context.about: Africa Theological Seminary (ATS) is a private, non-denominational post-secondary institution on a 20-acre campus in Section Six Estate, Kitale, Trans Nzoia County, registered with the TVET Authority (TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0165/2016) and operating under its parent organization International Christian Ministries on a semi-residential in-service model to train pastors, counsellors and Christian leaders already serving in ministry.
facilities: Two furnished office blocks with 24-hour internet access
Library with over 30,000 study and research materials
Computer laboratory with over 10 internet-connected computers
Prayer tower for private prayer and meditation
Guest houses for visiting faculty, speakers and church leaders
Carpentry workshop producing furniture on order
Chapel hall for worship and large gatherings
context.description: Africa Theological Seminary grew out of International Christian Ministries (ICM), which began teaching seminars in Kenya in 1986 and launched a degree programme in 1993; the name Africa Theological Seminary was given to the semi-residential programmes at the Kitale training centre in 2008. The seminary is registered as a post-secondary institution by the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority under registration number TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0165/2016, and most of its study programmes are accredited by the Association for Christian Theological Education in Africa (ACTEA). Its TVETA course table lists KNEC craft certificates in Information Communication Technology and Social Development, a KNEC diploma in Counselling, and TVET CDACC Level 5 certificates and Level 6 diplomas in Christian Chaplaincy, Christian Ministry and Counselling Psychology, while the seminary's own study page lists Theology and Counseling programmes at certificate and diploma level. ATS trains leaders 'in ministry' rather than 'for ministry': all programmes run on an in-service model built around block courses so students can continue serving in their primary ministries while studying. The institution sits on 20 acres of self-owned land on Waterworks Road in Section Six Estate, about 1.5 km from Kitale town's central business district, with dormitories, a 30,000-item library, a computer laboratory and a chapel hall on site.

context.description: The African Milling School is a certificated vocational school established in 2015 by the Buhler Group, sitting at the corner of Thika Road and the Eastern Bypass in Ruiru, Kiambu County, and registered and licensed by TVETA as TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0004/2016 with a licence current to 24 November 2026. It trains millers, maintenance technicians, quality controllers and operations managers for the flour, feed, coffee and baking industries, and publishes more than 1,625 graduates across 135 classes and trainees from over thirty countries. The flagship programmes are a one-year Head Miller Program, a two-year Apprentice Miller Program delivered with the Swiss School of Milling, and the Milling for Managers course, supported by short courses in flour quality and baking, feed milling, coffee handling and roasting, mechanical and electrical maintenance, PLC and automation, laboratory analytics, silo management and mycotoxins. The school publishes classrooms, a maintenance workshop, an analytics laboratory and a fully equipped school mill, and gives its address and course-coordinator contact as ams.nairobi@buhlergroup.com and +254 793 262 506, with Kipyegon Korir named as course coordinator on the Buhler location page. Neither the school pages nor the Buhler page publish qualification levels in the schema vocabulary, so programmes are recorded at the nearest level (the two-year apprenticeship as a diploma, workshops and short courses as certificates).

context.description: AIC Cheptebo Agricultural and Innovation Centre is registered by the TVET Authority as TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0138/2024, a private Technical and Vocational College (TVC category) in Elgeyo Marakwet County, Kenya, with the status Registered and Licensed. It operates as the Cheptebo Agricultural Training and Innovation Centre (CATIC), a ministry of Africa Inland Church Kenya established in 1986 and governed by a Board of Management drawn from the church, local leaders and community representatives. CATIC is located in Keiyo South Constituency, Soy North Ward, on the C51 Iten-Kabarnet road near Cheploch Gorge in the southern Kerio Valley, roughly 5 km west of the Chebloch Bridge. The college is purely agricultural, offering fully accredited TVET CDACC programmes from Level 3 to Level 5 in horticulture, dairy farm attendance, poultry production, sustainable agriculture, agriculture extension, agripreneurship, apiculture and integrated pest management, with trainees spending most of their time in hands-on learning on the centre's 20-hectare demonstration farm. Supporting facilities include a conference centre with four halls and residential accommodation for 100 guests, a KEPHIS-certified tree nursery and a fruit processing factory supported by the Government of Japan, and the college publishes a student portal at students.catic.co.ke and a CDACC results portal at cdacc.catic.co.ke.

context.about: AIC Kapsowar Medical Training College is a nursing college established in August 2008 and owned by the Africa Inland Church under AIC Kapsowar Mission Hospital, focusing on training health personnel at certificate and diploma level from the Kapsowar Hospital site in Elgeyo Marakwet County.
context.description: AIC Kapsowar Medical Training College, established in August 2008, is an accredited nursing school under the Nursing Council of Kenya. It is owned and run by AIC-Kenya under the auspices of AIC Kapsowar Mission Hospital, with its foundation rooted in missionary work, supported by missionaries, the government, the church and the community. Its vision is to produce competent Kenya Registered Community Health Nurses (KRCHNs) who are role models in providing quality general nursing, midwifery and community health services. The mission is to train healthcare-related programmes at certificate and diploma levels, championing quality healthcare delivery and professional advancement. The college emphasises mastery of high-level competencies for safe and quality care, aligning its core values with those of AIC Kapsowar Hospital: Quality and Safety, Dignity and Respect, Caring and Listening, Responsibility and Integrity, and Excellence and Innovation. The college offers courses in Kenya Registered Community Health Nursing (KRCHN), Perioperative Theatre Technology (Diploma and Certificate) and Community Health Assistant (Diploma), from its Kapsowar Hospital site in Elgeyo Marakwet County.

It is owned and run by AIC-Kenya under the auspices of AIC Kapsowar Mission Hospital, with its foundation rooted in missionary work, supported by missionaries, the government, the church and the community. Its vision is to produce competent Kenya Registered Community Health Nurses (KRCHNs) who are role models in providing quality general nursing, midwifery and community health services. The mission is to train healthcare-related programmes at certificate and diploma levels, championing quality healthcare delivery and professional advancement. The college emphasises mastery of high-level competencies for safe and quality care, aligning its core values with those of AIC Kapsowar Hospital: Quality and Safety, Dignity and Respect, Caring and Listening, Responsibility and Integrity, and Excellence and Innovation. The college offers courses in Kenya Registered Community Health Nursing (KRCHN), Perioperative Theatre Technology (Diploma and Certificate) and Community Health Assistant (Diploma), from its Kapsowar Hospital site in Elgeyo Marakwet County.

context.description: AIC Naivasha Technical Training Institute is a privately owned technical and vocational college on Kenyatta Avenue in Naivasha, Nakuru County. The TVETA register records it as private TVC TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0090/2016, registered on 14 April 2016 with a licence expiring on 28 February 2029 and a status of Registered and Licensed. Its own website describes it as a TVETA-regulated Christian technical institute grounded in the motto 'Live and Work; It Is God's Plan', running 11 training departments with 48 programmes and short courses across automotive, building and construction, business studies, carpentry and joinery, cosmetology, electrical and electronics engineering, food and beverage, garment making, health sciences, ICT and mechanical engineering. Students can enter at artisan, craft certificate, diploma or professional level depending on KCSE grade, and sit national examinations on campus through KNEC, TVET CDACC, NITA and KASNEB. Intakes run in January, May and September, with online applications, on-campus hostels and a student and staff portal for results, fees and timetables.

It has a long-standing reputation built on over twenty years of education, providing courses in travel and tourism, cabin crew, airport operations, hotel management, food production and international languages. Programmes lead to internationally recognised awards, including IATA Canada-framework certificates and diplomas and ICM (UK) qualifications, and every programme includes features such as guaranteed overseas and local attachment placement, full board accommodation, free computer lessons and two international languages. Its stated mission is to provide high quality training, research, consultancy and outreach services to individuals and corporate clients in tourism, hospitality and air transport.

Programmes lead to internationally recognised awards, including IATA Canada-framework certificates and diplomas and ICM (UK) qualifications, and every programme includes features such as guaranteed overseas and local attachment placement, full board accommodation, free computer lessons and two international languages. The centre also operates a Moodle-based e-learning portal that runs the same IATA and hospitality course cohorts online. Its stated mission is to provide high quality training, research, consultancy and outreach services to individuals and corporate clients in tourism, hospitality and air transport.

name: Akdogan Glaszner German Training Institute

context.about: Akdogan Glaszner German Training Institute, which trades as AG German Institute, is a private German language school registered by the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority as TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0067/2024 in Nairobi County. It was founded in late 2023 and became the first language school in East Africa to hold an OSD examination licence, teaching German up to B1 level at branches in Nairobi, Eldoret, Nakuru, Mombasa and Kisumu.
context.description: Akdogan Glaszner German Training Institute, which trades as AG German Institute, is a private German language school established in late 2023 by Tobias Glaszner, Kerem Akdogan and Victor Lekaram and registered by the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority as TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0067/2024 with a licence valid to 19 August 2030 under the status 'Registered Only'. In May 2024 it became the first language school in East Africa to receive an OSD licence, allowing it to offer internationally recognised German examinations, and it teaches German up to B1 level for nurses, early childhood educators, students and professionals preparing to work, study or live in Germany. The Nairobi branch operates from AMBANK House on University Way and publishes the telephone number 0707797543, while the wider institute lists branches in Eldoret, Nakuru, Mombasa and Kisumu. The institute states that it deliberately does not offer online classes, keeping delivery face-to-face at its branches. No e-mail address could be confirmed because the site obfuscates it, and the TVETA register publishes no accredited-programme table for the institute, so the language qualification is recorded from the institute's own course pages.

name: Alliance Francaise

context.about: Alliance Française de Nairobi is a French language and cultural centre in Nairobi operating within the Alliance Française network. It teaches French through programmes aligned to the Common European Framework of Reference and hosts DELF and DALF examinations, which it describes as being offered at Kenya's only accredited centre.
context.description: Alliance Française de Nairobi offers French language tuition at six levels, from Beginner (A1) to Proficiency (C2), with each level following the Common European Framework of Reference so that progress is recognised internationally. Learners can prepare for and sit the DELF or DALF examinations with the institution, which states that it is Kenya's only accredited centre for those examinations. Classes are delivered daily, on alternate evenings, in hybrid form or intensively, with total hours per level ranging from 120 hours at beginner level to 240 hours at mastery and proficiency levels. The centre also runs arts and culture programming, a library and a translation service, with separate contact lines for admissions, examinations and the library. The campus is at 05 Utalii Lane in Nairobi.

context.description: The institution appears in the TVETA register as AMANI COUNSELING AND TRAINING INSTITUTE, a private Technical and Vocational College in Nairobi County under registration number TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0006/2016, registered on 28 January 2016 with a licence valid to 2 July 2029 and a status of Registered and Licensed. Its website presents the training arm as Amani Counselling Centre and Training Institute, describing more than 30 years of counselling practice, accredited training and community initiatives, with training and capacity building offered as diploma, certificate and short courses in counselling psychology, social work and community development. The register lists three accredited awards: Craft-level Social Development and Diploma-level Counselling and Social Work and Community Development, all examined by KNEC; the certificates and short courses advertised on the website are not separately named in the register and are therefore not recorded as awards here. The website gives the headquarters as Raila Odinga Way in Nairobi, telephone lines +254 112 376713 and +254 722 626590 and e-mail info@amanicentre.org. The register separately carries 'Amani Counselling Centre and Training Institute Nairobi CBD' under TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0005/2026, a newer city-centre entry of the same provider, while this record retains the registered name and number that correspond to the database entry.

context.description: Amboseli Institute of Hospitality & Technology (AIHT) is a private hospitality and tourism tertiary institute accredited by the Kenyan Ministry of Education. With a legacy spanning over 30 years, AIHT delivers quality education in hospitality and tourism and counts more than 9,000 graduates. Its main campus is on Kiboko Road, behind Booth Extrusion, in Thika town, Kiambu County, about 40 km from Nairobi. Training blends theory with practical skills across a School of Hospitality, a School of Tourism, regular courses and short courses, backed by partnerships with hotels and organisations in Kenya and across the globe. The institute runs an eLearning portal at elearning.amboseliinstitute.ac.ke and prepares students for examinations by KNEC, City and Guilds, NITA, ICM and BTEC.

context.description: Angaza Bible and Training Institute is a private institution that presents itself as TVET-registered and delivers its own Certificate and Diploma programmes, with a main campus in Bungoma and additional campuses listed at Kangemi, Kisii-Etago, Kisii-Kereri, Nairobi-Kayole, Nairobi City and Trans Nzoia-Saboti. The institute's published programme table lists awards across faculties of biblical studies, theology and missions, Christian ministry, Christian chaplaincy, counselling psychology, community health, social work and community development, fashion design technology and automotive engineering, and it marks a number of entries as approved TVET CDACC courses. context.description: The Archdiocese of Nairobi Kariobangi Women Promotion Training Institute (KWPTI) is a private TVET institution operating in Nairobi County, Kenya, listed by the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority as TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0028/2019, a private Technical and Vocational College whose licence runs to 29 September 2029 with the status Registered and Licensed. It was founded in 1992 by the Comboni Missionary Sisters as an answer to young women in Kariobangi seeking refuge and assistance at the Holy Trinity Catholic Church, and is owned by the Catholic Archdiocese of Nairobi. KWPTI is a non-profit-oriented training school offering holistic training in skills such as catering, hairdressing and beauty, dressmaking and tailoring, alongside spiritual and human formation that prepares its students for the labour market. The institute reports that about 77 percent of its former students are employed or self-employed, and counselling is part of the programme to help the women reconcile with their past and discover their potential. Its published course table is artisan/trade-test level, with the food and beverage award examined by KNEC and the hairdressing, tailoring, dressmaking and beauty therapy awards examined by NITA.

context.description: Artwork School of Design is a private Technical and Vocational College registered by the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority under number TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0195/2025 on 6 November 2025. The regulator's register records its licence as Registered and Licensed with an expiry date of 5 November 2030 and lists two accredited competency-based awards. Both awards are in interior design, one at CDACC Level 5 and one at CDACC Level 6. Applying the Schologic level-normalisation convention, CDACC Level 5 maps to Certificate level and Level 6 to Diploma level, so the two awards are recorded as a Certificate and a Diploma in Interior Design assessed by TVET CDACC. No institutional website, e-mail address, telephone line or street address was published on the regulator's record, so those fields remain null rather than guessed. The college is registered as a private TVC in Nairobi County.

context.description: Auscare International College is a healthcare and community service training institution based in Nyali, Mombasa, established in partnership with Auscare Group (Australia) and Auscare Training Organisation, a healthcare provider, to bring Australian-standard education to East Africa. context.description: Austra Training Institute operates from Komora Centre on the fourth floor of Room 415 in Eldoret, Uasin Gishu County, and describes itself as a TVET-accredited vocational training provider preparing learners for domestic and international careers. Its website organises provision into six schools: Languages and International Studies, Science Engineering and Technology, Business Management and Economics, Health and Social Sciences, Hospitality and Tourism, and Music and Media Arts, advertising more than fifty courses. Featured programmes include the Certificate in Nurse Assistant, a dual qualification in Certificate III in Individual Support covering ageing and disability, and AutoCAD for Civil Engineering, and the institute also teaches German from A1 to B2 alongside IELTS preparation and caregiving pathways to Germany. The site lists TVETA, CDACC, KNEC, NITA and the Ministry of Education among its partners, but it does not publish a TVETA registration number and no matching entry could be located in the TVETA public register under this name, so the accreditation recorded here is the institute's own stated TVET accreditation rather than a verified registration. The institute is a teaching institution: it delivers the certificate and language programmes listed here and a large catalogue of short courses.

context.description: Established in 1980 as Bandari College by the Kenya Ports Authority (KPA), the institution was initially created to provide in-house training for port operations and cargo handling. Its primary objective was to ensure continuity in port operations following the collapse of the East African Railways and Harbours Corporation. Over time, the college expanded its scope to include nautical studies and began admitting students from the Indian Ocean hinterland, benefiting from international partnerships and government funding. In 2018, Bandari College was transformed into Bandari Maritime Academy (BMA), a Semi-Autonomous Government Agency (SAGA), to address the evolving demands of the global maritime sector and the burgeoning Blue Economy. BMA's vision is to be a World Class Centre for Maritime Education and Training, with a mission to provide competent maritime human resources for sustainable development. The academy is committed to excellence in teaching, training, scholarship, innovation, and research, aiming to generate employable skills that support the growth of Kenya's Blue Economy and ensure the highest international maritime standards.

context.description: Barut Youth Development and Sports Centre is a public vocational training centre registered by the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority under number TVETA/PUBLIC/VTC/0020/2015 on 15 July 2015. The regulator's register records its licence as Registered and Licensed with an expiry date of 2 July 2029 and lists two accredited award rows. Both rows are the same qualification, Fashion Design and Garment Making at NVCET level examined by the Kenya National Examinations Council, so de-duplication by course, level and exam body leaves a single distinct award. Following the Schologic level-normalisation convention, the NVCET National Vocational Certificate is recorded at Artisan level because NVCET is an artisan-equivalent award in Kenya's TVET framework. The centre is registered as a public VTC in Nakuru County and, as its name indicates, is a youth development and sports facility that also delivers vocational training. Seventeen accredited course rows are listed: two KNEC artisan awards in fashion design and garment making and food and beverage; five KNEC craft programmes in catering and accommodation operations, electrical and electronics technology (power), fashion design and garment making, food and beverage production and service, and housekeeping and laundry; five KNEC diploma programmes in catering and accommodation management, electrical and electronics engineering (power), food and beverage production, sales and service management, housekeeping management and information communication technology; and five NITA trade tests in electrical wireman, hairdressing, tailoring, dressmaking and beauty therapy. Register levels were normalised to the schema vocabulary, with Craft rendered as Certificate and trade tests rendered as Artisan. The institute's own site at beacontechnical.ac.ke was fetched on 2026-10-26 and publishes info@beacontechnical.ac.ke in its contact block alongside the postal address P.O. Box 4326-00200, Nairobi, so that published address is recorded as the institutional e-mail.

description: Beta Care Training Institute was founded in October 2018 as an initiative of Beta Care Hospital and states that it earned TVETA accreditation in 2021, after which it expanded from a single patient attendant course to certificate and diploma health programmes. Its classes are held on the second and third floors of the Beta Care Hospital building in Githunguri, so that students train alongside the hospital's clinical staff. The institute's own course pages publish the award level for every programme it advertises: the Patient Attendant course and the Health Services Support programme are both described as certificate programmes open to KCSE holders, while Perioperative Theatre Technology is offered as a certificate for a D plain entry grade and as a diploma for a C- minus entry grade. The TVET Authority register accredits two awards under TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0064/2021, Community Health at Level 4 and Perioperative Theatre Technology at Level 5, both examined by TVET CDACC, and the institute lists TVET CDACC examinations among its programme features. The institute's site also advertises orthopaedic and trauma care and nutrition and dietetics among its teaching areas but publishes no award level or examining body for those subject areas, so they are not recorded as qualifications here. No student enrolment figure, fee schedule or e-learning portal is published on the fetched pages.

context.about: Biosanitation Technology Training Institute (BTTI) is a privately owned Technical and Vocational College in Kisumu County, Kenya, registered and licensed by the TVET Authority as TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0074/2024. Its accredited competency-based programmes span biotechnology, community health, fashion design and food and beverage service, alongside three artisan trade tests recorded by the regulator.
context.description: The TVET Authority register lists Biosanitation Technology Training Institute (BTTI) as a private Technical and Vocational College in Kisumu County, registered on 1 August 2024 under number TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0074/2024 with a licence valid to 31 July 2029 and the status Registered and Licensed. Its course table contains twelve rows that reduce to eight distinct qualifications: three NITA trade tests at artisan level, one level-4 CDACC food and beverage certificate, one level-5 community health diploma and three level-6 higher diplomas in biotechnology, community health and fashion design; repeated rows for community health, biotechnology and fashion design were collapsed. Only the five competency-based TVET CDACC qualifications are carried in the structured course list, because the validation gate rejected NITA as an examination body on this record; the three NITA trade tests in electrical wireman, masonry and plumbing and pipe fitting are therefore recorded here in narrative form against the regulator register entry. No KNEC or KASNEB award appears for the institute. The institute's own domain biosantech.ac.ke no longer resolves to a public internet host from this environment, but the Wayback Machine capture of 23 March 2025 preserves the institute's site, whose contact block publishes the mailbox btti@biosantech.ac.ke and repeats the Gmail address biosanitationi@gmail.com; btti@biosantech.ac.ke is recorded here as the institutional e-mail. The regulator's record publishes no street address, telephone line or student figure, so those fields remain null.

context.about: BIPS Technical College, also trading as Blessing Institute of Professional Studies, is a private technical and vocational college in Kiambu County, Kenya, registered by the TVET Authority as TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0198/2025 and teaching hospitality, cosmetology, fashion, ICT, motor vehicle mechanics, plumbing, electrical installation, caregiving and community health.
context.description: BIPS Technical College is registered by the TVET Authority as a private Technical and Vocational College under TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0198/2025, registered on 6 November 2025 and licensed to 5 November 2030, and operates in Kiambu County with a branch on the Southern Bypass reached from the Waiyaki Way-Kikuyu and Wangige-Kikuyu sides. The college also presents itself under the name Blessing Institute of Professional Studies. The regulator's accredited course table carries two awards for the registration number, Food and Beverage Production (Cookery) at CDACC Level 4 and a NITA trade test in Caregiver, and those two awards are the only ones recorded here. The college's own site advertises a much wider catalogue organised into department pages: hospitality and catering, hair and beauty, fashion design and tailoring, information communication technology, motor vehicle mechanics, plumbing and pipe fitting, electrical installation, driving, baking and pastry, barista skills, caregiver and health support, community health, international languages and pre-departure training. Those department pages publish subject topics but no award level or examining body for the individual programmes, so the wider catalogue is described here rather than entered as qualification rows. The site publishes the postal address P.O. Box 612-00625 Kangemi, Nairobi, alongside the Kikuyu branch, and its contact numbers are +254 704 094 393, 0707 717 780 and 0790 222 885. No enrolment figure, fee schedule or learning-management-system portal is published on the fetched pages, and the '45,000+ Students Worldwide' line on the homepage is promotional copy with no published basis, so no student count is recorded.

context.description: Bishop Locati Technical Training Institute - Isiolo is named after Bishop Luigi Locati, an Italian Catholic missionary who helped establish educational institutions in the region, and is affiliated with the Isiolo Catholic Diocese. name: Bollington Training Institute

context.about: Bollington Training Institute is a private Technical and Vocational College in Nairobi, registered and licensed by TVETA under number TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0199/2025. It teaches short professional courses through schools of business, ICT, hospitality and secretarial studies, hairdressing and beauty therapy, health and nutrition, and digital content creation.
context.description: Bollington Training Institute is a private Technical and Vocational College in Nairobi registered by the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority under number TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0199/2025, registered on 6 November 2025 and licensed to 5 November 2030 with the status Registered and Licensed. The institute describes itself as a higher education and professional training provider built around six schools: Business Studies; ICT and Computer Studies; Hospitality and Secretariat Studies; Hairdressing and Beauty Therapy; Health and Nutrition; and Digital Content Creation. Its hospitality school publishes five short programmes — event planning, baking and pastry, front desk operations, hospitality management, and food and beverage production — most delivered over two months, and the institute states that it awards a Certificate of Completion for the course undertaken on successful completion while external certification depends on the examining body chosen. Training is supported by equipped training kitchens, front office laboratories and restaurant simulation rooms, with work-based internship attachments, and the institute operates student, applicant, teacher and director login portals on its website. The TVETA register currently publishes no accredited course table for the institution, so the programmes recorded here are the institute's own published short courses rather than regulator-confirmed awards. No street address is published on the pages retrieved, and the TVETA register places the institution in Nairobi County.

context.description: Established in May 2015, Boma International Hospitality College (BIHC) is fully owned by the Kenya Red Cross Society (KRCS) and managed by Boma PanAfrican. The college aims to nurture individuals to be leaders in service-oriented business entities through a practical, hands-on learning approach. BIHC operates in educational partnership with the Business and Hotel Management School (BHMS) in Switzerland, and its curriculum emphasizes the Swiss tradition of balancing theoretical knowledge with immediate practical applications within the Boma Hotel Complex. The institution also collaborates with Alpine Center Switzerland, United States International University (USIU), and Strathmore University. BIHC offers local and international internship opportunities to its students and is accredited by The Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority (TVETA) in Kenya.

context.description: Bomet College of Accountancy is a private Technical and Vocational College entered in the TVETA register as TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0153/2016, registered on 3 June 2016. context.description: Bondo Technical Training Institute is a public technical institution situated in Bondo Sub-County, Siaya County, approximately five kilometres along the Barkowino-Misori Road. TVETA registered it on 28 January 2016 under registration number TVETA/PUBLIC/TVC/0004/2016 and its licence is recorded as valid to 11 June 2031 with a status of Registered and Licensed. The regulator's accredited course table lists fifty-five qualifications spanning artisan, craft and diploma programmes examined by KNEC, NITA trade tests and modular TVET CDACC programmes from Level 3 to Level 6 in engineering, building, business, ICT, health and social work disciplines. The institute's own website describes a building and civil engineering complex delivered under Phase One of a five-phase development plan, and the contact page lists specialised plumbing, masonry and carpentry workshops, Soil Mechanics, Topology and Computer laboratories, a Jitume digital skills hub, a library and a multi-purpose lecture theatre. The institute publishes principal@bondotti.ac.ke and +254 115 508 393 as its contact channels and runs a separate e-learning portal at masomo.bondotti.ac.ke.

context.description: The college is recorded in the TVETA register of accredited TVET institutions as registration number TVETA/PUBLIC/TVC/0023/2017, a public Technical and Vocational College in Nyamira County, registered on 19 July 2017 and licensed to 21 February 2030 with the status Registered and Licensed. The register's course table resolves to 32 distinct TVET CDACC awards, which under this batch's mapping convention are recorded as four Artisan (Level 4), twelve Certificate (Level 5) and sixteen Diploma (Level 6) programmes spanning building, electrical, fashion, business, ICT, social work and health records disciplines. The institution's official website (https://borabutti.ac.ke/) brands it Borabu Technical Training Institute (BTTI) and presents academic departments in Business Studies (business, HR and cooperative management), Computing and Informatics (ICT with hands-on Python, Java and web programming) and Electrical and Electronics (power and telecommunication options), alongside a hairdressing department. The website reports approximately 980 enrolled trainees and 38 competent trainers, and its navigation lists an E-Learning Portal and a Students Portal, implying an online learning presence that could not be verified with a live platform URL. The college maintains institution-owned pages on Facebook, X and Instagram, and can be reached on +254746211764 or borabutti@gmail.com; its Google Maps listing places it at Nyangoge in Nyamira County, while directory listings also give the locality as Nsicha, Nyamira.

changelog_jsonb.new_val: Borabu Technical and Vocational College is a public technical and vocational college registered by the TVET Authority in Nyamira County, in Kenya's Nyanza region. It is one of the larger CDACC-accredited colleges in the county, offering competency-based awards from Level 4 to Level 6 across building, electrical, fashion, business, ICT, social work and health records disciplines.

The college is recorded in the TVETA register of accredited TVET institutions as registration number TVETA/PUBLIC/TVC/0023/2017, a Technical and Vocational College under public ownership in Nyamira County. Its licence was registered on 19 July 2017 and runs to 21 February 2030 with the status Registered and Licensed. The register's course table holds 34 rows which, after removing duplicate rows for the same course name and level, resolve to 32 distinct CDACC awards: four at Level 4, twelve at Level 5 and sixteen at Level 6. Under this batch's mapping convention CDACC Level 4 is recorded as Artisan, Level 5 as Certificate and Level 6 as Diploma, so the same trade may legitimately appear at more than one level. A vetted reference listing that carries the exact registered name and registration number publishes the physical location as Nsicha, Nyamira, the manager's phone number 0700152177, the email borabuTTI@gmail.com and the postal address P.O Box 222-40200 Kisii; that fetched source is used to populate the phone, email and town/location fields. No official website for the college was confirmed from a fetched source, so the website field remains null.

context.about: Brand Institute of Forensics and Security is a private technical and vocational college in Nairobi CBD, registered and licensed by the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority as TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0019/2023. It trains forensic investigation, security management, criminal justice management, public administration and information communication technology at CDACC certificate and diploma level, and operates a second branch in Nakuru.
context.description: Brand Institute of Forensics and Security, which brands itself BIFS, is a private technical and vocational college registered by the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority under number TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0019/2023, registered on 26 January 2023 and licensed to 25 January 2028 with the status 'Registered and Licensed'. The regulator's course table carries seven rows covering criminal justice management, information communication technology, forensic investigation, public administration and security management, all examined by the TVET Curriculum Development, Assessment and Certification Council; at CDACC Level 5 they are recorded here at diploma level and at Level 6 at higher diploma level, and the duplicated security management row is counted once. Criminal justice management is accredited at both diploma and higher diploma level, so the level is carried in the label to keep those two awards distinct. The college's own website describes certificate and diploma intakes of eight months and one and a half years and advertises professional short courses in criminal investigation, CCTV surveillance, crime scene management, cyber security awareness, fraud detection and report writing, but it does not publish the CDACC level of each programme, so the regulator's levels are used. The site publishes the e-mail info@bifs.co.ke, the telephone line 0796 354465 and the campus address on the fourth floor of Lois Plaza on Latema Road in Nairobi CBD, together with a Nakuru branch on the third floor of Mache Plaza reachable on 0795 554516. No e-learning portal, distance-learning mode, student enrolment figure or campus facility inventory is published on the fetched pages.

context.description: Bridgeworld College is a privately owned technical and vocational college recorded in the TVETA register under number TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0012/2016, registered on 28 January 2016 with a licence valid to 11 February 2031 and a status of Registered and Licensed. Its campus sits at Karen Triangle Estate, off Karen Road in the quiet Karen suburb of Nairobi. The institution has rebranded as Bridgeworld Theological Seminary (formerly Bridgeworld College) and describes itself as an inter-denominational, Christ-centred centre of theological excellence with over 22 years of training, whose graduates serve as Christian leaders across East Africa. Its current advertised programmes are a two-year Diploma in Theology, a two-year Diploma in Intercultural Studies and a one-year Certificate in Christian Ministry, while the TVETA register continues to accredit three KNEC-examined diploma programmes in Business Management, Counselling (Marriage and Family Therapy) and Social Work and Community Development. The site states that its mode of study integrates formal, non-formal and informal education, that fees are competitive with scholarships for qualified students, and that alumni can join BAAIM, an alliance of Bridgeworld alumni.

context.about: Brighter College is a private Technical and Vocational College operating in Ongata Rongai, Kajiado County, Kenya. The college states that it began operations in February 2013 and that its key competencies are in accountancy, information technology and technical fields. It is registered and licensed by the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority under TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0041/2022, and the regulator's accredited course table records a KASNEB Certified Public Accountants professional qualification and a KNEC craft Information Communication Technology programme.
context.description: Brighter College describes itself on its own website as a Technical and Vocational Training institute that started operations in February 2013 and today presents itself as the leading TVET institute in Ongata Rongai, with key competencies in accountancy, IT and technical fields oriented to digital transformation. The Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority lists the institution as BRIGHTER COLLEGE under registration number TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0041/2022, category TVC, type Private, County Kajiado, registered on 27 July 2022 with a licence valid to 26 July 2027 and the status Registered and Licensed. The regulator's accredited course table for this registration carries two programmes: Certified Public Accountants at Professional level examined by KASNEB, and Information Communication Technology at Craft level examined by KNEC; the professional KASNEB award has no equivalent in the canonical course-level vocabulary, so only the craft ICT programme is recorded as a structured course row and the CPA qualification is recorded here in narrative. The college's contact page gives its premises as the 3rd floor of the Ongata Rongai Women's Group Building, next to KCB Bank on Magadi Road, with telephone lines 0727 442315, 0782 191406 and 0722 832922 and the e-mail address brightercollege@gmail.com. No e-learning, distance-learning or virtual-campus provision is published on the pages fetched, and no teaching or teacher-training programme appears on the regulator's course table, so those attributes are recorded as absent or false rather than inferred. Course lists published by third-party directories for this college, including short computer-package and teacher-education titles, are not corroborated by the regulator's accredited table and are therefore not asserted in this record.

context.description:
Bunyala Technical and Vocational College was established in October 2017 and officially commenced operations in January 2018. Its establishment was a direct result of a government initiative to ensure at least one Technical and Vocational College in every constituency, with Bunyala TVC being among the first 60 institutions built under this program. Buruuj Training Institute, trading as BTI College, is a private technical and vocational college registered by the TVET Authority under number TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0008/2022 with status Registered and Licensed and a licence expiry of 2030-01-28. It was established in 2021, admitting its first students that year, and grew out of Tijara Consultancy, which rebranded as BTI College Consultancy. The college relocated from Ongata Rongai to its main campus on Mugima Road, about 190 metres off Magadi Road in Kiserian, Kajiado County. It positions itself as an accredited private TVET institution offering technical, business, ICT, banking, Islamic finance and Islamic studies programmes - over 25 accredited programmes across seven subsidiaries - via open, distance, online and in-person learning across Kenya, Ghana, Canada, Somalia, Ethiopia and Tanzania. The TVETA register course table lists a NITA trade test award in Food and Beverage Production, and the college operates a Moodle-based learning portal at lms.bticollege.ac.ke alongside active Facebook pages.

context.description: Bushiangala Technical Training Institute is a public technical training institute in Kakamega County, in Kenya's Western region, registered by the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority as TVETA/PUBLIC/TVC/0008/2016. The regulator's register shows registration on 28 January 2016 and a licence valid to 3 May 2028 with the status Registered and Licensed. Its accredited-award table shows the institute is a broad KNEC examination centre, offering artisan awards in electrical installation, craft awards in automotive engineering, electrical and electronics technology, fashion design and garment making, information communication technology, science laboratory technology, social development and welding and fabrication, and diploma programmes in applied biology, automotive engineering, civil engineering, electrical and electronics engineering, fashion design and clothing technology, ICT, social work and community development and supply chain management, with KASNEB accounting also listed. context.description: Candy College of Beauty and Applied Sciences publishes a programme and fee-structure table that names each award, its examination body and its enrolment grade, and that table is the source of the twenty-seven awards recorded here. The awards are spread across seven departments: beauty and cosmetology, fashion and clothing and textiles, interior design, health sciences, hospitality and institutional management, information communication technology, and social science. Examination bodies named in the table are the National Industrial Training Authority for the beauty, hairdressing, cosmetology, homecare management, tailoring and food and beverage trade awards, the Kenya National Examinations Council for the ICT, nutrition and dietetics, counselling and community development awards, and TVET CDACC for the Level 5 and Level 6 fashion, interior design, nursing assistant and perioperative theatre awards. Three awards carry the college's own CCBS code rather than an external examiner and are recorded here as internally examined. The table states no level for its Health Services Support and Perioperative Theatre Technology rows and offers Computer Packages as a six-week internal module, so those rows are not recorded as qualifications. The college publishes two campuses, Nairobi and Ruaka, and states that more than 400 learners are enrolled with it.

context.description: Cardinal Maurice Otunga Technical and Vocational College is a public TVET institution established in 2021 under the Government of Kenya TVET framework and accredited by the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority. Its site serves Bungoma County and the surrounding region, with training organised in nine departments: fashion design and cosmetology, hospitality and tourism, electrical and electronics engineering, building and civil engineering, business studies, agriculture and environmental studies, computing and information technology, mechanical and automotive engineering, and liberal studies. Programmes run from Level 3 to Level 6 and are all competency-based, combining theory with practical work delivered through workshops, laboratories, field practice and industrial attachments. The college states a mission to provide practical, effective and high-quality skills training to the youth for sustainable manpower development, and its principal describes ongoing investment in modern facilities, trainers and industry partnerships. context.description: Carenic Training College, trading as Carenic College, was established in 2010 and is registered and licensed by the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority under number TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0064/2020, registered on 16 April 2020 with a licence current to 21 January 2031 and the status Registered and Licensed. The college teaches beauty-industry and applied trades: hairdressing, beauty therapy, full cosmetology, nail technology, holistic massage, barbering, salon management, training of trainers, fashion and design, and a graded ICT programme, with the Certificate and Diploma levels published on the course pages and most programmes running three to eight months. The regulator's page for this registration lists one accredited award, the Trade Test in Hairdressing examined by the National Industrial Training Authority, and the college's own pages name the National Industrial Training Authority among the examination bodies for its programmes, alongside City and Guilds, the Institute of Commercial Management, the Kenya National Examinations Council and Industrial Qualifications Kenya; because each course page names several bodies rather than one, the courses here record the National Industrial Training Authority, the body the regulator records against this registration. Teaching is practical and salon-based: the college advertises a working training salon and professional equipment including facial steamers and galvanic and high-frequency machines, and classes run in day, evening and weekend shifts at the Nairobi and Makindu campuses. The Makindu operation also holds a separate VTC registration (TVETA/PRIVATE/VTC/0002/2020) in Makueni County, and no named officer, staff directory or student population figure is published on the site.

context.description: Carlile College is a private technical and vocational college registered and licensed by the TVET Authority under TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0005/2017 (registered 16 February 2017, licence running to 15 August 2027) and operating as an education ministry of Church Army Africa (CAA), an Anglican Society of Mission. The college traces its origins to 1958, when CAA started it with eight students undergoing basic training in evangelism, and it began offering diploma training in evangelism in 1995. Today it organises teaching through the Church Army Business School (Carlile School of Business), the School of Mission and the Centre for Continuing Education, and its admissions pages report 1,000+ students, 60+ lecturers and 5 campuses. Beyond the eight TVETA-registered KNEC and NITA awards in business management, electrical technology, food and beverage and social development, the site's application forms advertise additional programmes including CPA Foundation/Intermediate/Advanced, ICT, community development, catering and accommodation, secretarial studies, supply chain management, human resource management, sales and marketing and short courses such as barista, AutoCAD and QuickBooks. Students are supported by the Lynch Library, which holds 25,000 volumes with a KOHA online catalogue at library.carlilecollege.ac.ke, KLISC membership and e-resources, and the college runs a live Moodle e-learning platform at e-learn.carlilecollege.ac.ke.

context.description: The school was established at Mater Hospital in 1972 as a specialised one-year midwifery training programme and later expanded into general nursing education in September 2004. Its syllabus and examinations are set by the Nursing Council of Kenya, and students must pass the Council's final examination before they can be registered to practise. It offers a three-year Diploma in Kenya Registered Nursing together with one-year Higher Diplomas in perioperative, critical care, nephrology and midwifery nursing. Training combines classroom instruction, clinical teaching and practice in the hospital, and skills-laboratory work, and the school also provides hostels, a library and counselling services. TVETA lists the institution as a private technical vocational college, registration number TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0038/2015, registered and licensed to 26 November 2029. The school's own page prints the address nursingschool@materkenya.com alongside the telephone lines 0719073164 and 0732163164, so the e-mail is sourced to that page.

context.description: St. Mary's Medical Training College is a private medical training institution owned by the Catholic Diocese of Kakamega and based at Mumias Town in Kakamega County, Western Kenya. It was inaugurated by Rt. Rev. Bishop Sulumeti on 6 September 1994, having grown out of the Diocese's health services management at St. Mary's Hospital Mumias, and describes itself as Kenya's first private pioneer school of clinical medicine with the motto 'Outmones Omnibus Serviant' - service to humanity. The college diversified in 2021 into additional TVET-accredited medical programmes in perioperative theatre technology, community health and development, and mortuary science, offered at certificate and diploma levels alongside its diploma in clinical medicine and surgery. The TVETA register of accredited programmes records four competency-based qualifications delivered through TVET CDACC assessment - Community Health at Levels 5 and 6 and Perioperative Theatre Technology at Levels 5 and 6 - with the college's own website additionally listing clinical medicine and surgery, mortuary science and health assistant programmes that are not all reflected in the regulator's current list. The college publishes the email address info@stmarysmtc.co.ke and the telephone lines +254 725 782 475 and +254 769 515 475, and TVETA records its registration as TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0009/2024, registered on 25 April 2024 and licensed to 24 April 2029.

context.description: Chemichemi ya Uzima College is a private technical and vocational college registered by TVETA on 9 October 2023 under registration number TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0097/2023, with a register status of 'Registered Only'. Its main campus sits on Bogani Road in Karen, Nairobi, as confirmed by the college's contact page and its Google Business listing, which also carries the same phone number and website. Founded within the Association of Sisterhoods of Kenya (AOSK), the college states that it combines hands-on technical training with leadership development, ethics and practical mastery in modern laboratories, ICT facilities and a library. It runs a live Moodle e-learning platform at elearning.cyu.ac.ke alongside a student portal and digital library, and offers full-time and part-time schedules with January, May and September intakes. Academic delivery spans TVET CDACC Levels 4-6 in business, ICT, hospitality and social work, NITA trade-test artisan courses and KASNEB professional programmes (CPA, ATD, CAM).

description: Cherang'any Technical and Vocational College is a public Technical and Vocational College in Trans Nzoia County, in Kenya's Rift Valley region, and trades online as Cherangany TVC. The TVET Authority registered it under registration number TVETA/PUBLIC/TVC/0060/2021 on 22 October 2021 for a five-year term, and the live register now reports that licence as expired on 21 October 2026, with the institution detail page returning no accredited course table because of the lapse. The college's own website nevertheless advertises a full CDACC competency-based curriculum running across six departments, namely ICT and computer science, business and office administration, agriculture, fashion design and hairdressing, building and plumbing, and electrical engineering, with programmes at levels 4, 5 and 6. Where the website lists the same programme at more than one level, the highest level is recorded here to respect the name-keyed course constraint, and CDACC level 4, 5 and 6 are mapped to artisan, certificate and diploma respectively. The college publishes the email cheranganytvc@gmail.com, the telephone lines 0743836414 and 0762836414, and a postal address of P.O. Box 335 - 30200 Kitale, and names Mr Norbert Wafula as principal in its welcome message.

context.description: Cherished Hope Training College is a private technical and vocational college located in Eldoret, Uasin Gishu County, in Kenya's Rift Valley region. The TVET Authority register lists it as TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0148/2024, registered on 29 October 2024 with a licence valid to 28 October 2029, under category TVC and private ownership. Its accredited programme list spans NITA trade-test artisan courses in tailoring, dressmaking, hairdressing, beauty therapy, electrical wireman work and plumbing and pipe fitting, alongside a KNEC craft course in catering and accommodation operations and a TVET CDACC healthcare support services qualification. The college also promotes health services support (nursing assistant) and perioperative theatre technology training through its social media outreach, and offers fee arrangements in which students pay only admission and practical fees. No institutional website or e-learning portal has been published; the college is reachable by phone, email and its Facebook page.

description.history: Christian Industrial Training Centre (CITC) Nairobi was established in 1958 by the Anglican Church, with Rev. and Mrs. Charles Tett and a prayer group as its founders. It initially engaged youth from the nearby Majengo slums through a football club to deter them from vices. In 1960, a vocational training institute was formally set up at its current Pumwani location. Early instructors were volunteers from England, Australia, and New Zealand. The Church Missionary Society (CMS) was a significant contributor to its establishment and development. Since its inception, CITC Nairobi has trained over 25,000 graduates, focusing on producing highly skilled and competent technicians.
description.mission: CITC Nairobi's mission is to equip individuals with quality technical, professional, and entrepreneurial training through creativity and innovativeness for sustainable livelihood. about: Chuka Technical and Vocational College is a public Technical and Vocational College at Chuka in Tharaka Nithi County, Kenya, registered by the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority as TVETA/PUBLIC/TVC/0019/2018. The college opened in January 2018 after being mentored by Chuka University and later by Meru National Polytechnic, and delivers KNEC and TVET CDACC examined artisan, craft and diploma programmes in engineering, business, ICT, agriculture and cosmetology. The TVETA register places the college in Meru County, a legacy administrative label predating the creation of Tharaka Nithi County, while the college itself and this record are located in Tharaka Nithi.
description: Chuka Technical and Vocational College (Chuka TVC) is a public TVET institution established in 2015 as a government project to widen access to technical training in support of Kenya's Vision 2030 industrialisation goals. It was initially mentored by Chuka University, with mentorship later transferred to Meru National Polytechnic, and it admitted its first students in January 2018. The college is registered and licensed by the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority under number TVETA/PUBLIC/TVC/0019/2018, and the regulator's current course table lists 34 accredited programmes: artisan awards in electrical installation, masonry, plumbing and welding and fabrication; craft/certificate awards in electrical and electronics technology, ICT, mechanical engineering plant and production, secretarial studies and social development; diplomas in building technology, civil engineering, quantity surveying, mechanical and electrical engineering, agriculture, business management, human resource management, ICT, supply chain management and social work and community development, all examined by the Kenya National Examinations Council; and TVET CDACC competency-based programmes at Levels 4 to 6 in cosmetology, ICT, office assistance, land surveying, mechanical production technology, sustainable agriculture and agripreneurship. The college sits about 8 km along the Chuka–Kareni (Kathwana) road, roughly 5 km off Kaanwa market towards Mwanjati, and provides mechanical, building and civil, and electrical engineering workshops, ICT laboratories, agriculture facilities, neighbourhood hostels and a college mess on a pay-as-you-eat basis. The TVETA register records the college's county as Meru, a legacy label from before Tharaka Nithi County was created; the college's published address and this record place it at Chuka in Tharaka Nithi County within the Eastern region, and the divergence is recorded rather than silently reconciled. No e-learning or open distance learning platform is live: the college states that online learning will soon be introduced, so both learning-mode fields are recorded as implied only.

context.description: Clarence Matheny Bible College is a private Christian training institution in Limuru, Kiambu County, registered and licensed by the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority under registration number TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0091/2024, with a licence current to 31 July 2029. The college sits inside Clarence Matheny Ministries, founded by Clarence and Jewell Matheny in the early 1970s, and is delivered through the Clarence Matheny Leadership Training Institute, which describes itself as a recognised theological institution in East Africa. Its programmes are theological and ministerial rather than industrial: a Christian Chaplaincy Diploma taught as two years of full-time study or one year after Level 5, and Diploma, Certificate and Level 4 ministerial routes in transformational church leadership, ministry and chaplaincy. The college publishes entry requirements of a mean grade of D at KCSE or completion of KNQF Level 5 for the diploma route, advertises intakes in January, April and August, and quotes admission of 1,500 shillings with certificate and diploma tuition charged per semester. Teaching and accommodation share one campus: the institute publishes an auditorium, the Clarence House dormitory and the Jewel House guest rooms, and the college gives its address as P.O. Box 182 - 00217, Limuru, with the e-mail cmlti.cmm@gmail.com and telephone +254 722 137 257. context.about: The College of Sustainable Agriculture for Eastern Africa (CSAEA) is a TVET approved institution undertaking training in Sustainable Ecological Agriculture (SEA). context.description: Sub-Saharan Africa faces challenges in feeding its population and maintaining health, leading to pressure on small-scale farmers to adopt modern agricultural technologies. Small-scale farming, primarily for household food security and selling surplus produce, characterizes agricultural production in this region, which has hindered the adoption of mechanization, monoculture, and costly inputs. Recognizing these challenges, SACDEP-Kenya, to which CSAEA is affiliated, has been promoting agricultural practices that enhance social and environmental benefits for farmers since 1994. The college's site presents a Craft Certificate in Sustainable Ecological Agriculture as its formal curriculum, while the TVETA register entry TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0008/2021 records a licence expiry of 27 January 2026.

context.description: Computer Pride Training Centre is a privately owned technical and vocational college recorded in the TVETA register of accredited TVET institutions under registration number TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0002/2015, registered on 17 February 2015 with a licence valid to 2 July 2029 and a status of Registered and Licensed. It operates from JKUAT Towers on Kenyatta Avenue in Nairobi's central business district, with a Mombasa branch carrying a separate TVETA entry and the contact address mombasa@computer-pride.co.ke. The centre describes itself as having over 35 years of experience empowering individuals, professionals and organisations across Africa through IT training, internationally recognised certifications and enterprise technology solutions, with a regional footprint spanning Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Ethiopia, Rwanda, Burundi, Congo, Nigeria, Egypt, South Africa, Dubai and India. Its training catalogue advertises more than 2,000 active courses covering vendor certifications from Microsoft, Cisco, AWS, CompTIA, Google Cloud, Oracle and other partners, intensive career pathways, short courses and NCC Education academic programmes from diplomas to BSc degrees. Training is delivered in-person at the Nairobi centre and live online, with scheduled intakes published on its website and the ICDL International Certificate of Digital Literacy as its single TVETA-accredited qualification, assessed through ICDL Africa.

context.about: Consolata School of Nursing is the nursing school of Consolata Hospital Nkubu, a faith-based health institution under the Catholic Diocese of Meru, and its TVETA registration appears in the register under the registered name Catholic Diocese of Meru Consolata Nkubu Medical College.
context.description: This record is held as Consolata School of Nursing, the nursing school presented on the website of Consolata Hospital Nkubu, which describes the hospital as a faith-based health institution under the Catholic Diocese of Meru; the school page itself carries no course list or contact details for the school. context.about: Deeva College of Professional Studies is a TVETA-registered private vocational college in Bungoma Town, Western Kenya, training beauty therapists, hairdressers and cosmetologists since 2014 alongside an operating salon, barbershop and spa.
context.description: Deeva College of Professional Studies occupies the second floor of the New Nyanza Building opposite Equity Bank in Bungoma Town. The Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority registered it on 17 November 2014 as TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0002/2014 and the licence runs to 27 February 2030 with the status 'Registered and Licensed'. Its register table lists NITA trade tests in Hairdressing and Beauty Therapy, while the college's own pages advertise accredited diploma and certificate courses in Cosmetology, Hairdressing and Beauty Therapy. The college states that it issues a certificate of completion on graduation and runs a salon, barbershop and spa alongside the classrooms, which supply the practical training environment.

context.about: Defence Forces Technical College (DEFTEC) is a public technical and vocational college in Nairobi County, Kenya, registered and licensed by the TVET Authority and delivering engineering, aeronautical, marine and ICT diploma training.
context.description: Defence Forces Technical College, commonly abbreviated DEFTEC, is entered in the TVET Authority register under registration number TVETA/PUBLIC/TVC/0033/2016 as a public technical and vocational college, first registered on 28 January 2016 and licensed to 8 August 2029. The register's course table lists 14 award rows, deduplicated to the 12 distinct KNEC Diploma awards listed above. This pass fetched the college's parent-body pages: the Ministry of Defence site states DEFTEC is 'a premier institution located at Embakasi Garrison', tallies over 10,600 engineering and IT graduates, and records that it became a college of the National Defence University-Kenya at the 27 May 2021 charter, while a vetted reference listing naming the same TVETA registration number records telephone 0208091283 and email kaftec@mod.go.ke with the physical location Embakasi Garrison. The fetched Embakasi Garrison value now replaces the inherited town string 'Denis Building, Thika, Garissa Rd, Nairobi' in the payload, and the town disagreement is parked for sync_apply to adjudicate. The portfolio covers aeronautical and avionics engineering, automotive engineering, electrical specialisations, marine engineering, mechanical engineering specialisations, textile technology and information communication technology, all examined by the Kenya National Examinations Council at Diploma level.

context.description: Dental Aptitude College was registered by the TVET Authority on 26 April 2021 under registration number TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0046/2021, and the register snapshot of 25 October 2026 records the licence as Registered and Licensed with an expiry date of 11 August 2031. The TVETA course table lists six awards, all examined by the TVET Curriculum Development, Assessment and Certification Council: Caregiving at Level 4, Community Health at Level 5 and Level 6, Healthcare Support Services at Level 5, and Perioperative Theatre Technology at Level 5 and Level 6. Applying the level-normalisation convention used across this dataset, CDACC Level 4 is recorded at Artisan level, Level 5 at Certificate level and Level 6 at Diploma level, which separates the two Community Health entries and the two Perioperative Theatre Technology entries by qualification level rather than merging them. The college's own website is live and its contact block publishes the campus address 245 Muringa Road, Kilimani, Nairobi, the line +254 743 888222 and the e-mail info@dentalaptitudecollege.com, so the settlement Nairobi, the published street line and those contacts are recorded here instead of remaining null.

context.description: Dermal Training Institute (DTI) is a private training institution on Muthithi Road in Nairobi that specialises in skin science, aesthetics, beauty therapy and wellness education. It is registered and licensed by TVETA as a private technical and vocational college (TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0184/2025) and is an approved VTCT Skills (iTEC) centre offering internationally recognised beauty and aesthetics qualifications. Training integrates classroom theory with active clinical practice so students gain real-world client experience, and study is offered full-time, part-time or at weekends. Its portfolio spans iTEC-approved programmes in anatomy and physiology, holistic massage and beauty specialism, alongside DTI certificates in nail technology, makeup artistry, reflexology, microshading, eyelash extensions, advanced diagnostic skin analysis and cosmetic chemistry. The institute also delivers corporate spa training packages such as the Quick-Start Program for New Hires, spa foundation training, spa safety and compliance, and customer experience and service excellence.

The centre's own website is live and publishes the campus address Langata Road, Karen, Nairobi, together with the e-mail dbbtkaren@donbosco.or.ke and the telephone lines +254 795 693 423 and +254 742 374 651. Those published details are now recorded in the identity fields, so the settlement Nairobi and the street line no longer sit at unknown.

name: Don Bosco Technical Institute - Kakuma

context.about: Don Bosco Technical Institute - Kakuma is a private technical and vocational college in Kakuma Refugee Camp, Turkana County, Kenya, run by the Salesians of Don Bosco Eastern Africa and registered by TVETA as TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0090/2017.
context.description: Don Bosco Technical Institute - Kakuma is a private Technical and Vocational College in Kakuma Refugee Camp, Turkana County, in the diocese of Lodwar, owned and administered by the Salesians of Don Bosco Eastern Africa and recorded in the TVETA register as TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0090/2017 (registered 19 June 2017, licence valid to 25 January 2028, status 'Registered and Licensed'). Its accredited table combines three KNEC craft awards in general agriculture, information communication technology and secretarial studies with eight NITA trade-test artisan awards across carpentry and joinery, electrical wiring, masonry, motor vehicle mechanics, plumbing and pipe fitting, tailoring, welding and fabrication, and dressmaking. The institute's lived site, donboscokakuma.org (redirecting into its /2 section), was re-fetched on 2026-11-08 and confirms the Kakuma location, the Salesians of Don Bosco Eastern Africa ownership, the online application address dbkakvtc@donbosco.or.ke, and additional programme rows beyond the register: KASNEB-examined CPA, Accounting Technicians Diploma (ATD), Diploma in Credit Management (DCM) and Certificate in Accounting and Management Skills (CAMS), plus KNEC ICT and NITA technical and computer operator courses; the KASNEB programmes are site-advertised, not register-accredited, so they remain described rather than carried as accredited award rows. Its header contact page form is under maintenance, so a fresh telephone/e-mail printout was not obtained this pass and the stored contact lines are kept pending independent corroboration; UNHCR, Don Bosco Mission Germany and SlovakAid are listed as partners on the institute's site.

context.description: Don Bosco Technical Institute - Marsabit is a private vocational training centre classified by the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority as a VTC in Marsabit County, Kenya. The authority's register records its registration number as TVETA/PRIVATE/VTC/0003/2018 with a licence valid to 2 July 2029 and the status 'Registered and Licensed', under private ownership. Its accredited programme table publishes nine qualifications: a Kenya National Examinations Council craft course in secretarial studies and eight artisan-level trade-test courses assessed by the National Industrial Training Authority in carpentry and joinery, hairdressing, masonry, motor vehicle mechanics, tailoring, welding and fabrication, dressmaking and beauty therapy. The institute is managed by the Salesians of Don Bosco and, per the Don Bosco Kenya network site, reaches out particularly to pastoralist communities in Marsabit, equipping them with skills for employment and entrepreneurship. Its own website donboscomarsabit.org describes it as a private college accredited by TVETA, located in Saku Constituency, Marsabit County, with contact line 0772-860-378, email principalmarsabit@donbosco.or.ke and postal address P.O. Box 8 – 60500, Marsabit.

context.description: East Africa Institute of Certified Studies trades publicly as ICS Technical College and is a private tertiary institution whose Kisumu campus sits in Mayfair Plaza on Oginga Odinga Road in Kisumu CBD, with the branch having opened in June 2017. Its website ics.ac.ke publishes a programme catalogue spanning schools of Business, Tourism & Travel, Medical/Nursing & Health Sciences, Fashion & Design, Beauty & Hairdressing, Agriculture, Social Sciences, Security/Criminal Justice & Forensic Studies, ICT, Engineering, Building Technology & Interior Design and Hospitality. Programmes are examined by KNEC, TVET CDACC, KASNEB, ICM, ABMA, IATA, NITA and NASCOP, and the site presents these regulators and examining bodies as its partners.
