context.description: KMTC Kitui Campus was established in 2004 as a constituent college of the Kenya Medical Training College, and its first intake of 40 students reported in September of that year for the Diploma in Kenya Registered Community Health Nursing, which remains the campus's flagship award. The campus sits one kilometre from Kitui town along Hospital Road, next to the hospital then recorded as Kitui District Hospital, on 20 acres of land provided by the local community through the District Development Committee, and it occupies premises that formerly housed Better Living Institute Kitui. Its published programme portfolio spans eight awards: the 3.5-year Diploma in Kenya Registered Community Health Nursing, the 2.5-year World Bank sponsored Certificate in Kenya Enrolled Community Health Nursing, three-year diplomas in Medical Laboratory Sciences, Clinical Medicine and Environmental Health Sciences, a two-year Certificate in Health Records and Information Sciences, a two-year self-sponsored upgrading Diploma in Health Records and Information Sciences, and a two-year Certificate in Environmental Health Sciences. Teaching resources include two computer laboratories (a 30-desktop laboratory supported by the USAID Capacity Kenya Project as a family planning and reproductive health resource centre, and a JHPIEGO-funded phlebotomy resource centre with 20 computers), a demonstration laboratory for medical laboratory students, a skills laboratory with anatomical models, an administration block housing the library and a conference hall, a college bus, a standby generator, hostels accommodating more than half of the student population and a dining hall. The campus hosts two centres of excellence, one in family planning and reproductive health training launched on 21 April 2011 under a partnership between the Ministry of Health, KMTC and the USAID Capacity Kenya Project, and one in phlebotomy and safe specimen collection established under the JHPIEGO project. The campus email kitui@kmtc.ac.ke, its postal address Box 711-90200 Kitui, its telephone lines 020 3503234 and 0791360229 and its physical address on the Kitui-Kibwezi Road are published on the College's campus page, which is now only available as a 6 June 2017 Wayback Machine capture; the number held in the institution record could not be re-confirmed because the current campus contacts document could not be fetched in this pass. No campus-level student population, accreditation register entry or distance-learning provision is published, and the examination body for each award is recorded as internal rather than guessed.

context.description: Established in 1977, KMTC Kwale Campus was founded to address the critical need for training Public Health Officers in Kwale County. The college became operational from 1977 and was initially housed by the Government Training Institute, with land for its own development allocated in 1998. It gained autonomous status in 2015 and relocated to Tumbe in Msambweni Sub-County in 2016, where it sits next to Msambweni County Referral and Teaching Hospital. The campus is one of the 71 KMTC Colleges in Kenya, headed by Principal Ms. Kavwa Saidi Mwakaribu, with a student population of over 240. Its mission, aligned with the broader KMTC vision, is to develop fit-for-purpose middle-level health professionals through transformative training, research, and consultancy.

context.description: KMTC Lake Victoria Campus is a campus of the Kenya Medical Training College, the State Corporation established by an Act of Parliament under the Ministry of Health that trains middle-level health professionals for Kenya and the wider region. The campus was established in July 2013 as part of KMTC's expansion programme and sits in Kisumu County along Angawa Avenue, adjacent to Kisumu County Hospital, on approximately 3.5 hectares of land. The college's official campus contacts directory lists the campus as L. VICTORIA at P.O. Box 2268-40100 Kisumu, with the institutional e-mail address lakevictoria@kmtc.ac.ke and the telephone lines 0202584613/0759061689. The campus is headed by Principal Ms. Catherine A. Omasaja and hosts a student population of over 422 students. Its students undertake clinical placements at Kisumu County Hospital, Jaramogi Oginga Odinga Teaching and Referral Hospital, Kakamega Teaching and Referral Hospital, Vihiga County Hospital and Siaya County Hospital, as well as rural health facilities within and outside Kisumu County. The September 2025 Academic Programmes booklet names Lake Victoria among the campuses offering the upgrading Diploma in Public Health, the upgrading Diploma in Medical Laboratory Sciences and the upgrading Diploma in Community Health.

context.description: KMTC Makueni Campus is a campus of the Kenya Medical Training College, the state corporation established by an Act of Parliament under the Ministry of Health that runs 92 campuses across 46 counties with a student population the college reports as over 80,000. The college's February 2026 campus contacts directory gives the campus postal address P.O. Box 198-90300 Makueni, its institutional mailbox makueni@kmtc.ac.ke and its telephone line 0706037168, which match the values already held on this record. The college's September 2025 academic programmes booklet names Makueni as a centre for the upgrading Diploma in Nutrition and Dietetics, the upgrading Diploma in Orthopaedics and Trauma Medicine, the upgrading Diploma in Community Health and the upgrading Diploma in Health Records and Information, and lists it among campuses offering the one-year Health Care Assistant course; those campus-specific listings are the courses recorded here. KMTC teaches a unified curriculum across its campuses and operates the live Moodle portal at https://elearning.kmtc.ac.ke/, through which it delivers course content and examinations, and it publishes distance-learning higher diplomas including Palliative Care Nursing and Family Health Nursing. Campus-level student numbers, a street address, facilities and named campus officers are not published, so they remain null and the contacts list is empty.

context.description: KMTC Marsabit Campus is a campus of the Kenya Medical Training College, the State Corporation established by an Act of Parliament under the Ministry of Health that trains middle-level health workers, and it appears in the college's official campus contacts directory with its own postal address, institutional email and telephone line at P.O. Box 103-60500, Marsabit. The campus is listed in KMTC's Academic Programmes booklet as of September 2025 as one of the campuses offering the one-year Health Care Assistant course, whose entry requirement is a minimum D plain in KCSE. KMTC's own news pages describe the campus as running clinical placements at the Laisamis maternity wing for students pursuing nursing, clinical medicine and community health assistant programmes, indicating that the campus trains across more than the health care assistant course recorded here as a regulator-documented award. KMTC examines and awards its own certificate and diploma qualifications through the college board, so those awards are recorded with an internal examining body rather than an external national examination council. No campus-specific student population figure is published and the college operates a single institutional website at kmtc.ac.ke, so the campus has no separate domain of its own.

Its published awards include the Higher Diploma in Addictive Sciences and the Higher Diploma in Mental Health and Psychiatry in the college's upgrading and higher-diploma bulletin, alongside a Diploma in Kenya Registered Nursing (Mental Health and Psychiatry) reported by directory listings. context.description: KMTC Meru Campus is one of the campuses of the Kenya Medical Training College, the public State corporation under the Ministry of Health that trains the bulk of Kenya's mid-level clinical and health workforce. The college's official campus contacts directory lists Meru with the postal address P.O. Box 1484-60200 Meru, the campus email address meru@kmtc.ac.ke and the telephone numbers 064-3132537 and 0794673190, placing it in Meru County in the Eastern region. The college publishes 126 medical courses across seven faculties and eighteen departments, spanning certificate, diploma, higher diploma and short-course provision, and its academic programmes page details the certificate and diploma lists reproduced here. Campus-level allocation of individual programmes is not published in the public academic programmes listing, so this record lists the college-level certificate and diploma health programmes that define KMTC provision without asserting which of them are currently mounted at Meru. KMTC operates a shared e-learning platform at elearning.kmtc.ac.ke, an admissions portal at admissions.kmtc.ac.ke and a student portal at portal.kmtc.ac.ke, all linked from the kmtc.ac.ke site, and its headquarters sit off Ngong Road in Nairobi.

context.about: KMTC Mwingi Campus is a constituent campus of the Kenya Medical Training College, the public State Corporation that trains middle-level health professionals in Kenya. It opened in September 2015 after consultative meetings between the KMTC Board of Management, the Kitui County Government and Mwingi Level IV Hospital, and it operates on a five-acre site adjacent to that hospital in Mwingi town.
context.description: KMTC Mwingi Campus opened in September 2015 following a series of consultative meetings between the KMTC Board of Management, the Kitui County Government and Mwingi Level IV Hospital, and it was officially opened by President Uhuru Kenyatta on 11 June 2016. The campus occupies a five-acre piece of land adjacent to Mwingi Level IV Hospital, roughly one kilometre off the Mwingi–Garissa road along the Mwingi–Nzeluni road in Mwingi town, Kitui County, and is one of the Kenya Medical Training College's constituent campuses; it is headed by Principal Ms. Mary M. Kibui. Independent education pages report the campus's offer as a Diploma in Community Health Nursing alongside plans, recorded on the KMTC's own archived campus page, to add Clinical Medicine and short courses; the fetched education pages list the currently taught Diploma in Nursing and Diploma in Clinical Medicine with a planned Diploma in Pharmacy and a short course in HIC testing. Students gain clinical experience at Mwingi Level IV Hospital next door and at Migwani, Tseikuru and Kyuso hospitals, Ngomeni, Waita and Nguni health centres and Kitui County Referral Hospital. The campus publishes well-furnished classrooms, a fully equipped skills laboratory, a well-stocked medical library and an administration block among its facilities, and third-party pages report a student population above 835 as of 2023. Contact details were verbatim-corroborated on the fetched Teacher.co.ke and Daily Press pages: postal address The Principal, KMTC Mwingi Campus, P.O. Box 232-90400 Mwingi; telephone 0732405209 (with 0723359440 additionally listed by Daily Press) and email mwingi@kmtc.ac.ke. No separate campus e-learning provision or distance-learning programme is published, and the examination body for each award is internal to KMTC.

context.description: KMTC Nairobi Campus is the main campus of the Kenya Medical Training College, the public health-training institution headquartered off Ngong Road in Nairobi with a postal address of P.O. courses.name: Certificate in Health Records and Information Technology

context.description: Established in 2016, the campus specifically targets the modernization of Kenya's health workforce by training specialists in health information management and data-driven public health. Its unique value proposition is its direct affiliation with the Othaya Level 6 Hospital and several local Level 4 facilities, providing students with intensive exposure to digital health record systems in a clinical setting. The institution plays a critical role in the national shift toward Universal Health Coverage by producing community health workers who are experts in data management and primary care support. It is the premier choice for students aiming for administrative and data-centric roles in the healthcare sector.

Ministry of Health

context.description: KMTC Rachuonyo Campus is one of the constituent campuses of the Kenya Medical Training College, the public health training institution that trains middle-level health professionals for the Kenyan health sector, and it serves the Rachuonyo and wider Homa Bay County catchment from Oyugis town. The KMTC library catalogue records the campus address as post office box 148, Oyugis 40222, Kenya, with the telephone number 0748034396, and the college's published campus contacts list gives the campus email address rachuonyo@kmtc.ac.ke. Its programmes are the KMTC certificate and diploma health qualifications placed through the Kenya Universities and Colleges Central Placement Service, namely Certificate in Community Health Assistant, Certificate in Health Records and Information Technology and Diploma in Community Health, all examined by the college itself rather than by an external national examinations board. The campus shares the college-wide e-learning platform at elearning.kmtc.ac.ke and the staff and student portal at portal.kmtc.ac.ke, and its library holds the college's medical and health sciences collection. No campus-specific published fee schedule, student population figure or campus management contact name was located in a trusted fetched source during this research, so those fields are recorded as null rather than estimated.

context.description: KMTC Voi Campus is one of the 92 campuses of the Kenya Medical Training College, a State Corporation established through an Act of Parliament under the Ministry of Health to train middle-level health professionals for Kenya and beyond; the parent college reports over 80,000 students spread across 46 of the 47 counties. The Voi campus sits in Voi town in Taita Taveta County on the Coast, and is reported to have been established in 2016 as the first medical training college in the county. Its programmes are placed through the KUCCPS portal under campus code 5120, where the Diploma in Kenya Registered Community Health Nursing is listed for Voi (5120K04) alongside diploma and certificate programmes in clinical medicine, health records, orthopaedic trauma, community health and emergency medical technology. Students are supported by the college-wide Moodle e-learning platform at elearning.kmtc.ac.ke and the student portal at portal.kmtc.ac.ke, and the campus can be reached by post at P.O. Box 18-80300, Voi, or by phone on +254 705 751103.

context.about: KMTC Webuye Campus is a campus of the Kenya Medical Training College, the State Corporation established by an Act of Parliament under the Ministry of Health to train middle-level health professionals for Kenya. It is addressed at P.O. context.description: KMTC Webuye Campus is a campus of the Kenya Medical Training College, the State Corporation established by an Act of Parliament under the Ministry of Health that trains middle-level health workers for Kenya and the region. It appears in the college's official campus contacts directory at P.O. Box 734-50205, Webuye, with its own institutional email address, webuye@kmtc.ac.ke, and telephone line 020-2574902. KMTC's Academic Programmes booklet as of September 2025 lists Webuye among the campuses offering the one-year Health Care Assistant course, and among the campuses offering the upgrading Diploma in Community Health for holders of a KMTC certificate in community health and the upgrading Diploma in Health Records and Information for holders of a certificate in health records and information technology. Because the college examines and awards its own certificate and diploma qualifications through the KMTC board, the three campus programmes are recorded with an internal examining body. No campus-specific student population figure is published, and the college operates one institutional website at kmtc.ac.ke rather than separate campus domains.

context.about: Kaaleng Vocational Training Center is a public vocational training centre in Turkana County, Kenya. Registered and licensed by the TVET Authority (TVETA/PUBLIC/VTC/0053/2017), it delivers NITA trade-test artisan training in electrical wiring, hairdressing, masonry, motor vehicle mechanics, tailoring, dressmaking and beauty therapy to youth in the Kaaleng-Kaikor area.

context.description: Kaaleng Vocational Training Center is a public vocational training centre serving the Kaaleng-Kaikor area of Turkana County, with its postal address at P.O. Box 15-30504, Lokitaung. The TVET Authority register lists it as TVETA/PUBLIC/VTC/0053/2017, registered on 19 June 2017 with a licence valid to 25 January 2028, under category VTC and public ownership. Its accredited programmes are seven NITA trade-test artisan courses covering electrical wireman work, hairdressing, masonry, motor vehicle mechanics, tailoring, dressmaking and beauty therapy. Turkana County's own website article of 13 May 2024 ('Turkana TVET trainers equipped to boost competency-based education implementation'), preserved by the Internet Archive capture of 21 March 2025, lists the county's vocational training institutions as operating in Lodwar, Lokichar, Lokichoggio, Lokori, Kataboi, Lorgum and Kaaleng-Kaikor, catering to roughly 5,500 county trainees, which identifies the Kaaleng-Kaikor locality as this centre's host area. The centre maintains a Facebook page through which it reports engagement with the County Government of Turkana on strengthening high-quality, industry-relevant training for local youth. No official source publishes a telephone line, email address or institutional website for the centre, so those fields are left empty; the address tetvc.ac.ke that appears in one database belongs to Turkana East TVC, a different institution, and was not carried into this record.

context.description: Kacheliba Technical Training Institute is a public TVC in West Pokot County, registered by TVETA under TVETA/PUBLIC/TVC/0026/2025 with a status of Registered and Licensed. Its own website publishes the campus address as Kodich, P.O. Box 201, 30600 Kapenguria, together with the general email info@kachelibatti.ac.ke, an admissions address admission@kachelibatti.ac.ke, a single telephone/WhatsApp line and office hours of Monday to Friday, 08:00 to 17:00. The published catalogue runs to more than forty competency-based programmes across five departments - Building & Civil Engineering, Mechanical & Automotive Engineering, Computing Hospitality & Fashion, Electrical & Electronics Engineering, and Business & Liberal Studies - from Level 3 artisan to Level 6 diploma, all certified by TVET CDACC. The institute styles itself a Centre of Excellence in Building & Civil Engineering and promotes climate-smart training, mandatory three-month industry attachments and January, May and September intakes. It reports 300+ trainees and admits Form Four leavers with a KCSE mean grade of D- and above as well as Jua Kali artisans and professionals.

context.description: Kaelo Technical and Vocational College (Kaelo TVC) is a public technical and vocational college at Laare in Igembe North sub-county, Meru County, eastern Kenya. It is registered and licensed by the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority under registration number TVETA/PUBLIC/TVC/0037/2018, registered on 12 October 2018 with a licence valid to 24 October 2029. The college advertises more than 64 training programmes across 10+ departments with over 2,000 students enrolled, and publishes its motto as 'Innovation for a Better Future'. Its stated mission is to provide quality technical and vocational education that empowers students with practical skills and knowledge for successful careers and entrepreneurship, and its vision is to be the leading technical and vocational training institution in the region, recognized for excellence in skills development and innovation. Training runs under KNEC, TVET CDACC (competency-based) and NITA curricula, alongside a Jitume digital laboratory and Dual TVET workplace training.

description: Kaelo Technical and Vocational College (Kaelo TVC) is a public technical and vocational college at Laare in Igembe North sub-county, Meru County, eastern Kenya. It is registered and licensed by the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority under registration number TVETA/PUBLIC/TVC/0037/2018, registered on 12 October 2018 with a licence valid to 24 October 2029. The college's stated mission is to provide quality technical and vocational education that equips trainees with practical skills and knowledge for successful careers and entrepreneurship, and its vision is to be the leading technical and vocational training institution in the region. Its programmes are organised into agriculture and environmental sciences, building and civil engineering, business and entrepreneurial studies, computing and informatics, electrical and electronics, and fashion and design, and it delivers both conventional and dual-training (Dual TVET) modes. The TVETA register lists 42 accredited qualifications covering KNEC craft and diploma awards, NITA trade tests and TVET CDACC competency levels three to six, and the college runs a government-backed Jitume digital laboratory and held its first graduation ceremony in September 2026.

context.description: Kaimosi Friends Vocational Training Centre is a public vocational training centre at Kaimosi in Vihiga County, operating from the Kaimosi Complex on the Chavakali-Kapsabet road. It began in 1983 as Kaimosi Youth Polytechnic, a church-based institution managed by the East Africa Yearly Meeting (E.A.Y.M), and was taken over by the government in 2009, making it a public institution. The TVET Authority register records it as TVETA/PUBLIC/VTC/0094/2017, registered on 12 October 2017 with a licence valid to 19 August 2029, under category VTC and public ownership. Its TVETA-accredited programmes are five KNEC National Vocational Certificates covering agri-business, appropriate carpentry and joinery, electrical and electronics technology, fashion design and garment making, and food processing technology, while the county government lists further trade areas including motor vehicle mechanics, building and construction, hairdressing and beauty therapy, and ICT, examined through KNEC and NITA. In August 2026 an ABDP/NORAD-ARNSA implementation support mission visited aquaponics construction on site as the project approaches completion.

context.description: Kamel Park Training College, which brands itself KAPATCO, is a private TVET institution established in 2024 on the Kisii-Kilgoris road in Kisii County, with its campus in the Kiogoro area off that road. It was registered by the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority on 25 April 2025 under registration number TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0075/2025, with a licence recorded as valid to 24 April 2030 and a status of 'Registered and Licensed'. Its stated mission is to deliver vocational education that equips students with practical skills tailored to industry demands, and the college credits founder Jackson Ondiba's more than 25 years in education as central to its leadership. The TVETA register lists thirteen competency-based programmes examined by TVET CDACC, spanning business, information communication technology, hospitality, tourism, journalism and the creative arts, while the college website advertises a broader catalogue of diploma and certificate courses lasting from three months to two and a half years. Students are served by a live e-learning platform at elearning.kamelparkcollege.co.ke with student, lecturer and admin portals, plus on-campus hostels with Wi-Fi, dining, study rooms and 24/7 security. Admissions run through info@kamelparkcollege.co.ke and +254 755 386 594, with online application supported on the website.

context.description: Kapchepkor Technical Training Institute (KTTI), formerly Baringo North Technical and Vocational College, is a public institution at Kapchepkor Market Centre in Baringo County, Kenya. It was established under the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Act of 2013 and is registered by TVETA under number TVETA/PUBLIC/TVC/0006/2023, registered on 26 January 2023 with a licence valid to 25 January 2028. name: Karen Hospital Medical Training College

context.about: The Karen Hospital Medical Training College is a private medical training college in Nairobi County, Kenya, registered and licensed by the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority as TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0096/2017. It trains nurses, theatre technologists and specialist clinicians, and its courses are assessed by the Nursing Council of Kenya and the TVET Curriculum Development, Assessment and Certification Council.
context.description: The Karen Hospital Medical Training College (TKHMTC) is a private medical training college registered by the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority under registration number TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0096/2017, with a licence valid to 2 July 2029. It is the training arm associated with The Karen Hospital and positions itself around three pillars of academic excellence, professionalism and discipline, with a vision of becoming a model faculty for competent healthcare professionals in Kenya and beyond. Its published programmes are the Diploma in Kenya Registered Nursing (three years), the Diploma in Peri-operative Theatre Technology (two years), the Higher Diploma in Cardiology (18 months), the Higher Diploma in Cardiopulmonary Perfusion (two years) and a Community Health course, supplemented by Basic and Advanced Life Support short courses. The TVETA register of accredited programmes lists four additional CDACC qualifications in business management and community health at Levels 4, 5 and 6. The college displays accreditation marks for the Nursing Council of Kenya, TVET CDACC, HELB and LEAP on its website, and its published contact line is 0727 254222, with a second line on 0709 382086 and a postal address of P.O. Box 74240-00200.

context.description: Karumo Technical Training Institute is a public TVET institution under the Ministry of Education's State Department for Vocational and Technical Training, located in Athwana Location, Tigania West Sub-county, Meru County — about 3 km off the Meru-Maua road along Kwa Amos Junction. Established in 2015, the institute describes itself as celebrating over ten years of excellence in technical education and reports more than 140 professional staff and over 70 technical programmes. Its published course catalogue lists 75 programmes, the large majority accredited by TVET CDACC, spanning ICT and cybersecurity, building technology, civil engineering, electrical and electronics engineering, agriculture and environmental studies, hospitality and tourism, fashion and design, and cosmetology. The institute also advertises KASNEB professional qualifications, a Dual TVET programme built around industry-based apprenticeships, and Recognition of Prior Learning pathways. It is registered with TVETA (TVETA/PUBLIC/TVC/0014/2016) and is a registered KASNEB examination centre, and holds ODPC data-protection registration and ISO 27001:2013 certification for its information security management system.

context.description: Karuru Vocational Training Centre is recorded by the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority as TVETA/PUBLIC/VTC/0015/2018, a public vocational training centre in Murang'a County first registered on 12 January 2018 at Kahuro in Mugoiri Ward. The regulator's record shows the licence as expired on 25 April 2026, and because the institution is in expired status TVETA publishes no course table for it, so this record cannot carry a regulator-verified programme list; the single course entry recorded here, beauty and cosmetology, comes from 2021 press coverage describing the centre's then-new department and is marked with an unstated examination body rather than an assumed one. The same coverage reported carpentry production, plumbing, electrical and masonry trades activity at the centre, a trainee population rising from 49 to about 150 in 2021, and upgrading works funded by a charity and the county government. No official website, email address or telephone number could be verified from a primary institutional source, so contact fields are left empty.

context.description: Kasarani Technical and Vocational College is a public Technical and Vocational College recorded in the TVETA register of accredited TVET institutions as TVETA/PUBLIC/TVC/0022/2017, registered on 12 April 2017 with a licence valid to 18 July 2028 under the status registered and licensed. It is located in Nairobi County, in the Nairobi region. The register lists seventy accredited course rows: six KNEC artisan awards in electrical installation, food and beverage, general agriculture, motor vehicle mechanics, plumbing and welding and fabrication; fifteen KNEC craft programmes spanning automotive and mechanical engineering, building technology, business management, catering and accommodation, electrical and electronics technology, human resource management, ICT, information studies, supply chain management, social development and welding; twelve KNEC diploma programmes including agriculture, civil-adjacent building technology, electrical and electronics engineering, mechanical engineering (production) and social work and community development; one NVCET award in agri-business; and thirty-five TVET CDACC competency-based awards from level 3 to level 6. Register levels were normalised to the schema vocabulary, with Craft rendered as Certificate, NVCET rendered as Certificate, CDACC levels 3 and 4 rendered as Artisan, level 5 as Certificate and level 6 as Diploma. The college's own site at kasaranitechnical.ac.ke is live and states that the institution opened to its first trainees in September 2018 and is situated in Nairobi at Kasarani Constituency, 1.5 km from Kamulu Shopping Centre off Kangundo Road. Its contact page publishes a postal address of P.O. Box 51898-00200, Nairobi and the telephone line +254 716685054, and prints the template placeholder info@example.com in place of a real mailbox, so no institutional e-mail is recorded.

The register lists seventy accredited course rows: six KNEC artisan awards in electrical installation, food and beverage, general agriculture, motor vehicle mechanics, plumbing and welding and fabrication; fifteen KNEC craft programmes spanning automotive and mechanical engineering, building technology, business management, catering and accommodation, electrical and electronics technology, human resource management, ICT, information studies, supply chain management, social development and welding; twelve KNEC diploma programmes including agriculture, civil-adjacent building technology, electrical and electronics engineering, mechanical engineering (production) and social work and community development; one NVCET award in agri-business; and thirty-five TVET CDACC competency-based awards from level 3 to level 6. Register levels were normalised to the schema vocabulary, with Craft rendered as Certificate, NVCET rendered as Certificate, CDACC levels 3 and 4 rendered as Artisan, level 5 as Certificate and level 6 as Diploma. The college's own site at kasaranitechnical.ac.ke is live and states that the institution opened to its first trainees in September 2018 and is situated in Nairobi at Kasarani Constituency, 1.5 km from Kamulu Shopping Centre off Kangundo Road. Its contact page publishes a postal address of P.O. Box 51898-00200, Nairobi and the telephone line +254 716685054, and prints the template placeholder info@example.com in place of a real mailbox, so no institutional e-mail is recorded.

context.description: Kathonzweni Vocational Training Center is a public vocational training centre serving Kathonzweni in Makueni County, Kenya. context.description: KENA Hair and Beauty Training College is a private technical and vocational college operating from the third floor of Arnold Plaza in Westlands, Nairobi County. The Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority registered it under number TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0233/2025 on 6 November 2025, with a licence running to 5 November 2030 and a status of 'Registered and Licensed'. The regulator's register snapshot of 24 October 2026 publishes no accredited course table for the college, so the programme data recorded here comes entirely from the college's own courses page, which lists five main programmes: Cosmetology Level 6 as a seventeen-month diploma, Hairdressing Level 6 as an eight-month diploma, Beauty Therapy Level 6 as a nine-month diploma, and Hairdressing Level 5 and Beauty Therapy Level 5 as six-month certificates. Hairdressing and beauty therapy are therefore recorded twice each, at diploma and certificate level, with the level carried in the label so the two awards stay distinct. The college does not state the examining or awarding body for any of these programmes on the pages fetched, so exam_body is recorded as unknown rather than assumed from the CDACC-style level numbering. The site also publishes roughly forty short professional courses of one to four months in barbering, bridal styling, wig production, chemical hair work, natural hair care, nail technology, massage therapies and advanced facial treatments, which fall outside the schema's qualification levels and are therefore described here rather than listed as courses. The published contacts are the e-mail info@kenahairandbeautytrainingcollege.co.ke and the telephone lines +254 712 111122, +254 738 424240 and +254 777 424240. No e-learning platform, distance-learning mode, campus facility inventory or student enrolment total is published on the fetched pages.

name: Kengen Geothermal Training Centre

context.about: KenGen Geothermal Training Centre is the geothermal training institution of the Kenya Electricity Generating Company, based at Olkaria Geothermal Plaza in Naivasha, Nakuru County. It trains energy professionals in geothermal power plant operations, geology, geochemistry, geophysics and reservoir monitoring, combining classroom teaching with practical work at active geothermal sites and in its simulation and laboratory facilities.
context.description: The centre presents itself as East Africa's geothermal training centre and describes programmes in renewable energy, power plant operations and geological sciences. Its published diploma portfolio covers power plant operations and maintenance, geology technology, geothermal geochemistry technology, applied geophysics technology, steam systems technology, reservoir monitoring technology and energy project management, each advertised as a two-year programme. Training is supported by modern classrooms, a power plant simulation centre, a geology and geophysics laboratory, field training sites at active geothermal locations, an engineering workshop and a resource centre and library. The institution also runs short courses of five to fifteen days in SCADA, substation switching, high-voltage cable termination, grid operations, gas and steam turbines, and geothermal engineering, plus recognition of prior learning assessments in trades such as welding, masonry, carpentry, electrical installation and plumbing.

context.description: Kenswed Technical and Vocational Training College (KTVTC) was established in 2020 under the Kenswed Organization, with support from Swedish partners, to provide quality and affordable education. The institution's mission is to empower and equip youth with employable and self-reliant skills, creating a pathway to sustainable livelihoods. During the challenging times of the COVID-19 pandemic, KTVTC provided online classes in Computer Programming, basic ICT skills, and Entrepreneurship, offering a lifeline for numerous youths. The college officially opened its physical doors in September 2020, initially welcoming 20 students in hairdressing and beauty, and celebrated its inaugural graduation in June 2021 with 63 graduates across diverse courses. KTVTC fosters entrepreneurship by offering a platform for alumni to pitch innovative ideas through its competitive Start Up Accelerator Program (STAP), providing business loans to turn dreams into reality. The college also ensures graduates thrive through mentorship from industry leaders, post-graduation follow-ups, and additional support such as workshops and entrepreneurship assistance. KTVTC envisions becoming the leading training center in the region, setting the benchmark for excellence in vocational and technical education.

context.description: Kenswed Vocational Training Center appears in the TVETA register of accredited TVET institutions under registration number TVETA/PRIVATE/VTC/0007/2022, registered on 27 July 2022 in Kajiado County with a recorded expiry date of 26 July 2027, and the register marks the entry as Deregistered rather than licensed. The register separately carries a Kenswed Technical and Vocational Training College under TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0023/2024, which is the entity that publishes the ktvtc.ac.ke site at Ngong used by this record. Because neither register entry publishes an accredited course table, the course row carries a single placeholder recording that no verified programme name is available instead of programme names taken from the college's marketing pages. The ktvtc.ac.ke homepage lists teaching departments in ICT, fashion and design, cosmetology, hospitality, engineering, business and health sciences, together with a library, cafeteria, student portal and an eLearning link at elearning.ktvtc.ac.ke, but those departmental pages are the college's own marketing and were not treated as accredited awards. The entity question between the deregistered VTC row and the licensed TVC row is logged for the owner rather than resolved here, and no verified student population or named administrator could be confirmed.

context.description: Kenya Aeronautical College has trained aviation professionals at Wilson Airport in Nairobi since 2003 and describes itself as one of the region's most established aviation training institutions. It offers KCAA-aligned instruction in pilot training, aeronautical engineering, cabin crew, flight operations and airport operations, delivered with aircraft, workshops and industry links on the Wilson Airport campus. Published programme lists cover diploma pathways in aeronautical engineering (airframes and engines, and avionics), airline cabin crew, flight operations and dispatch, air cargo, airport operations, airline marketing, fares and ticketing and customer service, alongside certificate courses and an aircraft maintenance engineers licence track. TVETA separately registers the college as TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0116/2016 with accredited KNEC programmes in business management, banking and finance, human resource management, sales and marketing, marketing and co-operative management. Enrolment enquiries are handled on the college's published telephone lines and through application@kac.co.ke and info@kac.co.ke.

context.description: KAG EAST University is a private Christian university owned by the Kenya Assemblies of God and fully chartered by the Commission for University Education since November 2016. Its roots trace to the Northern Tanganyika Bible School established by the Assemblies of God USA in Arusha, Tanzania in the 1960s, which relocated to Kenya between 1975 and 1976 before growing into the present university, with the Kitengela campus admitting its first students in January 2015. The university operates a main campus at Kitengela in Kajiado County and a campus at Buruburu in Nairobi, and publishes front-desk contacts at frontdesk@east.ac.ke alongside admissions@east.ac.ke and ictsupport@east.ac.ke. Programmes span certificate, diploma, undergraduate degree and master's levels in theology, education, business, counselling psychology, community development and criminology, with TVETA-accredited certificate and diploma courses also offered, and it admits government-sponsored students through KUCCPS. The university runs a live Moodle e-learning platform at https://elearning.east.ac.ke/ (KAGEU ONLINE) and a student portal at https://portal.east.ac.ke/.

context.description: Kenya Forestry College is a public forestry training institution at Londiani in Kericho County, operating within the Kenya Forest Service and legally established under section 17 of the Forest Conservation and Management Act (FCMA) of 2016. The Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority licenses it as TVETA/PUBLIC/TVC/0014/2018, first registered on 12 April 2018 with a licence expiring on 2 July 2029 and a status of Registered and Licensed. The college's own website gives its contact address as P.O. Box 30 - 20203, Londiani, Kericho County, and lists a programme portfolio of diplomas in forestry, environmental management and wood science and technology alongside certificates in forestry and in wood science and technology, with the TVETA register also recording a Level 4 plumbing qualification. Its history pages trace the institution's origins to the 1950s, with formal establishment by the Kenya Government in 1974 to train forestry personnel for the Forest Department, now the Kenya Forest Service. Facilities include a computer laboratory with 40 workstations, hostels for up to 256 students, a library, a guest house and conference centre, an industrial sawmill for wood processing training, and the 4,152-hectare Masaita Forest Block used as a field training ground.

context.description: The Commission for University Education register of 15 September 2026 lists the university as Kenya Highlands Evangelical University, a Private Chartered University chartered in 2011, and the CUE accredited programme register of 31 July 2026 records nine awards under that registered name. All nine accredited awards are recorded here, spanning pastoral theology, Christian education, business management, education, computer science, information technology, records management and nursing, with the newest approvals dated 2023, 2024 and 2026. The institution trades with a shorter name in its own materials: its e-learning portal at https://elearning.khu.ac.ke identifies the operator as 'Kenya Highlands University (formerly Kenya Highlands Evangelical University)', so the registered CUE name and the current trading name are recorded side by side and the database name is left unchanged. General enquiries are published as info@khu.ac.ke and +254 716 477 588 on the khu.ac.ke domain, which also hosts the university's logo asset. The university runs a live Moodle e-learning portal at https://elearning.khu.ac.ke that posts ODeL tutorials and announcements, and it states on that portal that it belongs to the Africa Gospel Church. No student enrolment figure, campus list or named officer contact is published on the pages checked, so those fields remain null.

context.description: Kenya Industrial Training Institute is a public Technical and Vocational College registered in Nakuru County, Kenya, under TVETA registration number TVETA/PUBLIC/TVC/0006/2017, where the regulator prints the registered name as KENYA INDUSTRIAL TRAINING INSTITUTE - NAKURU. The TVETA register records the institute as registered on 19 June 2017 with a licence valid to 13 February 2029 and the status Registered and Licensed. Its accredited provision combines seventeen KNEC diploma programmes in architecture, automotive and mechanical engineering, building technology, construction plant, electrical and electronics engineering, food technology, fashion design, business, ICT and sales and marketing with KNEC craft awards in business management, human resource management, masonry, sales and marketing and an artisan food and beverage course. Nine NITA trade tests are also accredited, covering hairdressing, leather products, motor vehicle mechanics and electrician work, panel beating and spray painting, tailoring, dressmaking, beauty therapy and welding and fabrication, and the register additionally lists the KASNEB Certified Public Accountants professional qualification, which falls outside the qualification levels used in this schema and is not recorded as a course entry. The institute's own site at kiti.ac.ke, fetched on 26 October 2026, prints info@kiti.ac.ke in its contact information block with the Solai Road and P.O. Box 280-20100 Nakuru address, and that published address is recorded as the institutional e-mail.

context.description: KITI Nakuru is a public TVET institution on Solai Road in Nakuru, registered by the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority as TVETA/PUBLIC/TVC/0006/2017, registered on 19 June 2017 with a licence that runs to 13 February 2029 and a status of Registered and Licensed. The institute's own website publishes its programmes in competency-based education and training terms, listing nine certificate courses at CBET Level 5 and eight diploma courses at CBET Level 6 across electrical and electronics, mechanical, automotive, building and construction, leather and tannery, food and beverage, ICT and fashion and design departments. The regulator's course table for the same registration number publishes thirty-one further award rows examined by the Kenya National Examinations Council and the National Industrial Training Authority, covering artisan, craft, diploma and trade-test qualifications in engineering, business, hospitality and garment trades, and these are recorded alongside the institute's own list rather than replaced by it. Levels were normalised as follows: the register's craft awards are recorded as Certificate, its trade-test awards as Artisan, and the institute's CBET Level 5 certificate and CBET Level 6 diploma courses as published. The register also carries one professional award, the KASNEB Certified Public Accountants qualification, which has no equivalent in the schema's academic level vocabulary and is therefore described here rather than recorded as a course. The institute publishes General Enquiry as info@kiti.ac.ke and lists the lines +254 51 2216755, +254 51 2216291 and +254 774944615 with the postal address P.O. Box 280-20100, Nakuru; no named officer, student population or logo asset could be confirmed, so those fields are left null.

context.description: Kenya Institute of Development Studies (KIDS) is a private middle-level training institution registered and licensed by the TVET Authority under TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0097/2017, with a registration date of 19 June 2017 and a licence valid until 8 October 2028. The register places it in Nakuru County with a status of Registered and Licensed, and lists a commerce-focused accreditation table covering the KASNEB Accounting Technicians Diploma and Certified Public Accountants awards alongside KNEC craft and diploma programmes in Business Management and Information Communication Technology. Directory listings describe it as founded to close a training gap for learners who could not pursue or further their studies at university, imparting practical knowledge and skills for economic and social growth, with January, April and August intakes and a minimum entry of grade D for certificates and C- (or a related certificate) for diplomas. Its Naivasha campus is listed on Moi Southlake Road in the Oserian Estates, while a Nairobi presence is listed at Tumaini House, 6th Floor, Moi Avenue, and a Google Places record at 1st Optimum House, Naivasha confirms the phone contact +254 718 200222. The institution's own domain, kidstudies.ac.ke, is cited in listings but returned HTTP 500 on both http and https at the time of research, so no live website, e-learning or distance-learning portal could be verified.

name: Kenya Institute of Highways and Building Technology

context.about: The Kenya Institute of Highways and Building Technology is a public technical and vocational college in Nairobi County, Kenya, registered and licensed by the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority under registration number TVETA/PUBLIC/TVC/0014/2024. It specialises in highways, building and civil engineering technology, offering KNEC diploma programmes in architecture, building, civil, electrical, mechanical, quantity surveying, land surveying and ICT alongside NITA trade-test artisan trades.
context.description: The Kenya Institute of Highways and Building Technology appears in the TVET Authority register as a public Technical and Vocational College in Nairobi County under registration number TVETA/PUBLIC/TVC/0014/2024, registered on 15 May 2024 with a licence valid to 14 May 2029 and recorded as Registered and Licensed. The register publishes eleven accredited programme rows for the institute: nine KNEC diploma programmes in architecture, building technology, civil engineering, electrical and electronics engineering (power), mechanical engineering, mechanical engineering (plant), quantity surveying, land surveying and information communication technology, plus two NITA trade-test artisan trades in masonry and plumbing and pipe fitting. The institute's portfolio is concentrated in highways, building and civil engineering disciplines rather than general arts or business programmes. Register levels were normalised to the canonical vocabulary, with the NITA trade-test awards rendered as artisan level and the KNEC diploma rows left as diplomas. The institute's own contact page publishes the headquarters at Commercial Street, Industrial Area - Nairobi, with telephone lines 0202465760 and 0202465761 and the mailbox principal@kihbt.go.ke, and it also names KIHBT Ngong and KIHBT Kisii as further locations.

context.description: The Eldoret branch of the Kenya Institute of Management is registered with the TVET Authority as KENYA INSTITUTE OF MANAGEMENT - ELDORET under registration number TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0257/2016, registered on 19 September 2016 and licensed to 26 November 2029. The regulator's course table for the branch lists three KASNEB programmes: the Accounting Technicians Diploma, plus the Certified Public Accountants and Certified Secretaries professional awards, the two professional awards being recorded here under the nearest available schema level because the canonical level list carries no separate professional-qualification category. The institute's own website publishes seven 24-month KIM diplomas, listed here, which are institution-assessed rather than examined by KASNEB, and advertises certificate (KNQA levels 4 and 5), diploma and professional certification categories. The branch occupies the third floor of The KIM Plaza on Elgeyo Road in Eldoret, opposite Sirkwa Hotel, with branch phone 0712200805 and email eldoret@kim.ac.ke. The institute dates itself to 1954 and publishes a branch network of 13 to 14 offices plus an Online Branch for virtual classes.

context.description: Established in 1954, initially as the East African Management Forum, the Kenya Institute of Management (KIM) has historically served as a significant catalyst in advancing management knowledge and practices within both the public and private sectors of the East African economy, particularly in Kenya. As one of only two private national management development institutes in Sub-Saharan Africa, KIM's vision has been rooted in the belief that effective management is crucial for Kenya's social and economic development, aiming to make substantial contributions to this field. The institution's mission has been to champion excellence, integrity, and competitiveness among individuals and organizations, providing management consultancy and capacity-building services. However, as of April 20, 2026, the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority (TVETA) revoked KIM's accreditation and ordered the closure of all its campuses, including Kitengela, declaring all certificates issued after 2018 invalid due to the institution offering unapproved courses and employing unlicensed trainers.

context.description: The Kenya Institute of Management runs its Nakuru operations as one of the institute's regional branches, listed on KIM's own contacts page at Ereto Plaza, sixth floor, opposite Gatehouse along Mburu Gichua Road in Nakuru, with the branch telephone line 0712 200916 and the branch email address nakuru@kim.ac.ke. description: Kenya Institute of Project Management (KIPM) is a private training institute in Nairobi County, Kenya, registered and licensed by the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority under registration number TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0234/2025, granted on 6 November 2025 and running to 5 November 2030. The institute presents itself as a project management training and consultancy centre and states on its website that it is certified and accredited by NITA and TVETA. Its Diploma in Project Management is an eight-month programme examined by the KIPM Examination Board, taught through Saturday sessions, a distance-learning mode with monthly Saturday meetings, and an e-learning mode with online consultation and examination. KIPM's Learning Management System runs at https://portal.kipm.ac.ke/login, and the institute publishes the telephone number +254 727 595 550 and the email address Kipmtraining@gmail.com. No street address is printed on the pages examined in this pass; the location fields record the county the regulator assigns and the city, and the street address remains unverified.

Its own website states that the institute was initiated in 1997, incorporated on 22 June 2000 and registered by the Ministry of Education, Science and Technology on 22 August 2002 as a training institution without governmental, religious or political affiliation. context.description:
With over 13 years of experience in the technical education sector, the Kenya Institute of Software Engineering and Professional Studies (KISE) is a key player in Kenya's digital economy. The institution was founded to bridge the critical shortage of high-level coding and software development talent in the region, focusing on competency-based training.

KISE's mission is to provide quality-driven professional training that fosters applied research, innovation, and community outreach. The institute is particularly noted for its specialized labs in full-stack development, mobile engineering, and fiber optics, partnering with international bodies to provide certifications that are globally recognized and industry-relevant.

context.description: Kenya Institute of Special Education (KISE) is a public institution established in 1986 through Legal Notice No. 17 of 14 February 1986, operating as a semi-autonomous government agency of the Ministry of Education. It is registered with the TVET Authority as TVETA/PUBLIC/TVC/0003/2025 (registered 29 January 2025, licensed to 28 January 2030) and is based in Kasarani, off Thika Superhighway Exit 8, Nairobi. KISE's statutory mandate covers teacher training in special needs education, in-service and correspondence courses, functional and educational assessment of children with special needs, operation of an orientation and mobility centre, a model training unit, a pre-school department, research, and production and repair of assistive devices. Alongside its special needs education role, the TVETA register lists eight CDACC and NITA awards spanning computer operations, baking technology, food and beverage operations, food production and ICT at artisan, certificate and diploma levels. The institute also runs an Assessment and Research Centre offering physiotherapy, occupational and speech therapy, ARC Hotel conference facilities, a library and a documentation and resource centre, and delivers distance-learning joining instructions with a live e-learning portal at elearning.kise.ac.ke.

context.description: KMTC Mombasa Campus is one of the campuses of the Kenya Medical Training College, a State Corporation established through an Act of Parliament under the Ministry of Health and mandated to train middle-level health professionals. The campus is situated on Mombasa Island at Tononoka, Mzizima, along Abdel Naser Road and next to the Coast General Teaching and Referral Hospital, which serves as its principal clinical training site. The KMTC Academic Programmes booklet (September 2025) lists Mombasa as a centre for the Higher Diploma in Clinical Pharmacy, the Higher Diploma in Kenya Registered Nurse Anaesthesia, and the Higher Diploma in Clinical Medicine and Surgery specialisations in anaesthesia, family health and reproductive health, alongside upgrading diplomas in Health Records and Information, Mortuary Science and Emergency Medical Technician. It also offers the Diploma in Community Health Nursing by distance learning for the March intake and hosts the one-year Health Care Assistant short course. In October 2025 the campus hosted a four-day CIRHT and ECSACOG Training of Trainers workshop on sexual and reproductive health with the Coast General Teaching and Referral Hospital, and the campus skills laboratory is being modernised under that partnership. Campus leadership put enrolment at about 2,500 learners in February 2026, when the Mvita Constituency MP committed further NG-CDF funding to complete the Mvita block and add a floor to ease space constraints.
accreditations: KMTC programmes are approved and accredited by the relevant regulatory and accreditation bodies (KMTC institutional statement).

KMTC higher diploma and upgrading programmes require prior registration or licensing with the relevant professional regulators, including the Nursing Council of Kenya, the Pharmacy and Poisons Board, the Kenya Medical Laboratory Technicians and Technologists Board and the Health Records and Information Management Board.
Kenya Medical Training College is ISO 9001:2015 certified, as indicated by the certification mark carried on the College official logo.

context.description: Kenya Medical Training College (KMTC) is a state corporation established through an Act of Parliament under the Ministry of Health, and the Nairobi campus is one of the college's 92 campuses spread across 46 counties. The official KMTC Campus Contacts list of February 2026 records the campus at P.O. Box 30195, Nairobi, with the campus mailbox nairobi@kmtc.ac.ke; the contact list prints the campus telephone string in a concatenated and unusable form, so no telephone number is asserted for this record. context.description: The Kenya Methodist University TVET Institute is the competence-based training arm of Kenya Methodist University, operating from the university's main campus at Kaaga off the Meru-Maua Highway in Meru County, Kenya. The Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority licensed it as a private Technical and Vocational College on 26 April 2021 under registration number TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0042/2021, and its status remains Registered and Licensed with an expiry date of 14 May 2031. Its own programme page lists 46 programmes organised into National Diploma Level 6, Craft Certificate Level 5, Artisan Certificate Level 4 and professional short-course bands, covering business, accountancy, ICT, health records, community health, agriculture, hospitality, maritime logistics, security, sign language and peace and conflict studies, plus short courses such as ICDL, CISCO CCNA 1-4, foreign languages, music and KASNEB courses. Teaching is offered at the Meru Town Centre opposite the County Assembly, the Meru main campus, the Nairobi campus in the KeMU Hub Building on Monrovia Street, and the Mombasa campus at the former Oshwal Academy on Narok Road in Buxton, with intakes in January, May and September. The institute also records that its maritime programmes are approved by the Kenya Maritime Authority and that it publishes timetables, a student portal and a digital campus for online study.

context.description: Kenya School of Flying is a professional pilot training school whose main campus is situated at Wilson Airport in Nairobi, with other flight bases at Malindi, Orly Airpark and Ukunda airstrip. It operates a fleet of more than 10 training aircraft with ten full-time instructors and what the school describes as the first full-motion, twin-engine flight simulator in Africa. Its pilot pathway covers the Private Pilot License, a four-to-six-month course with 45 flying hours, and the Commercial Pilot License, an eight-to-twelve-month course with 155 flying hours, with KCAA ground exams, GFT bookings and licence application fees itemised on its course pages, alongside Multi Engine/Instrument Rating, Airline Transport Pilot License and Caravan Rating training. The institution also lists a BSc. in Aviation Management (For Pilots), an Aeronautical Engineering Programme and a Holiday Programme for high school students that hosts about 250 participants a year at Orly Airpark. On the TVETA register it appears as a private Technical and Vocational College, number TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0166/2024, registered on 29 October 2024 and licensed until 28 October 2029, with a programme table of Airport Operations, Airport Operations and Flight Dispatch and Dangerous Goods Regulation assessed by IATA, Aeronautical Engineering examined by KNEC, and Level 6 aeronautical engineering options in airframes and power plant and in avionics assessed by TVET CDACC. Contact is via studentcoordinator@flyingschool.co.ke and +254 (0) 722 754 580 / (0) 733 777 582.

conflict.proposed_value: Kenya School of Flying is a professional pilot training school whose main campus is situated at Wilson Airport in Nairobi, with other flight bases at Malindi, Orly Airpark and Ukunda airstrip. Its pilot pathway covers the Private Pilot License, a four-to-six-month course with 45 flying hours, and the Commercial Pilot License, an eight-to-twelve-month course with 155 flying hours, with KCAA ground exams, GFT bookings and licence application fees itemised on its course pages, alongside Multi Engine/Instrument Rating, Airline Transport Pilot License and Caravan Rating training. The institution also lists a BSc. in Aviation Management (For Pilots), an Aeronautical Engineering Programme and a Holiday Programme for high school students that hosts about 250 participants a year at Orly Airpark. context.description: Kenya School of Medical Science and Technology (KSMST) is a private medical and technical training college operating in Thika town, Kiambu County. The college is registered and licensed by TVETA (TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0045/2018) and states on its website that it is recognised by health-sector regulators including the Pharmacy and Poisons Board and the Medical Laboratory Board. It runs two campuses: the Main Campus on Upper Road in the Majengo area next to Kenya Tanning, and the Town Campus on the 5th floor of Thika Arcade. Its prospectus spans medical and health sciences such as perioperative theatre technology, orthopaedic trauma and medicine, nutrition and dietetics, community health and health services support, alongside applied sciences, hospitality and tourism, fashion and beauty, ICT and business programmes. The college also delivers international qualifications through ABMA (UK), City and Guilds (UK) and Cambridge International College (UK), and its fee accounts are held in the name of Central Memorial Hospital, reflecting its close association with that Thika facility.

context.description: The Kenya School of Revenue Administration - Mombasa is a public TVET institution operating in Mombasa County, Kenya, and is the coastal campus of the Kenya School of Revenue Administration, the national tax and customs training school. The Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority lists this campus in the accredited-institution register as TVETA/PUBLIC/TVC/0016/2016, a public Technical and Vocational College whose licence runs to 24 March 2027 with the status Registered and Licensed. The regulator's published course table records two diploma awards for the campus, the Accounting Technicians Diploma examined by the Kenya National Accountants and Secretaries Examinations Board and a diploma in maritime transport logistics examined by the Kenya National Examinations Council. The register publishes no street address, telephone line or institutional email address for the campus, and the domain carried on the database record belongs to the parent school rather than to this campus. The parent school's site, whose archived copy was read on 26 October 2026, prints kesra@kra.go.ke in its contact footer at Times Tower, and that published address is recorded for this campus. No e-learning or distance-learning provision is recorded for the campus.

context.about: The Kenya School of TVET (KSTVET), formerly the Kenya Technical Trainers College, is Kenya's national institution for training technical and vocational education trainers; it is a public National Polytechnic registered by the TVET Authority and operates a main campus in Gigiri, Nairobi, and a Moiben campus in Uasin Gishu County.
facilities: Mechanical engineering workshops and lathe training bays
Training kitchen and KSTVET Hotel training facility
context.description: The TVET Authority register lists the institution as KENYA SCHOOL OF TVET under registration number TVETA/PUBLIC/NP/0006/2016, registered on 14 July 2016 with a licence valid to 28 March 2030, categorised as a public National Polytechnic in Nairobi County, and records two accredited CDACC Level 5 programmes in criminal justice management and security management. The school's own website presents it as KSTVET, formerly KTTC, established in 1978 to train technically skilled personnel to teach in technical institutions, with a mandate to train technical teachers for all technical training institutions in the country and to conduct examinations and grant academic awards as provided under its establishing Order. Its main campus is on UN Avenue in Gigiri, opposite Gigiri Box Park and adjacent to the UNEP headquarters off Limuru Road, and its Moiben campus in Uasin Gishu County, opened in May 2025 and separately registered by the TVET Authority as TVETA/PUBLIC/TVC/0001/2026, houses the agriculture and applied sciences departments. Teaching spans nine academic departments including computer studies, business, education, electrical engineering, health and applied sciences, hospitality and institutional management, liberal studies and open and distance learning, offering a Diploma in Technical Training and a Certificate in Instructor Training for in-service and pre-service trainers, plus a large continuous professional development portfolio covering CBET curriculum development, competency-based assessment, digitalisation of content, dual TVET implementation, greening TVET, recognition of prior learning and leadership for TVET managers. The school runs a Moodle-based e-learning platform at elearning.kstvet.ac.ke, an admissions and student portal on the mycampuscurra platform, a CPD portal and a research repository, and it hosts the National ODeL in TVET centre. Its published leadership is Dr. Edwin Tarno as Chief Executive Officer and Nicholas Marete as Chairperson of the Governing Council; neither is published with an individual email address or direct telephone line, so no personal contact record is given.

context.description: The Kenya YMCA College of Agriculture and Technology is a core project of the Kenya YMCA that began in 1968 as the Limuru Boys Centre and now stands on the Limuru-Banana road next to the Kentmere Club in Kiambu County. The college's own pages organise the offer as diploma, certificate, artisan and short-course programmes and describe a regenerative demonstration farm, dairy unit, automotive workshop and food processing laboratory. It also publishes a Distance Learning page in its programme menu.

context.description: The KNH School of Nursing states that it was established in 1996 and has specialised in training healthcare workers, receiving students from the East and Central Africa region. All of its specialised nursing courses are approved by the Nursing Council of Kenya, and approximately 250 students graduate from the school each year, with trainees placed in the hospital's specialised units. description: The KNH School of Nursing states that it was established in 1996 and has specialised in training healthcare workers, receiving students from the East and Central Africa region. All of its specialised nursing courses are approved by the Nursing Council of Kenya, and approximately 250 students graduate from the school each year, with trainees placed in the hospital's specialised units. It offers six two-year Higher Diploma specialised nursing courses (perioperative, critical care, neonatal, nephrology, trauma and emergency, and oncology nursing) plus short certificate courses including Stoma, Wound and Continence Care and Theatre and Sterile Services Assistant; applications are made online through nursing.knh.or.ke. TVETA registers the school as a public Technical and Vocational College in Nairobi County under registration number TVETA/PUBLIC/TVC/0030/2019, registered on 2019-06-07 with licence expiry 2030-05-06; the TVETA course table itself lists no courses.

context.description: Kenyatta University Kitui TVET Centre is the Kitui Campus centre through which Kenyatta University's Directorate of TVET Programmes delivers skills-based, industry-aligned vocational training in Kitui County. The centre is registered and licensed by TVETA under TVETA/PUBLIC/TVC/0018/2023, registered on 31 July 2023 with a licence valid to 30 July 2028, and holds 'Registered and Licensed' status on the TVETA register. The Directorate states that the Main, Kitui and Mombasa campuses are accredited as TVET centres by TVETA and that the centres offer competency-based education and training (CBET) curricula in TVETA-approved programmes. Seven TVETA-approved diplomas are offered at the Kitui centre — Accountancy, Business Management, Human Resource Management, Marketing, Procurement and Supply Chain Management, Information Science, and Records Management and Information Technology — all studied full time and examined internally by Kenyatta University. Programmes are delivered in alignment with the Kenya National Qualifications Framework (KNQF) and the TVET Act, 2013, with entry typically requiring a mean grade of C- at KCSE or a relevant Level 5 craft certificate.

context.description: Kericho Teachers' Training College started at Kabianga before it moved to its present site in 1965, mainly occupying buildings of the former colonial-era European Primary School located on the Kericho-Nakuru Highway near Kericho Town. It is one of the oldest public teachers' training colleges in the Republic of Kenya and a centre of excellence in primary teacher education, with a capacity to host over 1200 students. The college offers regular and school-based DPTE, DECTE, UPTE and UDECTE programmes to holders of a KCSE mean grade C (Plain) and above or a P1 Certificate, producing highly trained Competency Based Curriculum teachers. It has about 50 teaching and 67 non-teaching staff, operates under a Board of Management with performance contracts signed with the Ministry of Education, and runs income-generating projects such as farming and chicken rearing. Beyond academics it is a powerhouse in co-curricular activities including games, sports, athletics, drama and music.

context.description: Kericho Township Technical and Vocational College appears in the TVETA register of accredited TVET institutions under registration number TVETA/PUBLIC/TVC/0018/2019, registered on 22 October 2019 with a licence valid to 20 January 2030 and a status of Registered and Licensed. The regulator's programme table lists ten KNEC qualifications spanning artisan certificates in food and beverage and in hairdressing and beauty therapy, craft certificates in electrical and electronics technology (power), masonry and plumbing, and diplomas in baking technology, business management, electrical and electronics engineering (power), food and beverage production, sales and service management, and supply chain management. The TVETA register lists this registration number under Migori County, whereas the college's own name and website place it in Kericho County; the institutional evidence is used for the county field here and the regulator discrepancy is recorded rather than hidden.

context.description: Keroka Technical Training Institute is a public technical and vocational college in Kisii County, Nyanza, recorded in the TVETA register of accredited TVET institutions as TVETA/PUBLIC/TVC/0017/2016 with a licence valid to 15 January 2030 and the status 'Registered and Licensed'. Its register entry is the fullest in its group, spanning artisan, craft, diploma and competency-based levels across engineering, building, applied science, business and hospitality. KNEC examines seventeen diploma programmes including architecture, automotive engineering, business management, catering and accommodation management, electrical and electronics engineering, food science and processing technology, medical laboratory technology, land surveying and social work and community development, alongside seven craft certificate courses and two artisan courses in electrical installation and motor vehicle mechanics. KASNEB adds an accounting technicians diploma. TVET CDACC contributes level 3 to level 6 competency-based courses in masonry, fashion design technology, food and beverage service, food production, accommodation operations, welding, automotive technology, building technology, office administration, accountancy, electrical engineering, library and information management and social work. Where the register lists the same programme name at more than one level, the highest accredited level is recorded once so the course list stays unambiguous. context.description: Khwisero Technical and Vocational College appears in the TVET Authority register as a public technical and vocational college in Kakamega County under registration number TVETA/PUBLIC/TVC/0017/2023. The register records a registration date of 31 July 2023 and a licence expiry date of 30 July 2028, with the status 'Registered and Licensed' on the 25 October 2026 register snapshot. Box 68-50135 Khwisero; the record's town carries the Mushiangubu locality within Khwisero, consistent with that address. The register entry itself carries no institutional website, e-mail address or telephone number. The college publishes no student population figures or e-learning portal.

context.description: Kiambatha Vocational Training Center is a public Vocational Training Centre (VTC) situated at Kiamyaga along the Kiambatha-Kavote Road in Kirinyaga County, Kenya. context.about: Kiambu Institute of Science and Technology (KIST), now operating as the Kiambu National Polytechnic (KINAP), is a public technical and vocational institution under the Ministry of Education's State Department for TVET. It was founded in 1973 through Harambee effort with donations from ICCO of the Netherlands and EZE of Germany, and admitted its first 125 students, 75 male and 50 female. The campus sits on Kiambu Road about 14 kilometres from Nairobi and one kilometre from Kiambu Town, and trains at CBET Levels 3 to 6 across applied sciences, engineering, ICT, business and hospitality.

context.description: The institution is the Kiambu National Polytechnic (KINAP), formerly Kiambu Institute of Science and Technology, registered and licensed by the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority as a public National Polytechnic under registration number TVETA/PUBLIC/NP/0005/2024, registered on 18 January 2024 with a licence valid to 17 January 2029. The TVETA register of accredited programmes lists 69 qualifications spanning KASNEB accounting and ICDL Africa digital literacy awards, KNEC diploma, craft and artisan trades, and a CDACC Level 6 industrial plant operations programme, while the institution's own catalogue advertises CBET Level 6, Level 5, Level 4 and Level 3 programmes with internal, CDACC and KNEC assessment. Training is competency-based, with substantial modular and dual-training delivery, and the polytechnic holds ISO 9001:2015 certification. Governance rests with a Board of Governors appointed by the Ministry of Education in consultation with stakeholders, which oversees day-to-day running of the institute. The polytechnic operates a student and staff portal at https://portal.kiambupoly.ac.ke, an admissions portal at https://admissions.kiambupoly.ac.ke, a live Moodle-based e-learning platform at https://elearning.kiambupoly.ac.ke, and dedicated complaints and guidance-and-counselling portals. Leadership changed in October 2026 when Lucy Mukiri Anampiu took over as Chief Principal from CPA Sammy K. Waititu, who retired after more than six years; the institution's principal page still carries an image whose alt text names the outgoing holder. The website advertises a January 2027 intake, and its animated counters for lecturers, courses, classrooms and students render as zero placeholders, so no enrolment figure is asserted here.

context.description: The Directorate of TVET at Kibabii University is presented on the university's own site as the unit that equips learners with practical skills, innovation capacity and entrepreneurial competence for the modern workforce through competency-based training, industry partnerships and hands-on learning. Its stated priorities span competency-based training and curriculum development aligned with national TVET standards and industry needs, investment in modern workshops and equipment, quality assurance and accreditation compliance with national regulatory bodies such as TVETA and KNEC, and the promotion of skills development, innovation and entrepreneurship. Through its programme page the directorate publishes 22 diploma programmes and one certificate programme covering computer programming, computer science, cyber security, data management and analysis, electronics, fingerprints and biometrics, ICT technician work, library and information science, network and system administration, applied biology, environmental management, aquaculture and a range of business and management disciplines. The directorate is led by Director (TVET) Prof. Makokha John Wanjala with a TVET coordinator and administrative staff, while Kibabii University as a whole operates a Moodle-based e-learning portal, a student portal and a dedicated Open, Distance and e-Learning directorate. The unit's TVETA registration as a public TVC (TVETA/PUBLIC/TVC/0035/2021) is recorded on the regulator's register with the licence shown as expired on 2026-07-20.
