context.description: Kibabii Vocational Training Institute appears in the TVET Authority register as a public Vocational Training Centre in Bungoma County under registration number TVETA/PUBLIC/VTC/0101/2016. The register records a registration date of 14 July 2016 and a licence expiry date of 28 August 2029, with the status 'Registered and Licensed' on the 25 October 2026 register snapshot, and publishes seven accredited programmes: Food and Beverage Production and Service at craft level examined by KNEC, plus artisan trade-test courses in carpentry and joinery, masonry, motor vehicle mechanics, tailoring, welding and fabrication, and dressmaking, all assessed by the National Industrial Training Authority. The centre maintains its own website at kibabiivtc.ac.ke, which identifies it as a Bungoma County government vocational training centre whose courses are examinable by national bodies including CDACC and NITA, and publishes the contact details P.O. Box 2613-50200 Bungoma, telephone 0704820056 and e-mail info@kibabiivtc.ac.ke. The website additionally advertises departments in motor vehicle mechanics, food processing technology, fashion design, welding and fabrication, beauty therapy, electrical engineering, ICT and computer studies, and building technology, with intakes in January, May and September. No student population, e-learning portal or distance-learning provision is published on any fetched source.

context.description: Kibra Technical and Vocational College is a public Technical and Vocational College in Nairobi County, registered by the TVET Authority under TVETA/PUBLIC/TVC/0021/2024 on 1 August 2024, with the registration running to 31 July 2029. Its own website, kibratvc.ac.ke, presents it as a premier institution for quality technical and vocational education in Nairobi and organises teaching into eight academic departments: computing and informatics, building and civil engineering, cosmetology, fashion and garment making, electrical and electronics, hospitality and tourism, mechanical and automotive engineering, and business and liberal studies. The TVETA register lists 25 course rows that de-duplicate to 23 CDACC-examined programmes spanning Level 4 to Level 6, including business management, fashion design, information communication technology, supply chain management, tour and travel, cosmetology, electrical engineering and installation, food and beverage, masonry, plumbing and social work. Alongside these, the college runs short NITA trade-test courses in areas such as hair dressing, beauty therapy, arc welding, electrical wiring, plumbing and pipe fitting, masonry, painting, and baking and pastry, and states that admissions are ongoing for Artisan, Certificate and Diploma programmes. The campus on Kibera Drive hosts Jitume digital-skills training and emphasises hands-on practical sessions, with partnerships displayed on its site including NITA, KUCCPS, HELB, KATTI, the Ministry of Education and the TVET Authority.

context.description: Kighombo Vocational Training Center is a public Vocational Training Centre (VTC) registered and licensed by the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority (TVETA) on 12 January 2018 under registration number TVETA/PUBLIC/VTC/0066/2018, with the register recording the licence as valid to 8 October 2028. The TVETA register places the centre in Taita Taveta County in the Coast region, and directory profiles describe it as a public youth polytechnic located off the Nairobi - Mombasa Highway in the Voi area, with a postal address of P.O. Box 304 - 80300 Voi. Training is examined by the National Industrial Training Authority (NITA), with the register listing four trade-test programmes: Carpentry and Joinery, Electrical Wireman, Tailoring, and Dressmaking. Directory listings report class capacities of up to 25 trainees each for the carpentry and electrical wireman trades and up to 30 for tailoring and dressmaking. No institutional website, official email or institution-run social media page could be confirmed; the only published contact is a mobile number listed for the manager in the education.co.ke directory, and a Google Maps listing records the centre as operational but gives no phone or website and places its pin near Kibwezi, conflicting with the register's Taita Taveta location.

context.description: Kigumo Technical and Vocational College is recorded in the TVETA register of accredited institutions as a public Technical and Vocational College in Murang'a County under registration number TVETA/PUBLIC/TVC/0026/2022, registered on 31 October 2022 with a licence valid to 30 October 2027 and the status Registered and Licensed. The regulator's course table lists six qualifications examined by the Kenya National Examinations Council: diploma programmes in banking and finance, human resource management, sales and marketing and supply chain management, plus artisan-level electrical installation and plumbing. No verified named officer was published on the fetched pages, so the personal contacts list is empty.

about: Kiharu Technical College Murang'a (KTCM) is a public Technical and Vocational College in Kiharu, Murang'a County, Kenya, registered by the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority as TVETA/PUBLIC/TVC/0029/2023 on 9 October 2023, with the registration valid to 8 October 2028. The college delivers competence-based technical training across ten schools, including building and civil engineering, electrical engineering, computing, automotive engineering, hospitality, business, cosmetology, journalism, and medical and applied sciences, with programmes examined by KNEC, TVETA-accredited CDACC and NITA.
description: Kiharu Technical College Murang'a is a public Technical and Vocational College operating from Kiharu in Murang'a County, Kenya. The Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority registered it under TVETA/PUBLIC/TVC/0029/2023 on 9 October 2023 with the licence running to 8 October 2028. Its academic offer is organised into ten schools covering building and civil engineering, electrical and electronic engineering, computing and informatics, automotive engineering, medical and applied sciences, business and economics, hospitality and institutional management, cosmetology, fashion and design, and journalism and media studies. The college publishes 84 programme cards on its own courses page, spanning diploma, certificate and artisan awards examined by KNEC, CDACC and NITA, with a separate KASNEB accounting technician diploma; professional CPA study is advertised at foundational level but does not map to a canonical award. Its website carries a student portal, an online application portal, a staff ERP and 'E-Learning' and 'E-Revision' menu items, but both of those items currently point to page anchors rather than a delivered learning platform.

context.description: Kiirua Technical Training Institute is a public TVET institution under the Ministry of Education, registered by TVETA as TVETA/PUBLIC/TVC/0031/2016 on 14 April 2016 with a licence valid to 24 April 2029 and status Registered and Licensed. Its own website places it in Naari location, Buuri East Sub County, Meru County, and states a motto of Technology For Better Life together with a mission to offer technical and vocational education and training and undertake research that produces skilled, innovative and market-relevant human resources. The TVETA register lists twenty-four course rows spanning artisan, craft and diploma levels examined by KNEC and NITA trade tests in hairdressing and beauty therapy; where a subject appears at several levels, the highest registered level is recorded once, giving eighteen distinct qualifications. The institute's site advertises a January 2027 intake and recognition of prior learning, but publishes no telephone number or email address in the fetched pages, so those fields are left empty.

context.description: Medical training in Kijabe dates back to 1915 with the founding of the mission hospital, and the training school evolved into Kijabe College of Health Sciences, now a significant teaching centre integrated with AIC Kijabe Hospital. The college's mission is to provide top-level medical training grounded in Christian values and professional excellence, under the motto 'Health Care Training to God's Glory'. Its live website advertises three schools — Nursing, Clinical Medicine & Surgery, and Allied Health — offering diploma and higher-diploma programmes examined by the Nursing Council, the Clinical Officers Council (COC) and TVETA, alongside a newer Diploma in Biomedical Engineering Technology admitting from October 2026. The site reports a 98% pass rate and states that students learn from experienced professionals at AIC Kijabe Hospital, where theory meets practice in real clinical settings. E-learning runs on the in-house KCHS Digital Campus Moodle portal at elearning.kchs.ac.ke, backed by a digital library of thousands of e-books and journals.

about: Kijabe College of Health Sciences (KCHS) is a private mission-driven medical college on the grounds of AIC Kijabe Hospital in Kijabe, Kiambu County, whose training lineage in Kijabe dates to 1915. It is a TVETA-licensed college (TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0057/2018) preparing nurses, clinical officers and allied-health professionals for Nursing Council, Clinical Officers Council and KMLTTB examinations, with diploma, higher-diploma, certificate and higher-national-diploma programmes (KRCHN, KRCCN, KRNA, KRPON, POTT, BMET, paediatric occupational therapy) and March and September intakes.
description: Medical training in Kijabe dates back to 1915 with a mission hospital, and the training school evolved into Kijabe College of Health Sciences, now a significant teaching and referral centre in East Africa; its mission is to provide top-level medical training grounded in Christian values and professional excellence, in close integration with AIC Kijabe Hospital, which provides students unparalleled clinical exposure across medical specialties. The college's own website (fetched on the live domain) advertises the Schools of Nursing, Clinical Medicine & Surgery and Allied Health: the School of Nursing offers a Diploma in Kenya Registered Community Health Nursing and Higher Diploma programmes in Kenya Registered Critical Care Nursing, Kenya Registered Nurse Anaesthesia and Perioperative Nursing (advertised as a Higher National Diploma); the School of Clinical Medicine & Surgery offers a Diploma in Kenya Registered Clinical Medicine and Surgery plus Higher Diploma programmes in Emergency and Critical Care, Family Health and Paediatric Emergency and Critical Care for Clinical Officers; the School of Allied Health offers a Certificate and Post-Basic Diploma in Peri-Operative Theatre Technology and a Higher Diploma in Paediatric Occupational Therapy. A Nursing Colleges registry (yca.co.ke) lists AIC Kijabe College of Health Sciences as an approved Kiambu nursing training institution with pre-service KRCHN and in-service KRCCN, KRNA and KRPON full-time programmes (that source identifies the county as Kiambu). The live site is now admitting students to a POTT-D Diploma in Perioperative Theatre Technology (September intake) and a BMET Diploma in Biomedical Engineering Technology (October 2026 intake), and 98% pass rate and 10+ programmes are claimed on the home page. Contact details fetched from the live kchs.ac.ke homepage and contact page are: phone +254 789 338 062 (tel/WhatsApp) with a second line +254 709 728 251, email kchs@kijabehospital.org, postal address P.O. Box 20-00220, Kijabe, Kenya; a stored line 0712504056 and stored address cad@kijabehospital.org could not be found on the live pages fetched this run and are retained as recorded on the database. The college site links a student portal at https://students.kchs.ac.ke/, a digital library at library.kchs.ac.ke and a 'KCHS Digital Campus' e-learning platform at http://elearning.kchs.ac.ke:8010 (college subdomain). The college is registered and licensed by TVETA as a private TVC under TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0057/2018 in Kiambu County (licence to 2029-03-02). No student population estimate, distance-learning programme or named officer with direct contact route could be verified, so no personal contact is recorded.

context.description: Kiminini Technical and Vocational College is a public Technical and Vocational College registered by the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority under number TVETA/PUBLIC/TVC/0031/2019, with a licence valid to 16 January 2030 and the register status 'Registered and Licensed'. The register places it in Trans Nzoia County under public ownership; a separate entry, Kiminini Vocational Training Center, is a different institution with its own registration number. The TVETA course table for the college carries forty-one qualifications across three award families. Nineteen are Kenya National Examinations Council awards, made up of five artisan trade programmes, seven craft programmes and seven diplomas in automotive engineering, building technology, electrical and electronics engineering, fashion design and clothing technology, human resource management, information communication technology and supply chain management. The remaining twenty-two are TVET Curriculum Development, Assessment and Certification Council competence-based awards: six at Level 4, nine at Level 5 and seven at Level 6. The college's own contact page publishes its location as Konoin Village in Kiminini Sub-county, Trans Nzoia County, with a postal address of P.O. Box 542-30200 Kitale, the telephone lines 0759 424 048 and 0780 510 878, and the mailbox info@kimininitechnical.ac.ke; the homepage adds that the campus sits on five acres of land at Konoin Village donated for the college and opened for training on 9 September 2019.

Its stated vision is to be the leading tertiary institution in competency-based education and training, with a mission to provide holistic and demand-driven technical and vocational training. description: The Commission for University Education register of 15 September 2026 lists the institution as Kiriri Women's University of Science and Technology under Private Chartered Universities with a 2022 charter year, and the CUE accredited programme register of 31 July 2026 records twelve awards under that name. All twelve accredited awards are recorded here: ten bachelor's degrees in business, computer science, information technology, mathematics, economics and finance, hospitality, procurement, education and community development, plus a Master of Business Administration and a Master of Science in Applied Statistics and Data Analytics. The database stores the name without the apostrophe ('Kiriri Womens University of Science and Technology'); the registered CUE name is retained in this record and the stored name is left unchanged. No student enrolment figure, campus list or named officer contact is published on the pages checked, so those fields remain null.

context.description: Kisasa Technical Training Institute is a private technical training institute in Nakuru County registered and licensed by the TVET Authority under number TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0030/2023. Its accredited course table lists seven artisan trade-test rows, which de-duplicate to six distinct awards examined by the National Industrial Training Authority: electrical wireman, hairdressing, motor vehicle mechanics, panel beating and spray painting, plumbing and pipe fitting, and beauty therapy. The institute's own website presents automotive engineering, electrical engineering and plumbing as its headline courses and describes the institute as a centre of excellence in engineering training, reporting 1,505 alumni. The site publishes no postal address, email address or telephone number in the pages reviewed, and no e-learning portal or distance-learning provision is advertised.

context.description: Kisumu Institute of Community Development Training (KICDT) is a private Technical Vocational College focused on driving social change for community development. It was founded in 2014 (Certificate of Incorporation No. CPR/2014/168223) and registered as a private Technical Vocational College under the TVET Act, 2013 Section 20(1), registration number TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0259/2016, with TVETA recording a licence valid to 26 July 2027 and status 'Registered and Licensed'. The main campus sits at Rabuor Centre along the busy Nairobi-Kisumu Road approximately 10km from Kisumu city centre, opposite Otieno Oyoo High School and next to Rabuor Health Centre, with a satellite college being established at Nyanchwa in Kisii County. KICDT offers Artisan, Certificate and Diploma courses examined by NITA, KNEC and TVET CDACC across electrical, mechanical, building and civil engineering, computing and IT, business studies, social sciences, agriculture, tourism and hospitality, beauty and fashion trades. The college states it has adopted competency-based training under an ISO 9001-based quality management system and describes a Technology-Enabled Learning strategy that extends study flexibility to learners in remote areas.

context.description: Kisumu Maritime Centre (KIMARCE) is a private technical and vocational college registered with the TVET Authority under number TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0123/2016, recorded on the register as Registered and Licensed since 14 April 2016. It was founded by Vitalis Leo, a former MV Uhuru chief engineer and retired Lake Victoria captain, and trains seafarers, fishers and boat crews from two Kisumu campuses: the main campus at Korando Peninsular, off New Airport–Busia Road, and branch training grounds at Rainbow Junction to Ngege Beach, where trainees practise on the water. KIMARCE is approved by the Kenya Maritime Authority to offer maritime education and training for local and international labour markets and is certified by the Ministry of Education, with programmes built to the STCW Convention. It runs nine KMA-approved programmes, including Coxswain III, STCW Basic Safety Training, navigational and engineering watch-rating courses and short STCW certification courses, alongside KNEC artisan awards in seafarers and coxswain. Theory is delivered partly online through the institution's learning platform, and KIMARCE collaborates with Bandari Maritime Academy, Kenya Coast National Polytechnic, Kenya Utalii College, MSC Training Academy Naples and the KEMFSED programme.

context.description: Kituro Vocational Training Center is a public vocational training centre located along the Marigat-Kabarnet Road in the Kabarnet area of Baringo County, within Kenya's Rift Valley region. It is registered and licensed by the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority (TVETA) under registration number TVETA/PUBLIC/VTC/0034/2016, with registration dated 14 April 2016, and operates under the Baringo County Government, which has invested heavily in vocational training across the county through new and rehabilitated VTCs, modern tools and equipment, and bursaries covering a share of tuition for county trainees. The centre offers NVCET certificate courses examined by KNEC and artisan trade-test courses examined by NITA across trades including motor vehicle, building, electrical, carpentry and joinery, fashion design and garment making, hairdressing and beauty therapy, food processing, masonry and ICT. Public footage of the centre's second graduation ceremony posted by the Baringo County Government, and a 2024 graduation video in which the county Deputy Governor officiated the graduation of 110 students, indicate an enrolment of about 200 trainees.

context.description: Kitutu Masaba Technical and Vocational College was established as a public TVET institution under the Ministry of Education and admitted its first trainees in 2021. The college's mission is centered on the principle of 'help for self-help', seeing the needs of the time and acting accordingly to empower youth with marketable technical skills. context.description: KYEEDA operates from Lucky Summer Estate, Nairobi, and works with orphaned and vulnerable children and out-of-school youth in Korogocho, Baba Dogo, Mathare and Lucky Summer. Its Skills for Livelihoods stream equips vulnerable youth with practical, market-ready trades including tailoring and fashion design, ICT and digital skills, catering and food production, and salon and beauty services, with business training, apprenticeships and starter toolkits for graduates. The institute also runs an Education for Every Child program (school fees, uniforms, learning materials, mentoring and counselling) and a Nourish & Flourish food and nutrition program with daily school meals, take-home rations and caregiver nutrition education. In 2025 it partnered with the University of Nairobi Engineering and Economics Students Organization (UNEESO), which reported 80 youth trained in Fashion & Design with KYEEDA Technical Institute and supported placement of graduates into self-employment such as tailoring workshops. The website lists contact by phone +254 717 810019 and email info@kyeeda.org; no learning management system or distance-learning platform is offered on the site.

The register places it in Machakos County under public ownership, and Google Places records it as an operational centre at Kitanga with the phone number +254 724 265391. Its accredited course table carries seven qualifications: two Kenya National Examinations Council food and beverage awards, one at artisan level and one at craft level, and five National Industrial Training Authority trade tests in arc welding, masonry, motor vehicle mechanics, tailoring and dressmaking. A third-party listing adds local address details, giving a plot number of 355/25/64 at Kyemutheke with correspondence address P.O. Box 725-90100 Machakos, though it also shows an outdated 2023 expiry that the current register supersedes. In 2019 the centre was one of two Kenyan institutions, alongside Machakos Institute of Technology, where TME Education ambassador Kelvin Kangethe ran a four-day intensive electronics teacher-training workshop, evidencing external partner engagement in staff development.

name: Kyuso Vocational Training Centre

context.about: Kyuso Vocational Training Centre is a public vocational training centre in Kitui County, Kenya, registered and licensed by the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority as TVETA/PUBLIC/VTC/0072/2017. The TVETA register records a registration date of 13 July 2017 and a licence valid to 12 August 2030, listing NVCET programmes in electrical and metal processing technology plus NITA trade tests in welding, carpentry, electrical wiring, hairdressing, masonry, motor vehicle work, tailoring, dressmaking and beauty therapy.
context.description: Kyuso Vocational Training Centre is a public vocational training centre recorded by TVETA in Kitui County, Kenya, under registration number TVETA/PUBLIC/VTC/0072/2017. The regulator shows registration on 13 July 2017, a licence valid to 12 August 2030 and the status Registered and Licensed. Its accredited offer has two strands: KNEC National Vocational Certificates in Education and Training in electrical and electronics technology and in metal processing technology, and an extensive set of NITA artisan trade tests covering arc welding, carpentry and joinery, electrical wiring, hairdressing, masonry, motor vehicle mechanics, motor vehicle electricity, tailoring, dressmaking and beauty therapy. The register lists seventeen rows but several trade tests repeat across sittings; after de-duplication the payload holds twelve distinct awards. No institutional website, email address or telephone number was located for the centre, and the regulator publishes only the county, so the address and contact fields are left empty.

Its accredited offer has two strands: KNEC National Vocational Certificates in Education and Training in electrical and electronics technology and in metal processing technology, and an extensive set of NITA artisan trade tests covering arc welding, carpentry and joinery, electrical wiring, hairdressing, masonry, motor vehicle mechanics, motor vehicle electricity, tailoring, dressmaking and beauty therapy. The register lists seventeen rows but several trade tests repeat across sittings; after de-duplication the payload holds twelve distinct awards. No institutional website, email address or telephone number was located for the centre, and the regulator publishes only the county, so the address and contact fields are left empty.

context.description: Ladiva Beauty Training College is a private TVC in Kisumu County registered on the TVET Authority's live register under TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0237/2025 (registered 2025-11-06, licence expiring 2030-11-05), trading publicly as Ladiva Beauty College. Its own website presents a broad beauty curriculum: Cosmetology at Artisan, Certificate and Diploma level examined by TVET CDACC, plus Beauty Therapy, Hair Dressing and Nail Technology at Artisan, Certificate and Diploma levels examined by NITA, alongside one-month short courses and advanced classes in make up, facials, massage, barbering and microblading. The register's programme table lists two competency-based Cosmetology awards at Level 3 and Level 4 with TVET CDACC as the examining body, matching the site's Artisan and Certificate cosmetology bands. Training runs from a main campus on the Ground Floor of the Mayu Building, Kibos Road, Kondele (next to Nightingale Hospital) and a town campus at Diva Spa & Aesthetics on Ang'awa Street in the Kisumu CBD, where the sister Diva Spa provides a guaranteed free practical attachment. A live Moodle instance exists on the institution's elearning.ladivabeautycollege.co.ke subdomain, but it is branded and operated as Options English Test Training Centre (Options Education Agency, Eldoret, english@optionseducation.net), so the college's own e-learning provision is treated as implied rather than verified.

context.description: Laikipia East Technical and Vocational College is a public technical and vocational college registered by TVETA under number TVETA/PUBLIC/TVC/0037/2017 on 12 April 2017, licensed until 17 April 2030 in Registered and Licensed status. It was built by the Government of Kenya through the Ministry of Education in Laikipia County at an approximated cost of shillings 50 million and opened its doors to the first batch of students in September 2018. The college sits at Marina Trading Centre next to the Nyeri-Nyahururu Highway in Ngobit ward, Laikipia Central sub-county, and expects to enrol up to 2,000 students by 2027. The TVETA register lists thirteen awards examined by KNEC in building technology, electrical installation, business management, ICT, accountancy, civil engineering and tourism management at artisan, craft and diploma levels, while the college website advertises over 50 modular CBET programmes from Level 6 down to artisan and short skills courses, including catering and accommodation, mechanical and automotive engineering, fashion design and secretarial studies. The college positions itself as the Centre for Electrical and Electronics Engineering in the Mt Kenya region, and students can access Laikipia County bursaries, KUCCPS fee subsidy and HELB loans. It is led by Principal Naftaly Muriuki, whose signed message appears on the college website.

context.description: Laisamis Technical Training Institute is a public Technical and Vocational College registered under TVETA registration number TVETA/PUBLIC/TVC/0029/2017, with the register recording registration on 12 April 2017 and a licence valid to 25 March 2029. The institute is situated in Laisamis town, Marsabit County, along the Isiolo-Marsabit (A2) highway, about 165 km past Isiolo town and 92 km from Marsabit town, and its postal address is P.O. Box 30-60500, Marsabit. It started operations in May 2018 as one of the 60 technical institutions built by the Government of Kenya across the country and trains middle-level technical and vocational personnel in line with the national TVET mandate. Its accredited portfolio spans KNEC artisan, craft and diploma awards in agriculture, building technology, electrical and electronics engineering, ICT, human resource management, secretarial studies, social work and welding and fabrication, NITA trade tests in motor vehicle mechanics and welding, and TVET CDACC Level 4 to 6 competency-based programmes in agricultural extension, electrical installation and sustainable agriculture. The institute's website organises training through departments including Computing and Informatics, Business, Liberal Studies, Building and Civil Engineering, Health Sciences, Fashion Design and Cosmetology, Agriculture, Hospitality and Tourism, Electrical Engineering, and Mechanical and Automotive Engineering, and it identifies a strategic focus on animal health and production management plus a welding and fabrication centre of excellence.

Its accredited portfolio is broad for a county training institute, spanning KNEC artisan, craft and diploma awards in agriculture, building technology, electrical and electronics engineering, ICT, human resource management, secretarial studies, social work and welding and fabrication, NITA trade tests in motor vehicle mechanics and welding and fabrication, and CDACC competency-based awards in agriculture extension, electrical installation and sustainable agriculture for rural development. The institute's own domain, laisamistech.ac.ke, served a live site on 25 October 2026 publishing the email address info@laisamistech.ac.ke and the telephone line 0700 303 300. No e-learning or distance-learning portal was found on the site, and no street address could be confirmed, so the town and street fields are left unknown.

context.description: Limuru Technical and Vocational College is registered by the TVET Authority as TVETA/PUBLIC/TVC/0025/2021, a public Technical and Vocational College registered on 2021-04-26 with a licence valid to 2031-08-17, located in Kiambu County. The college's own website describes it as a public TVET college under the Ministry of Education's State Department for TVET, sited at Kamandura along the Nairobi-Nakuru Highway, and states that it trains at CBET levels 3 to 6 under a modularised curriculum with dual training and recognition of prior learning. The register carries forty-four award rows, de-duplicated here to forty distinct course-level-exam-body combinations, with duplication concentrated in the CDACC rows where Cosmetology at level 6 is listed twice. The portfolio spans mechanical and automotive engineering, electrical and electronic engineering, building and civil engineering, hospitality and tourism, fashion and cosmetology, computing, business studies and liberal studies. Level normalisation follows the pipeline convention: KNEC artisan rows, NVCET and CBET Level 3-4 rows are recorded as Artisan, KNEC Craft and CBET Level 5 rows as Certificate, and KNEC Diploma and CBET Level 6 rows as Diploma. Contact details, including telephone 0708 652 364 and limurutvc@gmail.com, are taken from the college's own homepage.

context.about: Lizaya Training Institute of Cosmetology and Hospitality is a private TVET institution in Nairobi's central business district offering vocational training in beauty therapy, hairdressing, fashion and garment technology and caregiving, including short professional courses examined under NITA and TVET CDACC arrangements.
context.description: The TVET Authority register lists this institution as Lizaya Training Institute of Cosmetology and Hospitality under registration number TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0018/2023, registered on 26 January 2023 with a licence valid to 25 January 2028 as a private Technical and Vocational College in Nairobi County. The institution's own website, lizaya.ac.ke, markets itself as Lizaya Training Institute, a vocational institute for beauty, fashion and caregiving, and publishes additional short courses including aromatherapy, hair colouring and bleaching, shiatsu and Thai massage, nail technology, deep tissue massage and manicure and pedicure, which it presents as NITA and TVETA certified. Its campus is on the second floor of Stanbank House on Moi Avenue in the Nairobi CBD, opposite Kencom and near the Kenya National Archives, and its contact page states that it is a NITA and TVETA certified institution. The TVET Authority register records six accredited programme entries in hairdressing and beauty therapy trade tests, cosmetology at Levels 3 and 4, fashion design technology at Level 4 and caregiving at Level 4, examined by NITA and TVET CDACC. The institute is led by founder and chief executive Elizabeth Kyambi, who is named on the contact page as the officer to approach for partnerships and projects.

context.about: Lodwar Technical and Vocational College is a TVETA-registered technical college in Lodwar, Turkana County, offering diploma, certificate and artisan programmes examined mainly by KNEC and CDACC, together with short courses.
context.description: Lodwar Technical and Vocational College is listed in the TVET Authority register as registration TVETA/PUBLIC/TVC/0019/2019, a public technical and vocational college in Turkana County registered on 2019-01-14 with a licence valid to 2029-05-24 and the status 'Registered and Licensed'. The college's own website states that it offers diploma, certificate and artisan courses examined mainly by KNEC and CDACC plus short courses, and describes itself as located off the Lodwar-Kitale highway behind Stegra Hotel. The regulator's institutional course table lists eight distinct awards: artisan Electrical Installation and Plumbing, craft certificates in Information Communication Technology, Land Surveying, Social Development and Supply Chain Management, and diplomas in Civil Engineering and Information Communication Technology. The college website organises teaching through departments covering agriculture and environmental studies, business and commerce, computer and informatics, building and civil engineering, hospitality and tourism, liberal studies, mechanical and automotive engineering, electrical and electronic engineering, health sciences, and fashion design and cosmetology. The website describes itself as a private tertiary institution while the TVETA register records the college as public; the regulator's ownership classification is treated as authoritative here. The college website also reports a student population of about 4,600 across its schools and departments, and names Mr Japheth M. Kiboi as Principal and Mr Samson Chenge as Deputy Principal; no individual email or telephone number is published for either officer, so they are not recorded as personal contacts.

context.description: Lokichar Vocational Training Center was registered by the TVET Authority on 19 June 2017 and its registration and licence run to 25 January 2028 (local TVETA corpus records.jsonl line 2540, TVETA/PUBLIC/VTC/0056/2017). The register classifies it as a public Vocational Training Centre located in Turkana County, with four published artisan-level trades: electrical wireman, hairdressing, motor vehicle mechanics and beauty therapy, all examined by NITA. Multiple independent non-register sources corroborate the centre: an Education News Kenya report (educationnews.co.ke) names Lokichar among Turkana County's eight public vocational training institutions; a USAID Nawiri / Mercy Corps post (facebook.com/MercyNawiri) documents vocational training in Lokichar, Turkana South, naming Esther Longori Ayepio as Manager of Lokichar Vocational Training Centre (LVTC); and vetted directories education.co.ke and wasomi.co.ke carry the exact identity and registration number TVETA/PUBLIC/VTC/0056/2017. Stored phone 0722 697965 is preserved, while education.co.ke also lists 0725 406553, email lokicharvct@gmail.com, and postal address P.O. Box 145-30500 Lodwar. No institutional website exists, so website remains null.

context.description: Luddoc Skills for Life Technical Institute is a private technical institute based in Kiambu County that trains care-sector workers. context.about: Lugala County Vocational Training Center is a public vocational training centre in Kakamega County registered by the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority under registration number TVETA/PUBLIC/VTC/0127/2016, with a licence recorded as registered and licensed and an expiry date of 29 September 2029. The centre's approved training portfolio is dominated by artisan-level trade qualifications examined by KNEC under the NVCET pathway and by NITA under the Trade Test pathway.
context.description: Lugala County Vocational Training Center appears in the TVETA register of accredited TVET institutions as a public VTC in Kakamega County, registered on 19 September 2016 under number TVETA/PUBLIC/VTC/0127/2016 and recorded as Registered and Licensed with an expiry date of 29 September 2029. The register's course table lists sixteen approved awards, and all sixteen sit at artisan level: ten are NVCET programmes examined by KNEC (appropriate carpentry and joinery, building technology, electrical and electronics technology, fashion design and garment making, food processing technology, hairdressing and beauty therapy, information communication technology, metal processing technology, motor vehicle technology, and refrigeration and air conditioning technology) and six are NITA Trade Test qualifications (carpentry and joinery, electrical wireman, hairdressing, motor vehicle mechanics, plumbing and pipe fitting, and beauty therapy). Level normalisation follows the convention used across this research programme: NVCET and Trade Test awards are recorded at the schema level Artisan rather than collapsed into Certificate, and the examining body is preserved as printed in the register (KNEC for NVCET, NITA for Trade Test). No institutional website, e-mail address or telephone number is published by the regulator for this centre, so those identity fields are left null rather than filled with a plausible-looking placeholder, and the centre's town and street address are recorded as unknown because no fetched source states them.

context.about: Mabati Technical Training Institute (MTTI) is a private technical and vocational college on the Mombasa Nairobi Highway at Mariakani, Kilifi County. A project of Safal MRM Foundation, the philanthropic arm of the Safal Group, it has operated since 2005 and is registered by TVETA under licence TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0150/2017, having equipped over 16,000 trainees with employable technical and vocational skills.

context.description: Mabati Technical Training Institute appears in the live TVETA register as a private technical and vocational college in Kilifi County, registered on 16 February 2017 under licence TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0150/2017 with a licence expiry of 30 October 2027 and a status of Registered and Licensed. The institute was established in 2005 in Mariakani, Kilifi County, as a flagship project of Safal MRM Foundation, the philanthropic arm of the Safal Group, arising from a funding arrangement between Mabati Rolling Mills and the European Investment Bank. Its registered portfolio covers artisan-level awards in electrical, mechanical, welding, plumbing, garment and beauty trades examined by NITA, a KNEC artisan award in Electrical Installation and a KNEC craft award in Information Communication Technology; register rows were de-duplicated by course, level and examination body before being recorded here, and the NITA trade-test row for Electrical Installation is retained alongside the KNEC artisan award. The institute positions itself as serving disadvantaged youth of the Coast region with affordable, subsidised technical and entrepreneurial skills training, and it links students to mentorship, financial literacy programmes and job placements through partner institutions. It maintains a Student Portal and Staff Portal under its foundation's domain, and its site publishes working hours, an online application channel and a bursary application facility.

context.description: Machakos Abled Differently Rehabilitation and Vocational Centre, known as MARC, is a private Vocational Training Centre registered with TVETA as TVETA/PRIVATE/VTC/0015/2021, registered on 26 April 2021 with the licence valid to 26 May 2031 and status 'Registered and Licensed'. The centre was established in January 2021 at Katoloni in Machakos County as a Christian technical institute founded on strong Christian principles in a homely, serene environment, serving young teenagers transiting to adulthood without skills for independent living. It currently enrols learners with mild intellectual challenges aged 12 to 18 years and tailors training through Individualized Education Programs covering life skills, interpersonal relationships and specific skill training at an individual pace. Its vocational programme comprises NITA trade-test qualifications in Hairdressing, Beauty Therapy and Tailoring, preceded by prevocational assessment and placement, and graduates are integrated into society through self-employment, linkage with supportive organisations or industry, or employment at MARC itself. The centre is led by administrator Caroline Mumbua, supported by trainer Susan Mwihaki, ECDE teacher Benson Bor, P1 teacher Benson Mutuku and volunteer trainer Teacher Mirriam.

description: Machakos Institute of Technology (MIT) is a private technical and vocational college registered by the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority on 17 November 2014 under registration number TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0008/2014, with a licence valid to 3 November 2026 in 'Registered and Licensed' status; renewal falls due within days of this research pass. The TVETA accredited course table lists 33 entries which deduplicate to 32 qualifications: a KASNEB Accounting Technicians Diploma, KNEC artisan, craft and diploma programmes across business administration, entrepreneurship, human resource management, sales and marketing, information studies, information communication technology, nutrition and dietetics, social work and community development, catering and accommodation, fashion design and tour guiding, plus TVET CDACC competency-based programmes at Level 3, Level 4 and Level 5 in electrical installation, plumbing, food and beverage, accommodation operations, office assistance, social work, library and information studies and information communication technology. The institute's own website states that it offers short, artisan, certificate, diploma and advanced diploma courses and publishes admission grade requirements of C- for diploma, D or D+ for certificate and D- or KCPE for artisan entry. It lists NITA, KNEC, KASNEB, ABMA, ICM and ICDL among its examination and accreditation partners, describes itself as a centre of excellence for middle-level technical education, and links to a separately administered MIT Teachers Training College at mitttc.ac.ke. The institute's own website publishes the contact block recorded here at its Mbolu Malu Rd, Machakos campus; no email address is published on the pages fetched, so that detail remains unconfirmed.

context.description: Machakos Technical Institute for the Blind is a public institution that the TVETA register classifies as a Technical and Vocational College under public ownership, located in Machakos County in the Eastern region of Kenya, dedicated to technical training for learners with visual disabilities. context.description: Machakos Town TVC is a public technical and vocational college in Machakos County, in Kenya's Eastern region, registered by the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority on 15 May 2024 as TVETA/PUBLIC/TVC/0016/2024 with a licence valid to 14 May 2029. Its accredited-award table, taken from the regulator's per-institution record, lists competency-based programmes spanning CDACC levels 3 to 6 across electrical installation, masonry and building technology, welding, plumbing, fashion design, cosmetology, food production, information communication technology, agricultural extension and business management. Every award on the register is examined by the TVET Curriculum Development, Assessment and Certification Council rather than by KNEC, which indicates the college trains on the modular competency-based model. The college's own website prints two addresses in its Contact Us block, the institutional info@machakostowntvc.ac.ke and a backup Gmail account, together with the postal address P.O. Box 3544-90100 Machakos; the institutional domain address is recorded here and the website itself was not previously asserted in this record, so basic_info.website remains null in the payload while the stored column is unchanged.

description: The Commission for University Education register of 15 September 2026 lists Machakos University as a Public Chartered University chartered in 2016, and the CUE accredited programme register of 31 July 2026 records 51 Machakos University awards. The programmes recorded here are the leading set of that register: twelve bachelor's degrees in arts, commerce, economics, education, environmental sciences, library and information science, actuarial science and computer science, eight master's degrees in arts, business, economics and religious studies, and a Doctor of Philosophy in Applied Linguistics approved in 2020. The university publishes its address as P.O. Box 136-90100, Machakos County, with general enquiries and complaints reporting on +254 735 247 939 and info@mksu.ac.ke, and the same number appears in its complaints-handling procedure. Its e-learning provision runs on a live Moodle portal at https://elearning.mksu.ac.ke, which answered on 2026-10-25 with undergraduate and postgraduate course sections, and the university traces its origins to a 1957 Technical Rural Training School chartered as Machakos University in October 2016. context.description: Machakos University TVET Institute is a public TVET institution recorded in the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority register of accredited institutions as TVETA/PUBLIC/TVC/0029/2020, registered on 23 January 2020 with a licence valid to 10 April 2031 and a status of Registered and Licensed, in Machakos County; it is registered as a Technical and Vocational College even though its name associates it with Machakos University. The register lists KNEC artisan awards in building technology, fashion design and garment making, food and beverage and motor vehicle mechanics, and thirteen KNEC craft awards spanning automotive engineering, building technology, business management, catering and accommodation operations, electrical and electronics technology (power), fashion, food and beverage production and service, information communication technology, mechanical engineering (plant) and (production), sales and marketing, social development and supply chain management. Sixteen KNEC diploma awards are recorded across accountancy, automotive engineering, building technology, business management, catering and accommodation management, civil engineering, electrical and electronics engineering (power), fashion design and clothing technology, food and beverage production, sales and service management, information communication technology, mechanical engineering (plant) and (production), sales and marketing, social work and community development and supply chain management. The board's professional-level Certified Public Accountants qualification also appears on the register but falls outside the schema's qualification levels and is therefore described here rather than recorded as a course. Register levels were normalised to the schema vocabulary, with Craft rendered as Certificate, and the same subject appears at several levels where the register lists it separately rather than being collapsed. The register publishes no street address, telephone line or institutional email for the institute, and no institution-owned website was confirmed in this pass, so those fields are recorded as absent rather than estimated.

context.description: Mahanaim Educational Institute is a private technical and vocational college registered by the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority under registration number TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0221/2016, first registered on 14 July 2016 and licensed to 21 July 2031, operating in Nairobi County. The TVETA register records thirteen accredited qualifications spanning artisan, craft and diploma levels; where the same programme name appears at two levels the higher award is recorded here, giving ten distinct programmes. Craft and diploma awards in food and beverage production and service, tour guiding and travel operations, automotive engineering, fashion design and clothing technology, information communication technology and food and beverage management are examined by the Kenya National Examinations Council, while NITA nationally tests the beauty therapy, hairdressing and motor vehicle mechanics trade courses. The institute publishes the domain mahanaim.ac.ke, which served a live institutional site on 25 October 2026 carrying the contact address mahanaimcollege@gmail.com and the telephone numbers 0700 260 260 and 0700 351 048. The published programme mix shows a hospitality and fashion orientation alongside automotive and ICT training. No e-learning or distance-learning portal and no student population figure could be evidenced in this pass.

context.about: Maior Lugha School of International Languages (Malughas) is a private language school based in Nairobi, Kenya, that trains international languages online, principally German, English, French and Kiswahili alongside Spanish, Italian, Arabic and Mandarin. It presents itself as bridging communication barriers for international interaction and offers CEFR-graded courses from beginner to advanced level.

context.description: Maior Lugha School of International Languages, trading as Malughas, is a private language school with its administration in Buruburu, Nairobi, that specialises in training international languages online, in particular German, English, French and Kiswahili alongside Spanish, Italian, Arabic and Mandarin. It states that it has more than 20 years of experience and has taught over 500 students, and that learners can log in from anywhere in the world at their own pace. Courses are offered across CEFR levels from beginner through elementary, intermediate, vantage and advanced, with stated durations ranging from 90 to 100 hours for the shortest courses to 1,000 to 1,200 hours at the top level. The school describes its mission as leading the teaching and learning of languages through quality online language training for academic and personal purposes, with objectives covering understanding, speaking, writing and reading the target language. Qualified learners are offered grammar review and oral, audio and video programmes, while complete beginners are prepared for internationally recognised certificates, and the school also offers translation services.

context.about: Majengo Vocational Training Centre is a public vocational training centre in Siaya County, Kenya, registered and licensed by the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority as TVETA/PUBLIC/VTC/0010/2023. It offers artisan-level trade-test training in electrical installation, masonry and garment-making trades, assessed by the National Industrial Training Authority.

The regulator lists five programme entries, reduced here to four distinct qualifications because Dressmaking appears twice: Electrical Wireman, Masonry, Tailoring and Dressmaking, all at trade-test level assessed by the National Industrial Training Authority. context.about: Maji Mazuri is a Kenyan non-governmental organisation working in Nairobi's Mathare Valley, running a children's centre, the Headstart primary school and youth and teens groups that deliver vocational, computer and talent skills training alongside education and family support.
context.description: Maji Mazuri is a Kenyan non-governmental organisation founded in 1984 by Dr Wanjiku Kironyo that works in the Mathare Valley on the outskirts of Nairobi. Its own site describes programmes that include a children's centre for disabled children, the Headstart primary school serving more than 500 pupils in Mathare, and youth and teens groups that give young people access to vocational and talent development covering drama, sports, music, computer and environmental skills training. The vocational courses recorded here - computer training, graphics design, web development, entrepreneurship, life skills, beadwork, art and craft and small business management - are the organisation's own training streams and are certificated in-house rather than examined by KNEC, CDACC or NITA. The Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority register separately lists a public 'Maji Mazuri VTC' (TVETA/PUBLIC/VTC/0003/2024) in Baringo County with three NITA trade tests; that entry is a different county and ownership and is therefore not attributed to this Nairobi NGO record.

description: Maji Mazuri is a Kenyan non-governmental organisation founded in 1984 by Dr Wanjiku Kironyo that works in the Mathare Valley on the outskirts of Nairobi. Its own site describes programmes that include a children's centre for disabled children, the Headstart primary school serving more than 500 pupils in Mathare, and youth and teens groups that give young people access to vocational and talent development covering drama, sports, music, computer and environmental skills training. context.description: Manda Vocational Training Centre - Kakamega is a public vocational training institution in Kakamega County, Kenya, licensed by the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority. The TVETA register records registration number TVETA/PUBLIC/VTC/0260/2019, registered on 15 April 2019 and valid to 22 August 2029, carrying the status 'Registered and Licensed' when retrieved on 24 October 2026. The register lists seven programme rows, which reduce to six distinct trades once the duplicated Dressmaking entry is collapsed: carpentry and joinery, electrical wireman, tailoring, dressmaking, masonry, and motor vehicle mechanics. All six are assessed by the National Industrial Training Authority at trade-test level, which corresponds to the artisan band of the Kenyan qualifications framework. A 2026-11-09 fetch of TVETA's magazine The TVET Eye issue 004 (https://www.tveta.go.ke/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/THE-TVETA-EYE-2023-issue-4-final.pdf) again lists 'Manda Vocational Training Centre - Kakamega' among institutions registered as of end October 2023, a second fetched regulator source distinct from the on-disk corpus rows. A contacts-aggregator page (https://www.davidodigitalsolutions.com/2022/12/contacts-of-kenyan-colleges_16.html) surfaced in search with the indexed line 'MANDA VOCATIONAL TRAINING CENTRE - KAKAMEGA P.O BOX 550 - 50205 WEBUYE 724874349 mandapolytechnic@gmail.com', but the page's M-section could not be extracted within the fetch cap and Firecrawl scrape timed out, so those contact values are recorded here only as uncorroborated candidates pending a fetchable source. No independent centre website, social page or Google Business profile was confirmed; the historical Isibania/Migori address conflation noted by the prior pass remains unexplained and unadded.

context.about: Mandera Technical Training Institute is a public technical and vocational college at Neboi, about 8 km off Mandera Town in Mandera County, North Eastern Kenya. It is registered and licensed by the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority as TVETA/PUBLIC/TVC/0052/2016 and delivers competency-based training from Level 4 to Level 6 across electrical, ICT and secretarial, building and plumbing, business, health and social science, and mechanical and automotive departments.

context.description: Mandera Technical Training Institute, which brands itself Mandera TTI with the motto Technolojia na Ufanisi, is recorded in the TVETA register as a public Technical and Vocational College in Mandera County under registration number TVETA/PUBLIC/TVC/0052/2016; the register entry carried a licence expiry of 25 August 2026 and the status Expired License at the time of research, which is reproduced here rather than corrected. The institute states on its own website that it began in 2016 with ten students and now trains over 1,000 trainees, and that it is managed by a Board of Governors appointed by the Cabinet Secretary for Education while the Principal and support staff run day-to-day operations. Its academic offer runs across six departments, namely Electrical and Electronic, ICT and Secretarial, Building and Plumbing, Business Studies, Health and Social Science, and Mechanical and Automotive, and the institute publishes 29 competency-based courses from Level 4 to Level 6 with stated durations of one to three years. Intakes are advertised for January, May and September, with online application, a student and trainer portal at portal.manderatti.ac.ke and a learning-management-system portal at lms.manderatti.ac.ke. Its published contact details are P.O. Box 257-70300 Mandera, Neboi about 8 km off Mandera Town opposite Mandera Special School, telephone +254 723 172 746 and email info@manderatti.ac.ke. No named officer, student population figure or logo could be confirmed from the fetched pages, so those fields are left empty.

context.description: The Marianist Technical Institute - Malindi officially opened on June 20, 2024, following the laying of its foundation stone on July 26, 2023. This new branch transitioned from the Motolese Vocational Institute, previously under the Catholic Diocese of Malindi. As part of the Marianist East Africa projects, the institute aims to provide quality technical education and vocational training to the youth in the coastal region, thereby enhancing local skills development and employment opportunities. The broader mission of the Marianists, inspired by Father William Joseph Chaminade, focuses on using education and skills training to uplift individuals, foster Christian community, and assist women and youth in finding employment to lead lives of respect, dignity, and resourcefulness. The institution offers nationally certified post-secondary adult vocational certificate programs designed to prepare students for a dynamic and evolving economy.

context.description: Marist International University College is a private Catholic university college on Marist Lane off Langata Road in Karen, Nairobi, owned by the Conference of Major Superiors of the Marist Brothers of the African region. It began in 1986 as Marist International Centre, became a constituent college of the Catholic University of Eastern Africa in 2002 and was gazetted as Marist International University College by the Kenya Government in September 2011. Its programmes run from certificates and diplomas in business management, procurement and supply chain, information technology, religious studies, project planning, security studies and development studies and social work, through advanced diplomas and bachelors degrees, to the Master of Arts in Psycho-spiritual Therapy and Counselling taught with the Psycho-Spiritual Institute. All awards are examined internally by the college under its university mandate, and teaching is delivered physically and through blended learning. The college also runs a summer integrative course and a sabbatical programme, which are non-award offerings and therefore excluded from the course list.

It delivers artisan-level trade training in masonry, tailoring and dressmaking, tested by the National Industrial Training Authority.
context.description: Mariwa Vocational Training Center is a public vocational training centre registered by the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority under number TVETA/PUBLIC/VTC/0039/2016 on 14 April 2016. The regulator's register records its licence as Registered and Licensed with an expiry date of 21 July 2030 and lists seven accredited award rows in three trades. Those rows repeat Masonry three times, Tailoring twice and Dressmaking twice at NITA trade-test level, so de-duplication by course, level and exam body leaves three distinct awards. Following the Schologic level-normalisation convention, NITA Trade Test awards are recorded at Artisan level rather than Certificate level. No institutional website, e-mail address, telephone line or street address was published on the regulator's record, so those fields remain null rather than guessed. The centre is registered as a public VTC in Kisumu County.

context.description: Marungu Vocational Training Center is a public vocational training centre entered in the TVETA register of accredited TVET institutions under registration number TVETA/PUBLIC/VTC/0020/2020, registered on 16 April 2020, in Taita Taveta County within the Coast region. context.description: Established in 1986, Masai Technical Training Institute (MTTI), now known as Maasai National Polytechnic, is a premier public Technical Vocational Education and Training (TVET) institution under the Ministry of Education in Kenya. Its mission is to provide Competency-Based Education and Training (CBET) programs that equip youth with relevant skills aligned with industry requirements, fostering economic growth and development. The institute is located in Kajiado town, between the county headquarters and Kajiado town, along Nairobi-Namanga Road. MTTI has a history of expansion and infrastructure development, evolving from a technical school to a national polytechnic with an expanded mandate to train, assess, and certify. It boasts a serene and learner-friendly environment conducive to learning, creativity, and innovation, with six academic departments offering diverse courses. The institution has received national recognition for excellence in technical education and is committed to continuous improvement and relevance through industry linkages and a robust Quality Management System.

context.description: Masinde Muliro University of Science and Technology (MMUST) is a public university located in Kakamega in Kakamega County, western Kenya, describing itself as the premier university in science, technology and innovation. The university operates eleven schools, listed on its website as agriculture and veterinary sciences, arts and social sciences, business and economics, computing and informatics, disaster management and humanitarian assistance, education, engineering and the built environment, medicine, natural sciences, nursing midwifery and paramedical sciences, and public health biomedical sciences and technology. Its academic programmes booklet lists bachelors, diploma and certificate programmes examined internally by the University Senate, with intakes in January, May and September and a separate TVET Institute accredited by TVETA to offer diploma and certificate programmes. The university reports approximately 20,000 students and more than 400 programmes across the eleven schools, and it publishes an Open, Distance and e-Learning platform at odel.mmust.ac.ke through which online study is delivered. Admissions contact details published by the university are info@mmust.ac.ke and admissions@mmust.ac.ke, with telephone lines +254 702597360/1, +254 733120020/2 and 057 2505222/3.

It serves Machakos County in the Eastern region with artisan, craft and diploma programmes examined by KNEC and competency-based courses examined by TVET CDACC.
context.description: TVETA registered the college on 19 June 2017 and its licence runs to 2 July 2029 with status Registered and Licensed. The regulator's course table lists twenty-five accredited programme entries spanning electrical, agricultural, business, ICT, hospitality, tourism and social development disciplines. KNEC examines the artisan, craft and diploma awards, while TVET CDACC examines competency-based programmes including cosmetology at Levels 3 to 6 and mechatronics at Levels 5 and 6. Register levels were normalised to the schema vocabulary, with Craft rendered as Certificate, CDACC Level 3 and 4 as Artisan, Level 5 as Certificate and Level 6 as Diploma. The college's own website publishes a Contacts page that prints info@masingatechnical.ac.ke beside the telephone (+254) 746 327 094 and the postal address 181-90141 Masinga, which is the address recorded here as the institutional e-mail; the site additionally names a registrar as an alternative contact but prints no personal mailbox for him.

context.description: Matibabu Foundation College of Health Sciences is a private Technical and Vocational College registered by the TVET Authority on 16 February 2017 under TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0030/2017, with the licence valid to 8 October 2028. It operates as the Mary Ann Van Dam School of Nursing (MAVDSON) and is an affiliate of Matibabu Foundation Kenya, located in Ukwala town in Siaya County. Its current flagship offering is four main health programmes: a three-year Diploma in Community Health Nursing licensed by the Nursing Council of Kenya, Perioperative Theatre Technology at CDACC Level 5 (certificate) and Level 6 (diploma), and the Certificate in Healthcare Support Services at Level 5, while the TVETA register also records KNEC-examined business, ICT, counselling and social development programmes. The college runs a live Moodle learning management system at https://lms.matibabucollege.org/ carrying course categories for the community health nursing and perioperative theatre technology diplomas. Its Matibabu Emergency Care and Training Centre (MECTC) is Western Kenya's first AHA-certified emergency care training facility, fully integrated with a 75-bed hospital offering 24/7 emergency services, an ICU, three operating theatres and a simulation laboratory. Students gain hands-on experience through the college's library, skills and computer laboratories, hostels and affiliations with leading hospitals and health facilities.

context.description: Mbeere North Technical and Vocational College is recorded in the TVET Authority register as a public Technical and Vocational College in Embu County with registration number TVETA/PUBLIC/TVC/0014/2023, registered on 4 May 2023 and listed on the 24 October 2026 register snapshot as 'Registered and Licensed' with the licence running to 3 May 2028. The college's own website describes it as an institution under the State Department for TVET located in Mbeere North Constituency, three kilometres from Siakago Town, 28 kilometres from Embu town and 158 kilometres south-east of Nairobi, and publishes the postal address P.O. context.about: Mbita Technical and Vocational College is a public TVET institution on the Homabay-Mbita road in Homa Bay County, in the Lake Victoria basin of western Kenya. Established in 2024 and registered by TVETA under TVETA/PUBLIC/TVC/0026/2024, it serves over 2,000 trainees with competency-based certificate, artisan and diploma programmes across eight academic departments.
context.description: Mbita Technical and Vocational College (Mbita TVC) is a public technical and vocational institution established in 2024 and registered by the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority under registration number TVETA/PUBLIC/TVC/0026/2024, registered on 29 October 2024 with a licence valid to 28 October 2029. The college sits on the Homabay-Mbita road and describes itself as serving learners drawn from Homa Bay, Migori, Kisumu and Siaya counties and the wider Lake Victoria Basin. Its stated mission is to provide accessible, relevant and high-quality TVET that equips trainees with industry-driven competencies, and its own welcome page reports that it has grown to serve over 2,000 trainees across technical and vocational disciplines. Academic work is organised into eight departments: mechanical and automotive, liberal studies, computing and informatics, hospitality and institutional management, building and civil engineering, business and entrepreneurship, electrical and electronics, and agriculture and environmental studies. The TVETA register of accredited programmes lists 44 qualifications including KNEC diploma, craft and artisan trades and CDACC competency-based levels.

context.description: The Michuki National Polytechnic appears on the TVET Authority register of accredited institutions as MICHUKI NATIONAL POLYTECHNIC, a public National Polytechnic in Murang'a County, registration number TVETA/PUBLIC/NP/0002/2025, registered on 14 February 2025 and licensed to 13 February 2030 in 'Registered and Licensed' status. The register carries 50 accredited course rows for the licence; after collapsing rows that repeat the same course, level and examining body, 22 distinct awards are recorded here, and the remaining register rows beyond those published in the table segment retrieved were not transcribed rather than guessed. The institution's own site, which loads from both michukitech.ac.ke and themichukipoly.ac.ke, titles every page 'The Michuki National Polytechnic', describes itself as MiNaP and addresses correspondences to The Principal, The Michuki National Polytechnic, P.O. Box 4-10200, Kangema, with the polytechnic mailbox info@themichukipoly.ac.ke and telephone +254 114 426579, while its contact page additionally publishes a registrar mailbox and line. Teaching is organised into nine academic departments - hospitality and tourism, building and civil engineering, applied sciences, mechanical engineering, fashion and cosmetology, computing and informatics, liberal studies, business, and electrical engineering - and the site also advertises short courses in computer applications, mobile phone repair, CCTV installation and web design that carry no KNQF level and are therefore described here rather than recorded as levelled awards. Its management board lists a Deputy Principal (Academics), a Registrar and a Finance Officer, and the site names HELB, KUCCPS, KNEC, KASNEB, CDACC, NITA, TVETA, KICD and the Ministry of Education as partners. No enrolment figure is published; the polytechnic's ODeL Department (https://themichukipoly.ac.ke/e_learning) has deployed Moodle LMS and Google Apps for Education (Google Meet and Google Classroom) alongside the student portal at https://www.michukiportal.ac.ke/, and promotes blended distance/residential learning as well as flexible part-time training (evening, school holidays and weekends); legacy references to 'Michuki TTI' on the site are historical, the institution now being registered as a national polytechnic.

context.description: Minoke Technical Training Institute (MTTI) is a privately owned training institute operating from Zima Plaza, 4th Floor, on North Airport Road off Mombasa Road in Embakasi, Nairobi, and describes itself as the leading Kenyan trainer of caregivers and nursing assistants. Its website publishes a programme structure organised into a School of Skills Advancement, a School of Public and Environmental Health Sciences, a School of Community Health and Development, a CDACC/NITA accredited section, a School of Business Studies and a School of ICT. The School of Skills Advancement lists certificates in healthcare assistant, community mental health management, phlebotomy, basic life support and community health extension; the public and environmental health school lists diplomas and certificates in public health and environmental health sciences; the community health school lists diplomas in community health and development and peri-operative technology; the CDACC and NITA section lists certificate and diploma awards in health service support; and the business and ICT schools list certificates and diplomas in human resource management, accountancy, business management, ICT, web design and graphic design. Only the two health service support awards carry an explicitly named external awarding body, TVET CDACC, so the remaining school-based certificates and diplomas are recorded with the internal examining body because the source does not name another examiner; a Certified Public Accountant entry is excluded because a professional qualification of that kind is not schema-representable. The institute publishes the telephone line +254 795 509 887 and the email address info@minoketechnical.com and places its campus on North Airport Road in Embakasi, Nairobi. The live domain could not be fetched during this pass, so the institution's own pages are cited from the Internet Archive snapshot dated 23 March 2025; no named officer, student count or e-learning portal is published there.

context.description: Moffat Bible College describes itself as training men and women for effective Christian Ministry in Africa and the World. The college traces its origin to the W.Y. Moffat Memorial Bible Training Institute, opened on 11 February 1929 by the Africa Inland Mission at its Kijabe headquarters, and was renamed Moffat College of Bible in 1977 before adopting its present name in 2008. name: Moi University

context.about: Moi University is a public chartered university in Kenya, established by the Government in mid-1984 after the 1981 Mackay report and the 1983 Kenyan-UNESCO Project for the Second University recommended a second national university with a bias towards technology. Its main campus is at Kesses in Uasin Gishu County, near Eldoret, where the administration moved on 29 July 1986. It reports 242 academic programmes, 23,472 students and 145,203 alumni as of March 2025.

context.description: Moi University was established in 1984 and inaugurated on 6 December 1985 as Kenya's second public university. The Commission for University Education lists it as a public chartered university, established 1984 and chartered 2013. Teaching runs across four campuses: Main Campus at Kesses, the Eldoret Town and Annex campus hosting the College of Health Sciences near Moi Teaching and Referral Hospital, Nairobi Campus at Bazaar Plaza and Coast Campus in Mombasa. The university describes fourteen schools, one university college, directorates and institutes, delivering programmes in blended mode. The Institute of Open Distance e-Learning runs the MUSOMI learner management system for self-paced study, and the TVET Institute offers TVET CDACC approved Level 6 programmes.

context.description: Moi University was established by the Government of Kenya in 1984 as the country's second public university, founded by then President Daniel arap Moi to expand higher education beyond the University of Nairobi. The university has since grown into a multi-campus institution with schools spanning education, engineering, health sciences, business, law, agriculture, information sciences, arts and social sciences, science and tourism. Its Main Campus sits at Kesses near Eldoret, while teaching is also delivered through the Annex Campus and College of Health Sciences in Eldoret and the Nairobi Campus at The Bazaar Plaza on Moi Avenue. The institution combines face-to-face teaching with online delivery and supports Open, Distance and e-Learning through its MUSOMI platform under the Institute of Open Distance e-Learning (IODeL). The university is ISO 9001:2015 certified and its programmes are recognised by the Commission for University Education.

context.description: Moi University TVET Institute is the technical and vocational education arm of Moi University and publishes its prospectus on the university's official website, mu.ac.ke. The institute states that it offers TVET CDACC-approved Level 6 courses, grouped into five academic departments covering Computer Science and ICT, Agriculture, Health Sciences, Business Studies, and Social Sciences and Journalism. Minimum admission requirements are published as a KCSE mean grade of C- or a relevant Level 5 qualification, and applications are routed through the university's online admissions portal at admissions.mu.ac.ke. Enquiries are directed to Moi University Main Campus on 0722 459 155 or 0718 180 055. The Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority register also lists the institute as a public technical and vocational college under number TVETA/PUBLIC/TVC/0008/2024 in Uasin Gishu County, with a licence recorded as valid to 24 April 2029 and the status 'Registered and Licensed'. The institute publishes no separate mailbox of its own, and an earlier pass declined to resolve the TVET page's own contact line because it displays one address while its mailto target differs; the university's own Our Contacts page prints info@mu.ac.ke as the institutional mailbox for the Main Campus, Kesses, Eldoret, and that printed parent address is recorded here.

NITA trade-test awards are mapped to the schema's Artisan level and the single craft award to Certificate. The regulator's record for this centre carries the telephone line printed here from that same record; no institutional website or email address could be confirmed from a primary source, so those fields remain unverified. No distance-learning or e-learning provision is published for the centre.

context.description: Mudete Friends Vocational Training Centre is a public vocational training centre situated at Mudete Primary School near Mudete Friends Church in Mudete village, Chavakali Ward, Sabatia Sub-County, Vihiga County. The TVETA register records registration on 25 April 2024 under number TVETA/PUBLIC/VTC/0005/2024, a licence valid to 24 April 2029 and a status of 'Registered and Licensed', with category VTC and public ownership, and its programme table lists six artisan qualifications in building technology, electrical installation, information communication technology, motor vehicle technology, masonry and motor vehicle mechanics. The mobile number inherited from the source database appears on no fetched page and was dropped, and no e-mail address, student population, facilities inventory, e-learning portal or distance-learning provision is published on any fetched source.

description: Mukeu Vocational Training Centre is recorded by the TVET Authority as a public Vocational Training Centre in Nyandarua County, Central region, under registration number TVETA/PUBLIC/VTC/0017/2017, registered on 16 February 2017 and licensed to 18 October 2029 in 'Registered and Licensed' status. The regulator's accredited course table carries six entries, all NITA trade-test awards: carpentry and joinery, electrical wireman, masonry, motor vehicle mechanics, tailoring and dressmaking. All six map to the schema's Artisan level, since NITA trade testing certifies artisan-grade competence rather than a craft certificate or diploma. The regulator's record for this centre sits at Chepchonia on Ndunyu Njeru Road in Nyandarua County and carries the telephone line printed here from that same record; no institutional website, email address or additional street address could be confirmed from a primary source, so those fields are recorded as unverified rather than estimated. No distance-learning or e-learning provision is published for the centre.
