context.description: Shilolavakhali County Vocational Training Center was registered by the TVET Authority on 19 September 2016 under registration number TVETA/PUBLIC/VTC/0130/2016, and the register snapshot of 25 October 2026 records the licence as Registered and Licensed with an expiry date of 22 August 2029. The TVETA course table lists eleven rows which, after removing exact repeats of Masonry and Motor Vehicle Mechanics, reduce to nine distinct awards: three KNEC NVCET programmes in Agri-Business, Electrical and Electronics Technology and Fashion Design and Garment Making, plus six NITA trade tests in Masonry, Electrical Wireman, Food and Beverage Production, Motor Vehicle Mechanics, Tailoring and Dressmaking. Under the level-normalisation convention used across this dataset, both KNEC NVCET and NITA Trade Test awards are recorded at Artisan level because neither is a craft certificate or diploma. As a county vocational training centre the institution is publicly owned under the county government and is registered in the VTC category on the regulator register. The register publishes no postal address, town, e-mail address, telephone number, website or staff list, so those fields remain null rather than guessed.

The institute delivers technical, industrial, vocational and entrepreneurship training, including a Dual TVET model that combines company and institutional training.
context.description: Siala Technical Training Institute is a public technical training institute listed by the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority under registration number TVETA/PUBLIC/TVC/0027/2016 in Migori County, Kenya. Its published postal address is P.O. Box 164-40404, Rongo, and its website prints the telephone line +254 706 633334 together with the email addresses info@sialatech.ac.ke and admissions@sialatech.ac.ke. The regulator's accredited course table lists twelve qualifications: KNEC craft and diploma programmes in plumbing and welding and fabrication, plus TVET CDACC modular programmes from Level 3 to Level 6 in electrical installation, front office, automotive technology, electrical engineering, ICT, mechanical production and mechanical engineering. The institute describes its mission as providing quality technical, industrial, vocational and entrepreneurship training supported by research, innovation and staff development, and advertises a Dual TVET model in which sixty per cent of training is delivered in industry and forty per cent at the institute. Departments published on the site include building and civil engineering, and the institute states that it aligns its delivery with greening TVET objectives.

context.description: Sigalagala National Polytechnic is a public National Polytechnic in Ikolomani Constituency, Kakamega County, domiciled under the Ministry of Education's State Department for Technical and Vocational Education and Training and governed by a Governing Council appointed by the Cabinet Secretary for Education. The Council is chaired by Prof. Genevieve Mwayuli, Professor of Agribusiness – Aquatic Ecology and Deputy Vice Chancellor at Great Lakes University of Kisumu, with Mr. Evans O. Bosire serving as Principal, Accounting Officer and Council Secretary leading day-to-day management. Under the Sigalagala National Polytechnic Order, 2016 (Legal Notice No. 90) the institution is structured into four institutes - Hospitality and Consumer Sciences, Engineering, Applied and Natural Sciences, and Business - while teaching runs across ten academic departments. It operates three campuses: the main campus at Sigalagala, Kakamega Town Campus at IG Plaza in Kakamega town, and Maturu Campus along the Webuye–Eldoret Highway. Programmes are offered at artisan, certificate, diploma and higher diploma levels, mostly under the CBET framework examined by TVET CDACC alongside KNEC, KASNEB, HRMPEB and ICM awards, with a further range examined internally. The polytechnic also runs an NTSA-registered driving school, a journalism section holding an FM radio licence, and an ODeL centre, and aims to produce middle-level technicians and technologists for Kenya Vision 2030.

about: Sigalagala National Polytechnic is a publicly managed National Polytechnic in Kakamega County, Western Kenya, under the Ministry of Education's State Department for Technical and Vocational Education and Training. Established in 1950 as the Nyanza Technical and Trade School on a thirty-three-acre site inherited from British gold miners of the 1930s, it became a National Technical School in 1967, a Technical Training Institute in the late 1980s, and was elevated to National Polytechnic status by Legal Notice No. 90 of 2016 under section 26(2) of the TVET Act 2013.
description: Sigalagala National Polytechnic is a public National Polytechnic in Ikolomani Constituency, Kakamega County, domiciled under the Ministry of Education's State Department for Technical and Vocational Education and Training and governed by a Governing Council appointed by the Cabinet Secretary for Education. The Council is chaired by Prof. Genevieve Mwayuli, Professor of Agribusiness – Aquatic Ecology and Deputy Vice Chancellor at Great Lakes University of Kisumu, with Mr. Evans O. Bosire serving as Principal, Accounting Officer and Council Secretary leading day-to-day management. Under the Sigalagala National Polytechnic Order, 2016 (Legal Notice No. 90) the institution is structured into four institutes - Hospitality and Consumer Sciences, Engineering, Applied and Natural Sciences, and Business - while teaching runs across ten academic departments. It operates three campuses: the main campus at Sigalagala, Kakamega Town Campus at IG Plaza in Kakamega town, and Maturu Campus along the Webuye–Eldoret Highway. Programmes are offered at artisan, certificate, diploma and higher diploma levels, mostly under the CBET framework examined by TVET CDACC alongside KNEC, KASNEB, HRMPEB and ICM awards, with a further range examined internally. The polytechnic also runs an NTSA-registered driving school, a journalism section holding an FM radio licence, and an ODeL centre, and aims to produce middle-level technicians and technologists for Kenya Vision 2030.

name: Sikri Technical and Vocational College for the Blind and Deaf

context.about: Sikri Technical and Vocational College for the Blind and Deaf is a public technical and vocational college in Homa Bay County, Nyanza region, Kenya, registered and licensed by the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority as TVETA/PUBLIC/TVC/0006/2018 and accredited for KNEC artisan, craft and diploma programmes, NITA trade tests and TVET CDACC competency-based programmes at Levels 3 to 6.
context.description: Sikri Technical and Vocational College for the Blind and Deaf appears in the TVETA register of accredited TVET institutions as a public technical and vocational college (category TVC) in Homa Bay County, Nyanza region, and is distinctive among Kenyan TVET institutions for its mandate to train blind and deaf students. TVETA registered it on 12 April 2018 under registration number TVETA/PUBLIC/TVC/0006/2018 with a licence valid to 6 February 2029 in 'Registered and Licensed' status. Its accredited course table carries fifty-five rows which deduplicate to forty-two distinct awards: KNEC artisan, craft and diploma programmes in fashion and garment making, building technology, electrical and electronics technology, information communication technology, social development, hairdressing and beauty therapy, entrepreneurial agriculture and social work and community development; nine National Industrial Training Authority trade tests in carpentry, electrical wiring, hairdressing, masonry, plumbing, tailoring, welding, dressmaking and beauty therapy; and TVET CDACC competency-based programmes from Level 3 to Level 6 covering cosmetology, carpentry, computer operations, electrical installation, fashion design, horticulture, masonry, motor vehicle mechanics, plumbing, poultry production, dairy operations, information technology, social work, human resource management, building technology, civil engineering, cyber security, culinary arts and water engineering technology. Craft awards are recorded as Certificate level, trade tests and CDACC Levels 3 and 4 as Artisan, Level 5 as Certificate and Level 6 as Diploma in the Schologic level scheme. No institutional website, email address, telephone line, campus street address or student population figure is published in the sources fetched, so those fields remain unconfirmed rather than estimated.

The college's own website describes it as a training institution for professional and academic development across Africa and states that it operates in Kenya, Nigeria and Ghana, delivering Chartered Institute of Marketing, Digital Marketing Institute and Project Management Institute qualifications. The CIM page lists five qualifications, from the Foundation Certificate in Professional Marketing through the Certificate and Diploma in Professional and Digital Marketing to the Postgraduate Diploma in Professional Marketing, and the DMI page describes the ten-module Certified Digital Marketing Professional programme examined online with remote proctoring. description: Skypath Aviation College is a private aviation training institution based at Wilson Airport on Langata Road in Nairobi, registered by the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority as a Technical and Vocational College under number TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0052/2021, first registered on 21 July 2021. The TVETA register now records the licence as expired on 20 July 2026 and publishes no course table for the institution, while the college's own website continues to advertise open applications for its next intake. The college publishes five certificate programmes — airline cabin crew, flight dispatch, ramp operations, passenger handling and aircraft maintenance — of six months to one year, and five diploma programmes — airline cabin crew, airline customer service, flight dispatch, tours and travel, and aircraft maintenance — of eighteen months to three years, the aircraft maintenance diploma being a three-year airframe and powerplant programme preparing students for licensing pathways. Three programme titles are offered at both certificate and diploma level, so the award level is carried in each course label. Entry requirements are published per programme (typically KCSE grades between D and C with specified subject passes), and the college advertises experienced industry instructors, simulator and real-aircraft exposure, and career guidance with partner airlines. No examination or licensing body is named on the pages retrieved, so the awards are recorded as internally examined by the college; the site lists only aviation-industry licensing pathways without naming a regulator. The campus is at Wilson Airport and the published contact channels are the telephone lines +254 723 944885 and +254 758 466690 and the address admin@skypathcollage.com, reproduced exactly as printed on the site.

context.description: Skyworld Aviation Training College is recorded in the TVETA register of accredited institutions as a private Technical and Vocational College in Nairobi County under registration number TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0027/2018, registered on 12 April 2018 with a licence valid to 30 June 2030 and the status Registered and Licensed. The college's Facebook-page mirror at schoolandcollegelistings.com now verifies its published contacts: an intake notice from the college's own feed gives Call/WhatsApp 0739597979, matching the identity column's 0739 597979, with the address Ngong Road, Robanne House (3rd floor, Ngong Town; postal 00100 Nairobi, Bulbul), consistent with the stored town Ngong Rd Nairobi as a fuller form of the same place. The regulator's course table holds eight rows covering six distinct qualifications: Airline Cabin Crew and Travel and Tourism, both examined by the International Air Transport Association, recorded here at Certificate level with IATA as the examination body; KNEC craft programmes in business management and tour guiding operations recorded at Certificate level; and KNEC diploma programmes in business management and tourism management. Travel and Tourism was repeated three times in the register and was reduced to a single entry in this pass, and the business management award is accredited at two levels so both entries retain a level qualifier to keep them distinct. The college therefore combines an international aviation and travel certification portfolio with national KNEC business and tourism awards; its own published domain skyworldaviationcollege.co.ke was unreachable to automated fetch this pass, so no website is asserted in the payload.

context.description: The South Eastern Kenya University TVET Directorate describes itself on the university's own site as a dynamic directorate accredited by the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority to offer training at diploma and certificate levels. Its programme page groups its awards by school, listing diplomas and certificates from the School of Education, Humanities and Social Sciences, the School of Agriculture, Environment, Water and Natural Resources, the School of Science and Computing, the School of Business and Economics, and the School of Engineering and Technology. The engineering school publishes the largest block of awards, including diplomas in civil engineering, building technology, architecture, quantity surveying, automotive engineering, mechanical engineering (plant), three electrical and electronics engineering options, fashion and design, and agricultural engineering. Minimum entry requirements are published as a KCSE mean grade of C (minus) for both diploma and certificate programmes, and the directorate states that it offers specialised training with practical, entrepreneurial and industrial skills integrated with the national development agenda. The university's contact page publishes the main campus reception line as 0748605997 and the postal address P.O. Box 170-90200, Kitui, while separate lines are listed for Kitui Town Campus and the Mtito Andei and Migwani TVET centres.

context.description: Spring International Training College is a private Technical and Vocational College recorded in the TVETA register under registration number TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0085/2024, registered on 15 May 2024 with a licence valid to 14 May 2029 and the status Registered and Licensed, with Nairobi as its county. The regulator's accredited-course table lists a single programme for the college, Information Communication Technology at Craft level examined by KNEC, repeated across three identical rows. The college's own website publishes a wider catalogue than the accredited table, including a Certified Nursing Assistant (CNA) course running six months to two years with classroom instruction and supervised clinical practice, a Certificate in Teaching International Curricula delivered online, and further course pages for phlebotomy, digital marketing, graphic design, coding for children and language study for which no qualification level or external examining body is published. For the CNA and CTIC programmes the college does not name an external examining body either, so they are recorded here as institution-examined. It operates three campuses - Kilimani on Rose Avenue near Monarch Hotel, Nairobi CBD at View Park Towers on Utalii Street, and Westlands on Waiyaki Way - and runs a live Moodle site at e-learning.sitc-tvet.ac.ke headed 'Spring International Training College, center for Distance Learning'. Its history page records that the college was founded at Viewpark Towers, Wing B in July 2023 and has since grown to more than 4,000 alumni.

The TVETA register publishes twenty-two accredited course rows for the college, all assessed by the TVET Curriculum Development, Assessment and Certification Council; after collapsing the duplicated cosmetology rows at Levels 3 and 4, twenty distinct course-and-level qualifications remain, ranging from masonry, welding, plumbing and electrical installation to ICT, fashion design, cosmetology, business management, automotive technology and sustainable agriculture for rural development. The college's website field points to its official Facebook page ('Subukia Technical and Vocational College | Nakuru'), which was confirmed live but publishes no institutional email address, no campus street address and no course prospectus that could be verified, so telephone and email are left empty. The imported record carried the postal value 'P.o. BOX 62 kabazi' and the telephone 0112 990575, neither of which could be confirmed from a fetched official page. No student enrolment figure, facility inventory, e-learning portal or named officer could be verified.

context.description: Summit Institute of Professionals is a private technical and vocational college in Nairobi County, registered by the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority as TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0278/2016. The regulator's register records a licence currently valid to 2 February 2027 with the status Registered and Licensed. Its accredited-award table is concentrated in business and commerce: KNEC craft and diploma qualifications in business management, human resource management, banking and finance, accountancy, project management, sales and marketing, supply chain management and information communication technology, artisan awards in salesmanship and storekeeping, and KASNEB awards including Accounting Technicians Diploma and Certified Public Accountants. The register also lists an ICDL Africa digital-literacy certificate and KASNEB professional awards whose levels do not map onto the Schologic qualification levels, so they are recorded in this narrative rather than as course entries. No institution-owned website, email address, telephone line or e-learning portal could be confirmed from a fetched source in this research pass, so those identity fields remain empty.

context.about: SAPTA College is the training institution of Support for Addictions Prevention and Treatment in Africa, a Nairobi-based international NGO, and is registered and licensed by the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority as TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0236/2016. It trains addiction counsellors at diploma and certificate level and runs an online virtual school for its chemical dependency and addiction counselling programmes.
context.description: SAPTA College is registered by the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority under registration number TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0236/2016, registered on 14 July 2016 and licensed to 26 January 2027 with the status 'Registered and Licensed', and the regulator places it in Nairobi County. The accredited course table carries a single qualification, a diploma in counselling with a chemical dependency and addictions specialisation examined by the Kenya National Examinations Council. The college is the training arm of Support for Addictions Prevention and Treatment in Africa, an international NGO registered in Kenya, whose site describes a sixteen-month diploma delivered part-time one day a week and by distance learning, a five-month certificate in chemical dependency and addiction counselling, and Colombo Plan ICCE universal treatment curriculum and international certification programmes. Contact details published by the SAPTA organisation are the telephone +254 724 511 709, the e-mail frontdesk@sapta.or.ke and the postal address P.O. Box 21761-00505, Nairobi. The college operates a live virtual school at https://lms.saptacollege.ac.ke/ that publishes its online certificate and diploma in addiction counselling, so both e-learning and distance learning are recorded as verified; no student enrolment figure or campus facility inventory is published on the fetched pages.

context.description: Surfcrest Technology Training Institute (STTI) is a private TVET institution established, registered and licensed under the TVET Act, operating from a campus at Kahawa West next to La Phila on the Northern Bypass in Nairobi. The TVET Authority register records it as TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0098/2025, registered on 25 April 2025 with a licence running to 24 April 2030 and a status of Registered and Licensed. The regulator's course table lists ten accredited competence-based programmes, one at Level 3, four at Level 4 and five at Level 5, all examined by the TVET Curriculum Development, Assessment and Certification Council, spanning front office, accommodation operations, caregiving, cosmetology, electrical installation, business management, food and beverage, ICT, social work and catering. The institute organises its delivery into six schools (Cosmetology, Hospitality, ICT, Social Sciences, Business and Engineering, with a Foreign Languages link also shown) and says it works in partnership with TVET CDACC, NITA and KNEC using curricula developed for the Kenyan market. Its stated vision is to be an international centre of excellence in competence-based education and training, nurturing talents and developing technology-savvy professionals through industry-driven practical training.

name: Taita Taveta University Institute of TVET

context.about: Taita Taveta University Institute of TVET is a public technical and vocational college registered by the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority as TVETA/PUBLIC/TVC/0014/2025 in Taita Taveta County, Kenya. It is the TVET training arm associated with Taita Taveta University, accredited for TVET CDACC competency-based programmes at Level 5 and Level 6 across engineering, applied sciences, agribusiness and business fields.
context.description: Taita Taveta University Institute of TVET is a publicly owned technical and vocational college in Taita Taveta County licensed by the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority under registration number TVETA/PUBLIC/TVC/0014/2025, registered on 25 April 2025 with a licence valid to 24 April 2030. Its registered name identifies it as the TVET training arm attached to Taita Taveta University, and its offer is entirely competency-based TVET CDACC provision rather than KNEC craft and diploma courses. The register lists fourteen accredited qualifications, five at Level 5 and nine at Level 6. Level 5 covers counselling psychology, mechanical technology and maintenance, plumbing, science laboratory technology and solar PV installation. Level 6 extends to agripreneurship, aquaculture, civil engineering, counselling psychology, electrical engineering, culinary arts, human resource management, land survey and mining technology. The licence status is recorded as Registered and Licensed.

context.description: Tangaza University TVET Institute, as part of Tangaza University's mission to form transformational leaders, focuses on delivering practical, industry-relevant training designed to equip students for employment, entrepreneurship, and continued academic pursuits. The programs are aligned with TVET curriculum requirements, blending technical skills with soft skills to produce confident, innovative, and ethically grounded graduates. Learning is enhanced through modern facilities, experienced trainers, industry attachments, and a supportive academic environment. The institute aims to equip learners with practical skills, professional competence, and values essential for success in the competitive job market. Tangaza University itself began on August 25, 1986, as a constituent college of the Catholic University of Eastern Africa (CUEA), owned by the Association of Member Episcopal Conferences in Eastern Africa (AMECEA). It officially became an independent institution with a university charter granted on May 2, 2024. The university's mission is to prepare ethical and transformative servant leaders for the Church and society through quality education, innovative research, and community engagement, with a vision to be a distinguished university for academic excellence, innovative research, and service orientation for holistic transformation according to the Catholic Intellectual Tradition.

context.description: Techfix Training Institute is a privately owned technical and vocational college in Nairobi County, Kenya. It holds TVETA registration number TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0047/2025, granted on 29 January 2025 with a licence expiry date of 28 January 2030 and a status of Registered and Licensed. The TVETA register records three approved programmes at the institute: Computer Operations at Level 3, Computer and Mobile Repair at Level 4, and Information Communication Technology at Level 4, all examined by CDACC. Its training therefore concentrates on entry-level and intermediate computing and electronics repair skills. The institute's own site describes it as Nairobi's electronics repair training centre and gives its Contact Us block as P.O Box 1647-00606, Kalson Towers 6th Floor at The Crescent off Parklands Road, with the e-mail address Info@techfix.africa and the telephone number +254 750 560000. That street line sits in Nairobi, which is consistent with the Nairobi County recorded on the regulator register. The register entry itself does not record a public website, telephone number or postal address for the college.

context.about: Tetu Technical and Vocational College (Tetu TVC) is a public TVET institution in Tetu Sub-County, Nyeri County, established in March 2019 through a collaboration between the National Government and Tetu NG-CDF to decentralise technical education, offering competency-based Artisan, Certificate, Diploma and Higher Diploma programmes examined by TVET CDACC and KNEC.
context.description: Tetu Technical and Vocational College is a public TVET institution located in Tetu Constituency, about 10 kilometres from Nyeri Town off the Nyeri-Wamagana road. It was established in March 2019 through a collaboration between the National Government and Tetu NG-CDF, growing from an initial enrollment of 89 students into a recognised regional technical training centre. Its vision is to be the premier technical and vocational institution for self and global development, with the motto 'TVET skills for industrial growth'. Training is organised across eight academic departments: Cosmetology, Hospitality, Fashion and Textile, Building and Civil, Electrical, Computing and Informatics, Agriculture and Mechanical. The college also operates a dedicated ODeL Center at odel.tetutvc.ac.ke that publishes a virtual class timetable with Google Meet sessions and offers support via odelsupport@tetutvc.ac.ke.

context.description: Tharaka Technical Training Institute, also written Tharaka TVC, is a public technical and vocational college in Tharaka South Sub County, Tharaka Nithi County, Kenya. It is registered and licensed by the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority under TVETA/PUBLIC/TVC/0015/2017, with the licence running to 3 May 2028. The institute was constructed between 2013 and 2017 by the Government of Kenya and admitted its first trainees on 5 September 2017. It trains middle-level technical and vocational personnel in building and civil engineering, agriculture, electrical and mechanical engineering, fashion, hospitality and welding. Its programmes are delivered as Competency-Based Education and Training assessed by TVET CDACC, with NITA artisan trade testing also offered.

description: Tharaka Technical Training Institute is a public institution established and registered under the TVET Act (Cap 17, Laws of Kenya), with its campus at Marimanti in Tharaka Nithi County. context.about: Tharaka University TVET Directorate is the technical and vocational training arm of Tharaka University, registered and licensed by the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority as TVETA/PUBLIC/TVC/0005/2021. It delivers KNEC business and ICT craft and diploma programmes and CDACC competency-based levels 5 and 6 at the university's Marimanti campus in Tharaka Nithi County.
context.description: Tharaka University TVET Directorate is the technical and vocational training arm of Tharaka University, registered and licensed by TVETA under number TVETA/PUBLIC/TVC/0005/2021 on 28 January 2021, licence Running and Validated with an expiry date of 18 June 2031 and twenty-eight accredited award rows. The KNEC craft and diploma programmes in business management, human resource management, ICT, project management, sales and marketing, supply chain management and accountancy run alongside six CDACC Level 5 and nine CDACC Level 6 awards in counselling psychology, credit and credit management, distribution and financial sales, office administration, social work, biotechnology, cooperative management, environmental technology, forex and securities and library and information management. Applying the Schologic level-normalisation convention, KNEC Craft and CDACC Level 5 map to Certificate level, while KNEC Diploma and CDACC Level 6 map to Diploma level, preserving all twenty-eight distinct awards because each carries a unique name, level and exam body. This quality-gate pass re-fetched the university's live contact page, which publishes the directorate's institutional contact details: email info@tharaka.ac.ke and phone +254745838353 (Tel: +254745838353), plus the postal address P.O. Box 193-60215 Marimanti. The live page also confirms the three campuses (Main/Marimanti, Mukothima and Great Tana) and the university's online self-service and student portal infrastructure at students.tharaka.ac.ke.

context.description: The TVET Authority register lists the institution as THE BUNGOMA NATIONAL POLYTECHNIC under registration number TVETA/PUBLIC/NP/0003/2024, registered on 18 January 2024 with a licence valid to 17 January 2029 and the status Registered and Licensed, categorised as a public National Polytechnic in Bungoma County. The polytechnic's own website describes a 550-acre campus on the Bungoma–Nambacha–Kakamega road and states that it specialises in agricultural, technical and business courses, organised into departments of agriculture and environmental studies, building and civil engineering, electrical and electronic engineering, mechanical and automotive engineering, computing and informatics, business and entrepreneurship, hospitality and institutional management, fashion design and clothing, applied sciences, and liberal studies, with an additional driving school. The department pages publish the intake pattern and programme structure: artisan-level trades such as masonry, carpentry and joinery and plumbing run for six months at Level 4, technician programmes such as building technician, land survey and water engineering run for one to two years at Levels 5 and 6, and admissions are offered in January, May and September. The polytechnic publishes a student portal at portal.bungomapoly.ac.ke, an e-learning portal link at elearning2.bungomapoly.ac.ke and a staff webmail service, and its homepage carries a welcome message from Dr. Godfrey Murunga, Chief Principal and Council Secretary, but no individual officer email address or direct telephone line is published, so no personal contact record is created.

context.description: The institution appears in the Schologic register as The Kericho National Polytechnic, a public national polytechnic in Kericho County, and its own domain kerichopoly.ac.ke now carries only a notice that the website has moved from www.kerichopoly.ac.ke to www.buretipoly.ac.ke under the name The Bureti National Polytechnic, so both names are recorded here rather than overwriting either. The TVET Authority's TVET register likewise lists the institution under the registered name The Kericho National Polytechnic, registration number TVETA/PUBLIC/NP/0011/2024, registered on 18 January 2024 with the licence expiring on 17 January 2029 and a status of Registered and Licensed. The polytechnic's academic catalogue publishes 65 programmes across eight departments and four qualification levels, with each department headed by a named officer: Agriculture (9 programmes), Building and Civil Engineering (10), Business (12), Electrical and Electronics Engineering (3), Hospitality (7), ICT (10), Mechanical and Automotive Engineering (13) and a driving school (1). It assesses and certifies its own competency-based programmes: the polytechnic states that it is a registered Qualification Awarding Body accredited by the Kenya National Qualifications Authority, providing assessment and certification for TVET programmes from KNQF Level 3 to Level 7, which is why the CBET awards below are recorded as internally examined. The site publishes ISO 21001:2025 certification for educational organisations management, workshop and laboratory facilities including computerised automotive bays, VDI computing laboratories and renewable-energy test benches, and three intakes a year. Contact details printed on the site are P.O. Box 444-20406 Sotik, the lines 0742888444 and 0704 453 337, and the addresses principal@buretipoly.ac.ke and feedback@buretipoly.ac.ke; no enrolment figure and no named officer's individual contact are published, so both are recorded as null or empty.

context.description: The CUK Institute of Technical and Vocational Education and Training is recorded in the TVET Authority register of accredited institutions as a public technical and vocational college in Nairobi County, placing it in the Nairobi region. Its course table carries twenty-five awards: one KNEC diploma in accountancy, four TVET CDACC competency-based courses at Level 5, and twenty TVET CDACC Level 6 courses spanning business management, cooperative management, supply chain, banking, credit, corporate governance, marketing, human resource management, office administration, project management, computer science and programming, cyber security, environmental technology, agripreneurship, catering and accommodation, tourism and social work. The regulator publishes no street address, town website, e-mail address or telephone line for the college, so those fields remain null or unknown rather than guessed.

context.about: The Eldoret National Polytechnic Town Campus is a public TVET campus in Uasin Gishu County, Kenya, registered and licensed by the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority as TVETA/PUBLIC/TVC/0002/2023. It operates as a satellite campus of The Eldoret National Polytechnic and offers competency-based cosmetology training assessed by TVET CDACC.
context.description: The Eldoret National Polytechnic Town Campus is a public satellite campus of The Eldoret National Polytechnic, registered separately by the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority under number TVETA/PUBLIC/TVC/0002/2023 on 26 January 2023. The regulator records its licence as Registered and Licensed with an expiry date of 25 January 2028 and lists five accredited course rows, all in cosmetology at CDACC levels 3 to 6. The Town Campus complements its parent polytechnic, which holds its own registration as TVETA/PUBLIC/NP/0005/2016, and the parent institution publishes its web presence at tenp.ac.ke, which was fetched live and confirmed to be The Eldoret National Polytechnic. Applying the Schologic level-normalisation convention, CDACC Level 3 and Level 4 awards map to Artisan, Level 5 to Certificate and Level 6 to Diploma; because Level 3 and Level 4 cosmetology collapse to the same name, level and exam body, they are de-duplicated into one Artisan entry, yielding three distinct awards. No campus-specific e-mail address, telephone line or street address is published on the regulator's record, so those fields remain null rather than guessed.

context.description: The Jeremiah Nyagah National Polytechnic is a public national polytechnic under the Ministry of Education, State Department for Vocational and Technical Training, established in 1984 and previously known as Rwika Technical Institute. Its campus is adjacent to Rwika market in Mbeere South, Embu County, approximately 12.5 km from Embu town along the Embu-Kiritiri road at Gachoka, with its postal address P.O. Box 1264-60100 Embu. The institution is accredited and licensed by TVETA to offer quality training programmes in compliance with section 17 of the TVET Act, 2013. Its website lists eight academic departments covering mechanical and automotive engineering, business and entrepreneurship, electrical and electronics engineering, building and civil engineering, applied sciences and mathematics, agriculture and environmental studies, hospitality and institutional management, fashion design and cosmetology, and computing and informatics. It offers over 50 artisan, craft/certificate, diploma and higher diploma courses examined by KNEC, KASNEB, NITA and TVET CDACC, including competency-based education and training (CBET) programmes at Levels 3 to 6. Students can apply online through its jiunge application portal, and trainees receive guidance on applying for government scholarships and Higher Education Loans Board (HELB) funding.

Its published contacts are kaiboi@kaiboitech.ac.ke, +254 727 937 937 and +254 734 937 937 and P.O. Box 937-30100, Eldoret, with the campus at Kaiboi in Nandi County. The website carries an E-Recourses section at https://kaiboitech.ac.ke/e-learning/ and directs students to a separate application and records portal at https://www.kaiboitechportal.ac.ke/, but no public learning-management-system portal is published or reachable, so e-learning provision is recorded as implied rather than verified. KASNEB professional accountancy qualifications also appear on the register but have no matching schema level, so they are noted in the accreditations rather than fabricated into a level.

context.description: The Kipsoen National Polytechnic is recorded by the TVET Authority as TVETA/PUBLIC/NP/0009/2025, a public national polytechnic in Elgeyo Marakwet County registered on 10 July 2025 with a licence valid to 9 July 2030 and the status Registered and Licensed. The institution is established by Legal Notice 117 of 2025, the Kipsoen National Polytechnic Order, which commenced on 10 July 2025 and constitutes the polytechnic as a body corporate with a Council. This record was imported under the earlier working name Kipsoen Technical and Vocational College with category TVC; both the regulator, which now lists the institution in the NP category, and the institution's own website, which brands itself The Kipsoen National Polytechnic, support the current name and category. The polytechnic publishes its own address as P.O. Box 344-30700, Iten, situated along the Eldoret-Iten Road in Iten, Elgeyo Marakwet County, with the email address info@kipsoenpoly.ac.ke and telephone +254 797 868786. The regulator's accredited course table for this licence runs to 51 entries, of which the first nine are represented here: artisan programmes in building technology, electrical installation, fashion design and garment making, general agriculture and plumbing, plus craft-level secretarial studies, accountancy, building technology and electrical and electronics technology (power), all examined by KNEC. The polytechnic states that it trains through departments of mechanical and automotive engineering, electrical and electronic engineering, building and civil engineering, agriculture and environmental management, hospitality and tourism, and computing and informatics. No student population figure is published.

description: The Kipsoen National Polytechnic is recorded by the TVET Authority as TVETA/PUBLIC/NP/0009/2025, a public national polytechnic in Elgeyo Marakwet County registered on 10 July 2025 with a licence valid to 9 July 2030 and the status Registered and Licensed. The regulator's accredited course table for this licence runs to 51 entries, of which the first nine are represented here: artisan programmes in building technology, electrical installation, fashion design and garment making, general agriculture and plumbing, plus craft-level secretarial studies, accountancy, building technology and electrical and electronics technology (power), all examined by KNEC. The polytechnic states that it trains through departments of mechanical and automotive engineering, electrical and electronic engineering, building and civil engineering, agriculture and environmental management, hospitality and tourism, and computing and informatics. context.description: The TVET Authority register records The Kisumu National Polytechnic as a public National Polytechnic registered on 28 January 2016 with a licence valid to 30 October 2027 and a status of Registered and Licensed. The institution traces its foundational roots to 1967 and states on its homepage and Principal's Message page that it operates under ISO 9001:2015 Quality Management Systems to provide affordable, accessible and high-quality technical training. Its accredited programme table runs to 100 rows which, after de-duplication by course, level and examining body, amount to 81 distinct awards spanning artisan, craft and diploma qualifications examined by KNEC and KASNEB, NVCET vocational certificates examined by KNEC, aquaculture and fisheries qualifications at Levels 3 to 5 awarded by the polytechnic itself, and TVET CDACC competency-based programmes up to higher diploma level. Training is organised across academic schools including Agriculture; Applied Science and Environmental Studies; Building and Civil Engineering; Business and Entrepreneurship Studies; Computing and Informatics; Electrical and Electronics Engineering; Fashion Design and Cosmetology; Health Sciences; Hospitality and Tourism; Liberal Studies; and Mechanical and Automotive Engineering. The Chief Principal's message states that the polytechnic is expanding Open, Distance and e-Learning (ODEL) platforms and deploys the Jitume digital programme, alongside non-academic units such as a driving school, Recognition of Prior Learning and an Income Generation Unit.

context.description: The Mawego National Polytechnic is a public national polytechnic at Oyugis in Homa Bay County, Nyanza, recorded by KUCCPS as a public college under the Ministry of Education and publishing its own postal address as P.O. Box 289-40222, Oyugis. Its published 2026 fee structure shows a total annual charge of KSh 67,189 for tuition and statutory items, states that the institution is ISO 9001:2015 certified, and prints the contact lines 0725-050-033 and 0734-156-640 with the address info@mawegopoly.ac.ke, all of which are repeated on its contact page. Academic delivery is organised into ten departments - agriculture and environmental studies, applied science, building and civil engineering, business and entrepreneurship, computing and informatics, electrical and electronic engineering, health sciences, hospitality and institutional management, liberal studies, and mechanical and automotive - each of which publishes its own course table naming the programme, KNQF level, duration and examination body. Those tables show a competency-based ladder running from artisan and Level 3 trades examined by KNEC and NITA through Level 4 certificates, Level 5 diplomas, Level 6 higher diplomas and parallel KNEC craft and diploma awards, examined by KNEC or assessed by TVET CDACC; the courses below reproduce the departmental tables with short courses omitted because the Schologic level list has no short-course category. The departments also run NITA trade-test short courses, a driving school and a student application portal at portal.mawegopoly.ac.ke, but no LMS or VLE platform and no open or distance-learning programme is published, so both learning-mode flags are recorded as none. The TVET Authority's TVET register lists the polytechnic under registration number TVETA/PUBLIC/NP/0008/2024, registered on 18 January 2024 with the licence expiring on 17 January 2029 and a status of Registered and Licensed. No enrolment figure and no named officer's individual email or telephone is published, so the student count is null and the personal-contact list is empty.

Its accredited programme table is one of the largest in the register: ninety rows which deduplicate to eighty-two distinct qualifications, comprising five KNEC artisan awards, twenty-three KNEC craft certificates, thirty KNEC diplomas, one NITA masonry trade test, and TVET CDACC competency-based awards at Level 3, Level 4, Level 5 and Level 6. Craft awards are mapped to the schema's Certificate level, diplomas to Diploma, and both KNEC artisan awards, the NITA trade test and CDACC Levels 3 and 4 to Artisan, while CDACC Level 5 is mapped to Certificate and Level 6 to Diploma. Discipline coverage spans civil, mechanical, electrical, automotive, building and construction plant engineering, land surveying, quantity surveying, architecture, applied sciences, agriculture and horticulture, business and management, accountancy, secretarial studies, hospitality and tourism, food processing, fashion and clothing, library and information management, community health, health records, cyber security, animation and digital media. context.description: The Morendat Institute of Oil and Gas National Polytechnic is a public institution owned by the Kenya Pipeline Company and registered by the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority under TVETA/PUBLIC/TVC/0036/2016, with a licence valid to 14 March 2030; the registry entry is captioned 'THE MORENDAT INSTITUTE OF OIL AND GAS NATIONAL POLYTECHNIC - NAIVASHA' while the institution brands itself 'Morendat Institute of Oil & Gas National Polytechnic'. According to its own account, the institute was established in 2014 as a regional centre of excellence under the Northern Corridor Integration Projects and was gazetted as a National Polytechnic by Legal Notice No. 50 of 30 September 2024 under the TVET Act (Cap. 210A). It operates three campuses: the Naivasha training and conferencing centre with 51-bed accommodation on the Naivasha-Nakuru highway, a Nairobi technical training hub with welding, mechanical, pipeline and instrumentation workshops and a training and testing laboratory, and an Eldoret fire and safety training centre; the Naivasha campus is the one covered by this Nakuru County record. The institute states that it is the only NEBOSH-approved training and assessment centre in Kenya and reports partnerships with the South African Institute of Welding, the American Welding Society and the International Institute of Welding, plus accreditation as a Recognition of Prior Learning assessment centre. The TVETA register lists fifteen accredited qualifications, comprising KNEC artisan, craft and diploma programmes in welding and fabrication, electrical and electronics technology, petroleum geosciences, science laboratory technology, analytical chemistry, chemical and process engineering and mechanical engineering, and five CDACC Level 5 oil pipeline programmes in fire fighting, instrumentation and control, laboratory technology, mechanical maintenance and operations. The imported database record carried the town value 'MVVC+HWH, Nanyuki Rd, Nairobi', which is a Nairobi campus geocode rather than the Naivasha site; the address published on the institute's contact page has been used instead.

context.about: The Nairobi West Hospital College of Health Sciences is the health-sciences training college of The Nairobi West Hospital in Nairobi, Kenya. It delivers hospital-based clinical training programmes in perioperative theatre technology, critical care nursing, community health assistance, counselling psychology and short professional courses, examined internally by the college.
context.description: The Nairobi West Hospital College of Health Sciences (TNWHCHS) is the health-sciences training college attached to The Nairobi West Hospital, operating its own website at tnwhchs.com. The principal's message on that site, signed by Mrs. Serah Kamamo, states that the college offers 'a variety of short courses, perioperative theatre technology, and higher diploma in critical care Nursing'. The college's programme catalogue publishes eleven awards: diploma and certificate counselling psychology, certificate in community health assistant at Level 5 and diploma at Level 6, certificate in perioperative theatre technology at TVET Level 5 and diploma at TVET Level 6, higher diploma in critical care nursing, certificate in echocardiography and electrocardiography, certified nurse assistant, and short courses in emotional intelligence for healthcare professionals and basic counselling skills. The college states that it collaborates with accredited hospitals, medical regulatory bodies and healthcare institutions in Kenya, and names The Nairobi West Hospital among its clinical partners; it also runs a student portal at portal.tnwhchs.com and an online application at tnwhchs.com/application. The college does not appear in the TVET Authority register of accredited institutions under this name on the 25 October 2026 snapshot, and its category is recorded as TVC on the strength of its college-level diploma provision because the register carries no entry to copy. No street address, student population or e-learning provision was confirmed from a fetched source.

context.about: The New Dimension College is a private Technical and Vocational College registered by TVETA in Nairobi, Kenya, with its main campus on Moi Avenue and sister campuses in Mombasa and Lamu, offering business, secretarial and supply chain programmes.

It describes itself as situated in Nairobi with sister campuses in Mombasa and Lamu, and says it has offered training since 2010 in schools covering ICT, accounting, human resource management, front office operations and tourism management. Its contact page lists Mageso Chambers on Moi Avenue, opposite Nairobi Sports House and next to Family Bank, with three telephone lines and the address info@thenewdimensioncollege.co.ke. TVETA registers the Moi Avenue branch as a private Technical and Vocational College under registration number TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0243/2016, registered on 2016-07-14 with licence expiry 2028-01-26, offering craft and diploma programmes in human resource management, secretarial studies and supply chain management examined by KNEC. Human resource management and supply chain management are each accredited at both craft (certificate) and diploma level, so each level is recorded as its own row with the level in the label.

context.about: The Nyamira National Polytechnic is a public national polytechnic at Nyamira in Nyamira County, Nyanza region, created by the Technical and Vocational Training (Nyamira National Polytechnic) Order of 2024 as the successor to Ekerubo Gietai Technical Training Institute; it is TVET Authority licensed up to higher diploma level, is a registered Qualification Awarding Institution, and trains in modularised competency-based programmes across engineering, computing, business, hospitality and liberal studies.

context.description: The Nyamira National Polytechnic was established through the Technical and Vocational Training (Nyamira National Polytechnic) Order of 2024 as the immediate successor of Ekerubo Gietai Technical Training Institute, whose initial buildings were funded by the Government of Kenya between 2009 and 2014; the pioneer principal was posted in January 2015, the first trainees reported in February 2015 and the first Board of Governors was inaugurated in April 2015. Its own About Us page states that it is registered and licensed by the TVET Authority to offer training up to higher diploma level, that it is a registered Qualification Awarding Institution mandated to collaborate with recognised universities for technology degrees, and that it intends to offer Recognition of Prior Learning; the TVET Authority's register records the licence as registration number TVETA/PUBLIC/NP/0006/2024, registered on 18 January 2024 with the licence expiring on 17 January 2029 and a status of Registered and Licensed. The campus occupies 32 acres with a further 27 acres of government land reserved for expansion. Delivery is modularised and competency-based: the Computing and Informatics department explains that each programme is broken into separately assessed modules so trainees can train part-time while working, pause and resume, and gain employable skills before returning to upgrade, and the polytechnic admits three times a year in January, May and September. The published course brochure lists NITA trade-test awards in storekeeping, cake making and pastry, arc welding and records keeping alongside KASNEB accounting awards, while the departmental pages describe modularised information technology, information science and social work and community development programmes without naming their award levels, so only the awards with a stated examination body and grade are recorded below. Contact details are P.O. Box 382-40500 Nyamira, telephone 0794 519 220 (also 0707 043 673), the registrar's address registrar@nyamirapoly.ac.ke and the general address info@nyamirapoly.ac.ke; no enrolment figure is published, so the student count is null.

context.about: The Nyeri National Polytechnic (NNP) is a public national polytechnic in Nyeri County, Central region, offering modularised competency-based training from artisan and certificate level through diploma and higher diploma in applied sciences, health sciences, engineering, ICT, business, hospitality and liberal studies, and assessing and certifying its own programmes under the national qualifications framework.
facilities: Applied sciences and health sciences laboratories
Student and staff self-service portal and examinations portal
context.description: The Nyeri National Polytechnic is a public national polytechnic in Nyeri County, Central region, recorded by KUCCPS as a public college under the Ministry of Education and describing itself on its website as 'a national polytechnic of excellence' delivering quality training, skills development and applied research. Its published programme catalogue is organised by department - applied sciences, health sciences, engineering, ICT, business, hospitality and liberal studies - and lists each award with its national qualification level, duration and examining body, with NNP itself recorded as the examining body for every programme, which is why the courses below carry the exam body 'internal' rather than a national board. The catalogue shows a competency-based ladder from Level 3 artisan awards such as makeup artistry and Level 4 certificate awards such as dairy processing, through Level 5 diplomas and Level 6 higher diplomas in applied biology, applied statistics, analytical chemistry, food technology, dairy technology, community health and science laboratory technology, alongside fire rescue and pharmaceutical technology qualifications; the recorded course list reproduces the awards visible in the catalogue and omits short, non-levelled courses such as a two-week food safety course. The polytechnic runs a set of dedicated portals - an e-learning platform, a staff and student portal, an examinations portal, an e-library, an online application portal, an industrial placement portal and a graduation portal - and advertises a partnership network including the Northern Rangelands Trust recognition-of-prior-learning assessment visits. Its published contact points are info@thenyeripoly.ac.ke and 0724 477 942; no street address is printed on the pages checked, so the location is recorded only to town and county level, the enrolment figure is null because none is published, and the personal-contact list is empty because no named officer's individual contact appears.

Its published programme catalogue is organised by department - applied sciences, health sciences, engineering, ICT, business, hospitality and liberal studies - and lists each award with its national qualification level, duration and examining body, with NNP itself recorded as the examining body for every programme, which is why the courses below carry the exam body 'internal' rather than a national board. The catalogue shows a competency-based ladder from Level 3 artisan awards such as makeup artistry and Level 4 certificate awards such as dairy processing, through Level 5 diplomas and Level 6 higher diplomas in applied biology, applied statistics, analytical chemistry, food technology, dairy technology, community health and science laboratory technology, alongside fire rescue and pharmaceutical technology qualifications; the recorded course list reproduces the awards visible in the catalogue and omits short, non-levelled courses such as a two-week food safety course. The polytechnic runs a set of dedicated portals - an e-learning platform, a staff and student portal, an examinations portal, an e-library, an online application portal, an industrial placement portal and a graduation portal - and advertises a partnership network including the Northern Rangelands Trust recognition-of-prior-learning assessment visits. Its published contact points are info@thenyeripoly.ac.ke and 0724 477 942; no street address is printed on the pages checked, so the location is recorded only to town and county level, the enrolment figure is null because none is published, and the personal-contact list is empty because no named officer's individual contact appears.

context.description: The Rift Valley National Polytechnic (RVNP) is a public national polytechnic established in 1979 in Nakuru County, then in Rift Valley Province, and is located ten kilometres west of Nakuru town along the Nakuru-Njoro Road. Its programme portfolio on the TVETA register spans 139 distinct qualifications from artisan to Higher National Diploma level, examined by KNEC, KASNEB, City and Guilds, DIT and CDACC, delivered across nine departments including engineering, ICT, hospitality, health and applied sciences, and business studies. The institution holds an ISO 9001:2008 QMS certification from KEBS and maintains a 25-year collaboration with Delta College, Michigan, USA. Beyond its main campus it runs two town campuses in Nakuru city (Ndimu House and Prestige Mall along the Nairobi-Nakuru Highway) and one in Kericho at the Ndege Chai Building. Per its own website the polytechnic serves a student population of over 5000 with 203 academic and 148 non-teaching staff.

context.description: The Shamberere National Polytechnic is a public National Polytechnic at Kambi ya Mwanza, roughly one kilometre off the Kakamega-Malava-Webuye Road in Kakamega County, Western Kenya, and is also referred to by its registered trading abbreviation TSNP. The institution was upgraded from Shamberere Technical Training Institute to National Polytechnic status, with the TVETA register recording it as TVETA/PUBLIC/NP/0010/2024, registered on 18 January 2024 and licensed to 17 January 2029 under a status of Registered and Licensed, and it celebrated its first graduation as a polytechnic on 8 August 2025. That register record and the regulator's programme table were taken from the archived capture of the TVETA institution-details page dated 11 May 2026, because the live tveta.go.ke domain is currently serving substituted third-party content. Its academic organisation covers departments of building and civil engineering, electrical and electronics engineering, mechanical and automotive engineering, computing and informatics, applied sciences, hospitality and institutional management, business and entrepreneurship studies, agriculture and environmental studies, and liberal studies, and the regulator's register of accredited programmes lists artisan, craft, diploma and higher diploma qualifications examined by KNEC, KASNEB and TVET CDACC; the register table publishes duplicate rows for titles offered more than once, so the rows here are de-duplicated by title and level and the award level is carried in each label where a title recurs. The polytechnic's own catalogue lists its competency-based programmes from Level 3 to Level 6 with the examination line 'Exam: TVET CDACC / T.S.N.P', which is consistent with CDACC assessment delivered at the polytechnic as assessment centre rather than a competing claim to the KNEC and KASNEB awards on the regulator's table. The polytechnic publishes income-generating activities including a guest house and conference service, catering services, a mechanical workshop producing metal products, a farm enterprise, an ICT production unit and a day care centre, and it provides student accommodation on a first-come, first-served basis. The institution publishes the telephone line +254 739 922 223 and the email info@shambererenationalpoly.ac.ke, and it operates a staff portal, a student self-service portal and institutional webmail alongside its public website.

changelog_jsonb.rationale: The stored 'none' tuple is a stale negative that the live portal disproves. I fetched https://tsnpcomputingandinformatics.gnomio.com/ myself in this run: HTTP 200, title 'Home | eLearning', headed 'COMPUTING & INFORMATICS E-LEARNING PORTAL / TSNP SCHOOL OF COMPUTING & INFORMATICS / Welcome to The Shamberere National Polytechnic School of Computing & Informatics', with enrolled course units (Computer Essentials, Computer Programming Principles, Perform Graphics Design, Diploma in Computerized Secretarial Studies III), teacher allocations, assignment deadlines and a 'Powered by Moodle' footer. That satisfies the schema requirement that a 'verified' learning mode carry a live portal URL, and it is a first-hand operator source plus the institution's own site linking it as 'Online Learning'. The replacement is an upgrade on evidence, not a clearance on absence: no sourced fact is destroyed other than the superseded 'no LMS' assertion, which the live fetch contradicts. has_distance_learning is left at 'none' and untouched (no ODeL programme is published); nothing else on the record is changed.

It actively collaborates with government agencies, industry partners, and community stakeholders to promote practical skills training, entrepreneurship, and green technology.

context.description: The Sigalagala National Polytechnic is a publicly managed National Polytechnic in Ikolomani Constituency, Kakamega County, established in 1950 as the Nyanza Technical and Trade School on land and buildings inherited from British gold miners, converted into a Technical Training Institute in the late 1980s and elevated to National Polytechnic status by Legal Notice No. 90, The Sigalagala National Polytechnic Order, 2016. It operates three campuses - the Main Campus at Sigalagala, a Kakamega Town Campus and a Maturu Campus - and is mandated to offer programmes at artisan, craft, diploma and higher diploma levels across ten academic departments spanning building and civil engineering, electrical and electronics, mechanical and automotive engineering, computing and informatics, applied sciences, health sciences, hospitality and fashion, business and entrepreneurship, agriculture and environmental studies, and liberal studies. The TVETA register of accredited programmes records over sixty distinct qualifications for the polytechnic, including KNEC artisan, craft and diploma programmes and TVET CDACC competency-based levels 4 to 6, with the polytechnic's own website also advertising higher diploma progression in several engineering and applied science fields. The institution runs an online learning platform at elearning.sigalagalapoly.ac.ke alongside a staff and student self-service portal, and publishes its contact line +254 725 66 33 22 and email info@sigalagalapoly.ac.ke. TVETA records its registration as TVETA/PUBLIC/NP/0002/2017, first registered on 12 October 2017 and licensed to 25 January 2028, with a current status of Registered and Licensed.

context.description: The Tseikuru National Polytechnic is a public national polytechnic located in Tseikuru Town, Mwingi North Constituency, Kitui County. It was established as a TVET institution in 2016 with the aim of offering technical and business courses to Form Four leavers, and it now operates as a national polytechnic. Its training is organised under academic departments including Computing and Informatics, Electrical and Electronics Engineering, Mechanical and Automotive Engineering, Building and Civil Engineering, Business Studies and Entrepreneurship, Hospitality and Institutional Management, Fashion Design and Cosmetology, and Liberal Studies. Courses run at artisan, certificate and diploma levels and are accredited by TVETA, with KNEC and TVET CDACC as awarding bodies. The institution runs a Higher Education Financing desk that liaises with KUCCPS on placements and helps trainees apply for HELB loans, scholarships and bursaries, and it hosts ICT Authority Virtual Desktop Infrastructure (Jitume) training alongside an ongoing driving school.

context.description: Thika Institute of Business Studies, which trades as TIBS College, is a private technical and vocational college on the Thika Super Highway in Kiambu County, registered by the TVET Authority as TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0244/2016 on 14 July 2016 with a licence valid to 3 November 2026 and the status Registered and Licensed. The college was founded in October 2003 and its own homepage now reports 3,500 registered students, 93 staff members, 90 courses on offer and 11 examination bodies. It publishes its address as P.O. Box 321-01000 Thika, between Thika Town and the Witeithe section of the Thika Super Highway opposite the JOMOKO matatu stage, and lists the telephone lines 067 223 1160, 067 222 1786, 0715 067 272 and 0793 684 897 with the inbox info@tibs.ac.ke. Provision is organised into eleven faculties spanning accountancy, business, computer studies and IT, engineering, health and social sciences, hospitality, journalism, mass communication and languages, tourism, fashion and interior design, and cosmetology, plus a college driving school. The course table retains the 56 programme entries carried by this record's earlier import and its levels are recorded in canonical form: Advanced Diploma awards are recorded as Higher Diploma, and the KASNEB Certified Public Accountant qualification, a professional award with no dedicated schema level, is recorded at Diploma level in line with the convention used elsewhere in this database and is flagged here as a professional qualification. Teaching is supported by a live Moodle e-learning portal at learning.tibs.ac.ke organised by faculty, while the site publishes no distance-learning or ODeL programme. The published facilities are accommodation, a college library and e-library, a candy shop with agent banking, lecture halls, a mass communication studio, engineering workshops, computer laboratories, a salon and a training restaurant, with buses and vans for student transport.

context.description: Thika School of Medical and Health Sciences is a private health training college founded in 2007 and headquartered at Thika Makongeni, along the Thika-Garissa Highway about 800 metres from Ananas Mall in Kiambu County. The college reports 28-plus accredited programmes, four campuses, more than 12,000 alumni and 18 years of operation, and it publishes campuses in Thika, Kisumu, Mombasa and Kitui. Its programmes blend academic training with hands-on clinical practice at partner hospitals, and the college states that its qualifications are recognised by KNEC, the Kenya Medical Practitioners and Dentists Board, the Pharmacy and Poisons Board, the Kenya Nursing Board and the Kenya Medical Laboratory Technicians and Technologists Board. TVETA registers the college under number TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0072/2016, registered and licensed with a licence expiry of 24 October 2027, and the accredited programme list covers KNEC craft and diploma courses in medical laboratory technology, nutrition and dietetics, applied biology, social work and human resource management, plus TVET CDACC programmes in community health, counselling, health records, perioperative theatre technology, caregiving, environmental and science laboratory technology.

Thika Technical Training Institute appears in the TVET Authority register of accredited institutions as a public TVC in Kiambu County, under registration number TVETA/PUBLIC/TVC/0008/2017, registered on 2017-06-19 with licence expiry 2027-10-24 and status Registered and Licensed. Its own site describes it as a government TVET institution under the Ministry of Education, State Department for Technical, Vocational Education and Training, with a mandate to provide quality technical, industrial, vocational and entrepreneurship training. The register course table resolves after de-duplication to 144 distinct awards spanning KNEC artisan, craft and diploma programmes together with TVET CDACC competency-based qualifications at levels 3 to 6, across electrical and mechanical engineering, building and civil works, agriculture, business, ICT, hospitality and applied sciences. The institute's January 2027 intake banner invites applications for Level 4, Level 5 and Level 6 Engineering, Business and ICT programmes, states that CDACC courses and slots are available, and advertises virtual classes through its Open Distance and Flexible Learning (ODFL) mode. Applications are taken online through the institute's student portal at thikattiportal.ac.ke, and the site's FAQ records minimum entry requirements of KCSE C- and above for Level 6, D+ and above for Level 5 and D plain and above for Level 4.

Level normalisation follows the pipeline convention, recording CBET Level 3-4 rows as Artisan, CBET Level 5 as Certificate and CBET Level 6 as Diploma. Topmax Training College is a private middle-level college registered by the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority under TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0034/2021, with registration dated 26 April 2021 and a licence valid to 30 April 2031. The college describes itself as training artisans and offering certificate, diploma and advanced diploma programmes across schools of business and economics, ICT and engineering, hospitality and languages, beauty and fashion design, media studies, social sciences, health sciences and driving, plus ICT short courses. Its published catalogue includes business management, accounting and finance, ICT, hospitality management, beauty therapy, fashion design, journalism and media studies, social work and community development, and health-science programmes such as community health, peri-operative theatre technology and orthopaedic trauma. The main campus is located at Pipeline, Embakasi, Nairobi, off Outer Ring Road, and a second unit, Topmax Training College Bee Centre, holds separate TVETA registration TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0135/2024. Admissions are handled online through the college website, which also advertises a student portal and ongoing intakes.

context.about: Total Technical and Vocational College is a public Technical and Vocational College in Nakuru County, Kenya, registered by the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority as TVETA/PUBLIC/TVC/0015/2019 with a licence running to 27 May 2030. Its accredited table is one of the broader ones, covering KNEC artisan, craft and diploma awards together with TVET CDACC competency-based programmes from level 3 to level 6 in building, civil, electrical, water, surveying, ICT, business, social-work and cosmetology disciplines.
context.description: Total Technical and Vocational College is a public TVET institution recorded in the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority register of accredited institutions as TVETA/PUBLIC/TVC/0015/2019, registered on 22 October 2019 with a licence valid to 27 May 2030 and a status of Registered and Licensed, in Nakuru County. The register lists KNEC artisan awards in building technology, electrical installation, plumbing and storekeeping, KNEC craft awards in business management, general agriculture and information communication technology, and KNEC diploma awards in building technology and supply chain management. Competency-based training is delivered under the TVET Curriculum Development, Assessment and Certification Council across four levels, with a level 3 plumbing award, level 4 awards in office assistance, social work, electrical installation, plumbing and information communication technology, eight level 5 awards covering office administration, electrical engineering, business management, architectural draftsmanship, ICT, social work, plumbing and land surveying, and nine level 6 awards spanning social work, civil engineering, cosmetology, building technology, computer science, land survey, accountancy, electrical engineering and water engineering technology. Register levels were normalised to the schema vocabulary, with Craft and CDACC level 3 to level 5 rendered as Certificate and CDACC level 6 as Diploma, and the same subject appears at several levels where the register lists it separately rather than being collapsed. The register publishes no street address, telephone line or institutional email for the college, and no institution-owned website was confirmed in this pass, so those fields are recorded as absent rather than estimated.

context.description: Trans Eastern Airlines Aviation College (TEAAC) is a private aviation training college in Nairobi, Kenya, founded in 1990 by a group of airline experts and operating since 1993. The college describes itself as a pioneer of aviation training in East Africa and states that it is fully registered by the relevant government ministries, subscribing to IATA, KATA, ICAO and KNEC, with its Aeronautical Diploma courses validated by the Commission for Higher Education (CHE). The TVET Authority register records TRANS EASTERN AIRLINES AVIATION COLLEGE as a private TVC, registration number TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0078/2022, registered 2022-04-20 with licence valid to 2027-04-19, status Registered and Licensed. It operates from two Nairobi sites: the Jomo Kenyatta International Airport (Freight Terminal) and Information House, 5th floor, in the CBD. Its current catalogue spans diploma courses in Aeronautical Engineering (Mechanical and Avionics options), Telecommunication Engineering, Flight Operations/Dispatch, Aircraft Maintenance, IATA diplomas in Cargo Services Operations, Clearing Forwarding & Shipping Management, Passenger and Aircraft Handling, Airline Cabin Crew Training, Travel & Tourism (Management) and Airport Operations, plus certificate courses such as Weight & Balance, diploma-level business courses (Entrepreneurship, Business Management, Sales and Marketing, Procurement and Supply Chain, Ground Operations Management) and language diplomas in German, French, Chinese, Italian, Spanish and Arabic. The college homepage reports 24 diploma courses, 44 certificate courses, 45 qualified lecturers and over 24,000 graduates.

Tricent School of Medical Health Sciences and Technology is a private Technical and Vocational College registered by the Technical and Vocational Education and Training Authority as TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0245/2016, with a licence running to 26 January 2028 and status Registered and Licensed. Its stated mission is to provide humane and integral health sciences, business and technology education with emphasis on primary health care in underserved communities, especially rural areas. Teaching combines theory, practical sessions, laboratory work, clinical attachments and mentorship, and the college advertises certificate and diploma programmes for the healthcare, business, technology and community-development sectors. Featured programmes on its website include Perioperative Theatre Technology, Community Development and Social Work, and Nutrition and Dietetics, while the TVETA register lists KNEC-examined craft and diploma awards and CDACC-examined optical technology and orthopaedic and trauma medicine awards at Levels 5 and 6. The college operates multiple campuses, with the Nairobi campus at Eastend Plaza, Bukani Road in Nairobi West, and further campuses in Juja town opposite JKUAT, Kisumu opposite Swan Center, and Homa Bay opposite Makongeni Petrol Station.

context.description: Tropical Institute of Community Health and Development (TICH) in Africa is a private TVC on the TVET Authority register in Kisumu County, registered on 23 January 2020 as TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0018/2020 and licensed through 28 July 2030. Its accredited portfolio covers twenty-two distinct awards once the register's duplicate rows are collapsed: twenty KNEC craft certificate and diploma programmes across accountancy, banking and finance, business management, catering and accommodation, food and beverage, human resource management, ICT, project management, sales and marketing, social work and supply chain management, plus two TVET CDACC community health programmes at Levels 5 and 6. LOCATION/CONTACT NOTE (updated 2026-11-17): the institute's own website https://www.tichinafrica.org/ is live and publishes the address 'Tom Mboya Street, Milimani, Kisumu', email info@tichinafrica.org and phone +254 743 964 736 — an additional D2 contact line, with the stored primary line 0703 244335 retained. The town column still carries the imported plus-code token 'WQRQ+F7F, Wathorego'; whether Wathorego is a real locality near Milimani and what the canonical town should be could not be established with two independent operators this pass, so both value sets are preserved — the plus-code stays in the town column and the published Kisumu address stands in the location field. The community health provision aligns with the institute's stated focus on health and development training.

context.description: Ujuzi Fursa Africa Training Institute - Mombasa is the Mombasa branch of a privately owned caregiver and healthcare-support training provider registered by TVETA under registration number TVETA/PRIVATE/TVC/0195/2024, registered on 29 October 2024 with a licence valid to 28 October 2029 and a register status of 'Registered and Licensed'. The operator trades as Ujuzi Fursa Africa Training Institutes under the Care360 brand and positions itself as a social impact enterprise advancing decent work and quality education. Training runs through three routes: in-class study over five months, a hybrid route with online theory and in-person practicals one or two days a week, and an online-only caregiving essentials certification completed in three to thirty days. The TVETA register lists Healthcare Support Services at Level 5 and Caregiving at Level 4 examined by TVET CDACC, plus Elder Care and Child Care certificate courses examined by iCare Learning. Practical training includes a hospital-like skills laboratory and internship placements, and the operator reports having trained more than 7,000 caregivers since 2017, nine in ten of them women.
